# 1.0 Rust port: ultracode chunk map

Task #25629. Approved by Josh on 2026-11-05 (ruling 23). Written 2026-11-05 on 0.5.0. Brought up to the cut SHA (0.5.0 at 0256724f1f) and to ruling 24 on 2026-11-12, under task #25933. The machine-readable map is
`1.0-ultracode-chunk-map-2026-11-03.json`, and its supporting files are in `1.0-ultracode-chunk-map-2026-11-03/`.

## Status

Approved. Josh, 2026-11-05: "chunk map is approved, but we can't begin until all worktrees except 0.5.0 and wiki are resolved" and "and the tmux purge is complete." The relay names no row answered differently, so every default below stands (ruling 23). On 2026-11-12 Josh waived the start gate work that was still open and moved the tmux purge into the port as its first chunk (ruling 24). 0.5.0's last push, 0256724f1f, is the cut SHA, and the map was brought up to it that day; the next section lists what changed. No port code has started and 0.9.0 does not exist yet. Since approval the #21542 tree changed in two nodes: #25629 closed and #25935 was added.

- 134 chunks in dependency order on branch 0.9.0, each with a self-contained, decision-complete brief.
- Every one of the 1,094 ledger rows is owned by exactly one chunk, and every Python engine has an owning chunk.
- Every one of the 447 open #21542 nodes has a disposition with evidence (Appendix B).
- Your stops: 11 checkpoint reviews need your go, in a session you open when the dispatcher names it. You also open a session for each of the 15 cutovers; it reaches you for a rollback, a refused promotion, a red CI run past its fix bound or a trigger outside the table you approved. Before CP-NODE-CUT's first tag you merge the tap's pull request (D127), and after each client tag the one its update job opens; at CP-NODE-CUT you push the release tags and lend a Mac with no Python, Rust or Zig; at POST-CLEAN you fast-forward main and push the release tags. You open the security-auditor seat and the port dispatcher once, and you prompt the dispatcher whenever TMUX-PURGE, GEN-ROLLBACK, a review or a cut closes, or a no-go files fixes. You open TMUX-PURGE's session, approve its refreshed plan's expansion and run D31's two restore commands when it closes. The start gate's operator steps on A and P are yours, and A adopts a checkpoint only when you start that adoption.
- Landing freezes: each runs from its cut's step 3 to its close. The observation windows alone are at least 144 hours: 11 of at least 8 hours, 2 of 12 hours, and at least 16 hours each for CP-TEMPLATE-CUT and CP-PREDELETE-CUT. Backup, rehearsal, the CI wait, any fix-forward and, at CP-NODE-CUT and POST-CLEAN, your tag pushes add to each. Other sessions' finished chunks queue during a freeze.
- Reviews: Every fix round was adversarially verified. A lens review read every brief: 81 findings kept and 38 more from its verifiers. A completeness critic then walked the fleet's path from approval to 1.0, swept the code for behavior no chunk owned, and read the merged whole: 44 findings and 24 more from its verifiers, 6 of them blockers. Its one allowed repeat ran on the fixed map: 56 findings kept and 19 more from its verifiers, 4 of them blockers, with no disposition changed. A real spawned session confirmed the sandbox's limits: Workflow, seat spawn, parent messages, crates.io, PyPI and cargo pass; GitHub, gh and Docker fail. It did not try a worktree spawn, land_commit, the isolated harness or a restart, so the first chunks prove those. Every finding is fixed in the map or listed in Appendix A or C, and the last review's stated limits are below.

## Changed on 2026-11-12 (ruling 24)

These changes take effect with your word on ruling 24's change list. Until then each is a default.

- **Machines.** P, the port machine, is this laptop now and your Linux machine later (D128). A is the Game Goblins machine: a copy restored from P's backup, on origin's 0.5.0 at the cut SHA, where nobody edits gobby (A-GG-NOEDITS). No 0.9.0-gg branch is forked, A needs no policy commit, and A gets a gobby fix only by adopting a checkpoint (D40).
- **Start gate.** Items 1 to 3 are waived or superseded. 0.5.0's last push is the cut SHA, so the CI and AGENTS.md commit and the map-approval commit are 0.9.0's first commits, and nothing lands on 0.5.0 again. The backup that seeds A is taken after 0.9.0's push, once the chunk tasks exist, so A's hub holds them too, idle. The numbering offset is not run unless you ask for it. On A, before its first daemon start, you turn off the gobby project's Telegram channel and the cron jobs that launch seats or pipelines in that project (item 17, step 3).
- **TMUX-PURGE** is new and comes first (D129). Its task is the existing epic #25486, it follows its own plan and not the chunk protocol, and GEN-ROLLBACK depends on it. It is an exception to three rules, for this chunk only: its leaves promote outside a cut, its two migrations are destructive and land outside a cut, and its Python edits are live.
- **#25935**, removing /clear handoffs, is port work that no chunk owns until its plan is approved (D130).
- **Brought to the cut.** Every cite moved from 08f709e822 to the cut SHA. Five readers, each followed by a verifier, reread the chunks against what landed on 0.5.0 since approval: 195 text corrections, 162 cite corrections beyond the renumbering, and an owning chunk for 95 of the 96 new modules; the other, a Python reader of a record that Rust already holds, ports nothing. The ledger went from 1,085 rows to 1,094 (11 added, 2 removed). Five rows had no owner and now have one: `gobby build-sweep` (V3), `GET /api/admin/usage/ledger` (OBS), `POST /api/hooks/codex-thread-credential` (HOOK-3), `compose_status_report` (COMMS-2) and `set_status_line` (SES-2).
- **Two facts that changed under the map.** `land_commit` generates version bumps only on a branch named 0.5.0, so on 0.9.0 each commit carries its own bumps, as D39 already says, and 0.9.0's first commit rewords the AGENTS.md paragraph that says otherwise. Since #25900 the default definition waives the security-review gates, so the wait for the security-auditor seat (D115) rests on protocol step 7 and no gate enforces it.
- **Left open.** The reread found 20 gaps that no decision settles. None is decided here; `1.0-ultracode-chunk-map-2026-11-03/gaps-2026-11-12.md` lists them. No brief points at that file yet, and two need your ruling: a spawned seat's signed restart request, which the native restart row would refuse from CP-RUNNER-CUT (gap 1), and the project skill startup sync, which has no native owner (gap 3).

The sections below are the approval request as approved on 2026-11-05, corrected only where ruling 24 or the cut made a line false. Appendices A and C stand as of that date, with cites at 08f709e822.

## Before you approve

- Two chunk sessions run at most until CP-TEMPLATE-CUT closes (D23). You then name the number.
- The port stays on this laptop, which is already set up. The Game Goblins machine's setup is your own work (start gate item 17), and so is the later move to the Linux machine (D128).
- Three steps are undone only by a backup restore, which loses every write made after that backup: CP-WAVE3-CUT's attachment relocation and the drops at CP-FINAL-CUT and POST-CLEAN. Once S3-DELETE lands, no generation from before CP-PREDELETE-CUT can be restored.
- A Homebrew `gobby` cannot run a daemon until your first publication at CP-NODE-CUT (D60), as today.
- Limits the last review stated. `compute_sandbox_paths` against `paths.rs` rests on the corpus, not on a comparison. Other native code that chunks reuse was not compared step by step, so a miss like AG-1's launch path, which lacked four of Python's steps, may repeat; D124 makes each such chunk run that comparison first. fnmatch sites, psutil and docs prose were only sampled. The citation check is range-only, though most citations were reread by hand.

## What one approval does

Approval takes every default in the tables below. Answer any row differently and the other rows stand.

Then, in this order (start gate item 21 has the full order):

1. On P: 0.5.0's last push is the cut SHA, and nothing lands on 0.5.0 after it. 0.9.0 is created at the cut SHA on your word, and P's main checkout moves to it.
2. 0.9.0's first three commits follow, unpushed: the CI and AGENTS.md edits; the map-approval commit carrying `docs/port/` with the cut's ledger; and the policy commit with P's `project_policy` and AGENTS.md rule 15 change, which lands on your word.
3. On P, chunk tasks are created as direct children of #21542, and open nodes close or move under D31, apart from the few it names for later; you restore the plan files those closes archive.
4. 0.9.0 is pushed, and you lock 0.5.0 on GitHub. Then you take the hub backup that seeds A (start gate item 18); its `gobby start` is P's first start on 0.9.0.
5. You open the security-auditor seat (D115), the port dispatcher (D116) and the unspawned session that runs TMUX-PURGE, the first chunk (D129), and after it the one that runs GEN-ROLLBACK. The dispatcher starts the rest once you prompt it after GEN-ROLLBACK closes.
6. On A, which does not gate the port: base install, restore, KEK copy, machine id, the second install run and item 17's step 3, all before its first daemon start, with its main checkout on origin's 0.5.0.

## Your #25341 items

The map's "Josh's #25341 items" section answers each in full.

- **Thin specs:** P0-RECORD commits `docs/port/record.md`, and each untargeted task gets its targets by absorption into a chunk brief.
- **Compare-mode blind spots:** P0-LOWTRAFFIC records voice, comms, install and node install corpora in Phase 0, and GW-2 adds per-tool Compare.
- **Interface churn:** the seam wave and A1 write a checked-in contract, and `gport check-slice` refuses B-slice edits to frozen files without a Found Work reference.
- **Golden fixtures capture current shell-guard bugs:** both remedies. Queued items are fixed before the cut, and the rest become known-bad rows that Rust does not copy.
- **Freeze vs priorities:** nothing freezes beyond ruling 6 and each cutover window's landing freeze. The hub, the node and runbooks v4 keep running.
- **"Push 1,020 commits" is stale:** dropped. The start gate requires 0.5.0 pushed and in sync at the cut.

Your suggested pilot is kept in your order, except that rulings 14 and 16 put the runner and MCP checkpoints ahead of A1 going live: Phase 0, then A1, then B0, through CP-TEMPLATE-REVIEW's partial/stub measurement and CP-TEMPLATE-CUT's live Compare day, before the template fan-out starts.

## How to read the rest

The map follows in this order: start gate and how 0.9.0 is cut; checkpoint and cutover model, with rollback; chunk protocol; the chunks with their edges; decisions; your #25341 items; open problems. Appendix A lists where the map overrides a plan. Appendix B has the disposition of every open #21542 node. Appendix C routes found work.

# The map

This map applies Josh's rulings 1-24. He approved it on 2026-11-05 (ruling 23), and on 2026-11-12 it was brought up to the cut SHA, 0.5.0 at 0256724f1f, and to ruling 24. 134 chunks on 0.9.0, which is the integration branch and the port machine's main checkout (rulings 15, 18 and 24); every one of the 1,094 ledger rows is owned exactly once; every decision has a default or a resolution. TMUX-PURGE comes first (ruling 24, D129): the tmux purge that ruling 8 had on 0.5.0. GEN-ROLLBACK follows (D38): generation-retaining promotion, a window hold, an owner-bound landing freeze and gobby rollback. Phase 0 and the recording wave follow. R0-R6 and SCHEMA-WINDOW land dormant, and CP-RUNNER-REVIEW and CP-RUNNER-CUT switch the daemon to the Rust runner as a one-way switchover (ruling 16); R-RETIRE then removes the Python runner launch path. CP-MCP takes the native gateway live (GW-1, GW-2). CP-TEMPLATE reviews the first route family (A1 and the tasks pilot, with the pilot calibration folded in) and activates it in four cutovers: both families to Compare, then A1 and the tasks reads Native, then the writes, then close and landing. Stage 2 runs in five waves, each closed by a review and a cutover (CP-WAVE3-REVIEW runs the second calibration). Stage 3's verbs, S3-FREEZE and S3-NAME end at CP-PREDELETE, whose cutover makes the live generation Python-free; S3-DELETE follows; CP-FINAL drops the tables that are now dead (ruling 17). Stage 4 lands dormant and goes live at CP-NODE; POST-CLEAN is the last cutover. Every cutover runs nine steps, from its announcement to its rollback recipe. Chunk protocol: gport start (every depends_on task closed as done, and its commit on 0.9.0 except for a review), then claim; merge 0.9.0 into the worktree; one ultracode Workflow; local validation including the dormancy proof; the code-reviewer seat; merge 0.9.0 again; land and push, with no promotion, because only checkpoint cuts promote (D39); close. The port runs on this laptop for now and moves to Josh's Linux machine later (ruling 24, D128). The Game Goblins machine is seeded from this laptop's backup, runs 0.5.0 at the cut and makes no gobby edits; it adopts a checkpoint by its tag when Josh decides (D40).

**Angle.** ORACLE-FIRST, grafted, now with checkpoint cutovers: every chunk's oracle exists or is recorded before its port; every landed commit is dormant through code defaults and promoted only by the next checkpoint cut (D39); each checkpoint is a review pause with Josh followed by a live cutover with a backup, a rehearsed rollback, a bounded window and three outcomes; MCP routes per tool; families are library crates in one gdaemon, rolled back by generation.

## ASSUMPTIONS

- **A1-RULING14.** Checkpoints are review pauses with Josh, each followed by a live cutover of what that stage built, and there is no single end-of-port cutover. The named checkpoints come after the runner, after the MCP proxy and after the first route family, then one per wave. *Basis:* Ruling 14: 'Setting checkpoints during development is probably a good idea, especially after we port the daemon runner, the mcp proxy, and the first family.' Then: 'By checkpoints I mean we pause and check that we're going in the right direction. Once we build one route family that will serve as the template for others, for example.' 'Checkpoints are review pauses, then cutover as you described above.' 'Not a single end-of-port cutover.' *If wrong:* If Josh wants reviews without live cutovers, remove the CP-*-CUT chunks, point each review's dependents at the review, and restore one final cutover after S3-DELETE.
- **A2-RULING16.** The runner switches once, at CP-RUNNER-CUT, with three outcomes; the first or second retires the Python runner for the rest of the build (R-RETIRE), and every checkpoint cutover reuses the same three-outcome window with a pinned pre-cutover generation. *Basis:* Ruling 16: 'I think the runner needs to be a firm switchover. Either it works, it works enough that we can debug it, or we roll back to python and reassess.' Then: 'When we move the runner off python I want to be off the python runner for the remainder of the build.' Josh confirmed the window and pinned generation for every checkpoint cutover (about 19:25 CT). *If wrong:* If Josh wants the Python runner kept as a fallback, drop R-RETIRE, move #25467 back to R6, and let GEN-ROLLBACK keep Python-runner generations restorable.
- **A3-SHAPE.** Each checkpoint is one review chunk (kind checkpoint, category manual, closed only on Josh's go) and one cutover chunk (kind cutover, category code, owning the activation commit). CP-TEMPLATE is one review with four cutovers. A review that regenerates the record or census writes it under ~/.gobby/port/<review chunk id>/, outside the checkout and outside any session scratchpad or /tmp, named in its packet attestation, and its cutover lands it as its first, docs-only commit. Every other chunk task is category code, because create_task requires a category and the coding closure rules select on it (src/gobby/install/shared/workflows/rules/task-closure/coding.yaml:9-13). *Basis:* Ruling 14; the manual review protocol in docs/port/facts-F4.md; item 6's activation order for the tasks pilot (reads, writes, close and landing, each through Compare first). *If wrong:* To give each pilot step its own go, split CP-TEMPLATE-REVIEW into four reviews, one before each CP-TEMPLATE cutover.
- **A4-CPRUNNER.** CP-RUNNER covers R0-R6 and what they need (P0-RECORD, P0-HARNESS, SEAM-FAMILY, GEN-ROLLBACK, SCHEMA-WINDOW). Changed dependencies: R4 drops A1-RUNTIME; A1-RUNTIME gains R4 and registers its own rotate_due job; P0-RECORD and P0-HARNESS gain GEN-ROLLBACK; CP-RUNNER-REVIEW depends on R6, SEAM-FAMILY, P0-HARNESS, GEN-ROLLBACK and SCHEMA-WINDOW. R-RETIRE removes the Python runner launch path after CP-RUNNER-CUT's window. The gateway (PROJ-1, SEAM-CALLERS, SEAM-WS, GW-1, GW-2) and the pilot (A1-RUNTIME to B0-CLOSE) build and land dormant during CP-RUNNER's and CP-MCP's pauses and windows, because the runner is on the critical path and D23 runs the pilot path beside it. On a no-go at CP-RUNNER-REVIEW or CP-MCP-REVIEW, their sessions stop at their next checkpoint and land nothing until the fixes Josh names close. *Basis:* Ruling 16's notes: 'CP-RUNNER must cover the whole runner before CP-MCP and the first family'; 'R4's native rotate_due registration moves into A1-RUNTIME.' *If wrong:* If Josh wants rotate_due in R4, restore R4's A1-RUNTIME edge and move A1-RUNTIME ahead of CP-RUNNER-REVIEW. If that overlap is wrong, add GW-1 on CP-RUNNER-REVIEW and A1-RUNTIME on CP-MCP-REVIEW (longest chain 57).
- **A5-CPMCP.** 'The MCP proxy' means the native gateway built by GW-1 and GW-2 (/mcp, the meta-tools, the REST tool routes, per-tool routing, the Python compatibility backend and the single policy pass), with every tool still on Proxy. The external server pool (MUX-1, MUX-2) and MCP-FLIP go live at CP-WAVE5. CP-MCP-REVIEW depends on GW-2, CP-RUNNER-CUT and R-RETIRE. The gateway and pilot overlap during CP-MCP's pause and window follows A4-CPRUNNER. *Basis:* Ruling 14 names the MCP proxy as the second checkpoint; the pool is single-owner state whose last Python callers port in wave 4, and MCP-FLIP needs every internal server native. *If wrong:* If Josh means the whole MCP surface, move CP-MCP-REVIEW after MCP-FLIP, merge it with CP-WAVE5, and let the pilot's tools stay on Proxy until then. That move reverses the order in rulings 14 and 16 and needs Josh's word.
- **A6-CPTEMPLATE.** The first route family is Josh's pilot (A1 and B0). CP-TEMPLATE-REVIEW runs the pilot calibration (D17's gate, resizing, census) and depends on B0-CLOSE, P0-DECISIONS and CP-MCP-CUT. A1 goes live at CP-TEMPLATE-READS-CUT. The tasks activation order is reads, then writes, then close and landing, each after CP-TEMPLATE-CUT's Compare day. #24474 and #25521 move to the cutovers that activate them. *Basis:* Ruling 14 ('one route family that will serve as the template'); Josh's pilot order (Phase 0, A1, B0, soak); item 6. *If wrong:* If A1 alone is the template, end CP-TEMPLATE after CP-TEMPLATE-READS-CUT and move the writes and close cutovers into CP-WAVE1.
- **A7-WAVES.** One checkpoint per Stage 2 wave. The template fan-out (TERM-1, TPL, SRC, AI-1A, OBS, PROJ-2, AUTH, RULE-1A and HOOK-ENV) depends on CP-TEMPLATE-CUT, so a rollback on the pilot's live Compare day holds it. Each later wave's first chunks depend on the previous wave's review, not its cutover, so building overlaps the previous window: SES-1, ACP-CLIENTS and AG-4 on CP-WAVE1-REVIEW; CIX-1, COMMS-1, CHAT-1, MCP-CRATE and MEM-1 on CP-WAVE2-REVIEW; HOOK-1, PIPE-1 and NODEHUB on CP-WAVE3-REVIEW (which runs the second calibration); TERM-HOST, AG-WAIT, MUX-1 and COMMS-2 on CP-WAVE4-REVIEW; V1A to V5B on CP-WAVE5-REVIEW. The landing freeze holds their landings only while a cutover runs, from its step 3 to its close; it covers neither review pauses nor the gaps between windows. On a cutover's outcome 3, its session sends one project send_message naming the in-flight chunks that depend on its review: they stop at their next checkpoint and land nothing until Josh's reassessment is recorded on that cutover's task. This rule applies from CP-TEMPLATE on; A4-CPRUNNER covers the runner and MCP checkpoints. Waves 2 and 3 stay separate. *Basis:* Ruling 14 ('later ones per wave'); the earlier map's wave groups; the manual review protocol in docs/port/facts-F4.md, whose default is that next-stage chunks depend on the cutover task, with the exception that an individual edge may point at the review task where the live flip is not an input. *If wrong:* To build nothing during a window, point each later wave's edges at the previous wave's cutover instead; to cut one checkpoint, merge CP-WAVE2 into CP-WAVE3.
- **A8-D36.** Families are library crates on gcore inside one gdaemon; a family rolls back by generation, as D36 shows for gtask in each phase. *Basis:* Ruling 14's gtask example ('the previous version as a backup binary'); D36. *If wrong:* If Josh wants per-family processes, add a process-boundary seam chunk after SEAM-FAMILY and a per-family supervisor, and resize every family chunk.
- **A9-D37.** Landed code is dormant through code defaults; only activation commits flip them; rollback restores the pinned generation; no runtime switch is added and front_door.routes is not used live. *Basis:* Josh's confirmation: 'dormancy works through code defaults plus generation rollback, with no runtime switches'; D37's reasons against front_door.routes. *If wrong:* If Josh wants a live switch, use front_door.routes per family in each cutover's activation step instead of a commit, and add a preflight check for its values.
- **A10-D38.** GEN-ROLLBACK is the first 0.9.0 chunk after TMUX-PURGE, in Python, and V1A ports it. *Basis:* Ruling 16 needs a pinned generation; nothing retains one today (bin_set_coherence.py:88-153). *If wrong:* If Josh refuses the Python work (rulings 6 and 10), roll back by rebuilding the pinned commit with gobby cutover --path <worktree at the pinned commit> (same-source re-promotion is permitted) and rely on the landing freeze; a Rust rollback verb in gclient instead still needs Josh's word on its Python call site.
- **A11-VERSION.** Promotion follows D39 as resolved (option B, amended): a landing bumps gdaemon when it changed it and never promotes; gcode, ghook, gmcp, gclient and gterm are bumped only in a cut's shipping commits (its activation commit, each outcome-2 fix commit and its deactivation commit) and in emergency cutover commits, because the gcode and ghook pins are runtime floors; each cut's activation commit bumps every binary whose fingerprint changed since its last bump, and only checkpoint cuts promote. *Basis:* Josh's ruling that binaries are promoted on checkpoints; any session's cutover builds and promotes the whole stamped set from the workspace it is given (src/gobby/cli/cutover.py:46-50, 455-481); the gcode and ghook managed pins are their runtime floors (src/gobby/code_index/gcode_versions.py:5-6; src/gobby/hooks/runtime_compat.py:17, 28); the release guard refuses a changed source without a bump only at promotion (src/gobby/install/bin_release_identity.py:234). *If wrong:* If a landing must go live before its checkpoint, it goes through an emergency cutover on Josh's word, with a cut's nine steps; if the gcode and ghook pins stop being runtime floors, both may bump at landing like gdaemon.
- **A12-SCHEMA.** Migrations are expand-only until CP-FINAL-CUT and land only inside checkpoint cuts, as prepared commits in step 6, after the backup and the rehearsal (D22); from CP-RUNNER-CUT on every retained generation accepts a hub ahead by expand-only receipts (SCHEMA-WINDOW), so a rollback across an expand step is the binary restore plus the deactivation commit; every drop is an irreversible step with its own go, at CP-FINAL-CUT and POST-CLEAN only, where rollback is the backup restore. *Basis:* Josh's rulings of 2026-11-03 and 2026-11-04 on rollback versus migrations and on promotion; ruling 17; hub-backup's restart start-half proof (src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/cli.py:228-235; src/gobby/storage/schema_divergence.py:251-265); the schema checks that SCHEMA-WINDOW relaxes for expand-only receipts (crates/gdaemon/src/main.rs:276-297; crates/gcore/src/schema/runner_plan.rs:153-169) and the destructive directive it pairs with a filename marker (crates/gcore/src/schema/runner_plan.rs:281). *If wrong:* If SCHEMA-WINDOW cannot make a gate accept expand-only receipts, every cut that carries an expand step names its backup restore as an irreversible step with Josh's go, as the drops do, and its rehearsal proves the backup path.
- **A13-STAGE4.** Stage 4 runs after CP-FINAL-CUT, lands dormant on 0.9.0 and goes live at CP-NODE-CUT, a checkpoint this map adds; POST-CLEAN follows it. *Basis:* Decision 26 (Stage 4 after Python retirement); ruling 15 (everything lands on 0.9.0). *If wrong:* If Josh wants node work live sooner, activate each S4 chunk at a checkpoint of its own instead of CP-NODE-CUT (D24's fallback), and point POST-CLEAN at the last of them.
- **A14-DELETION.** Python is deleted in one go at S3-DELETE, after CP-PREDELETE-CUT. *Basis:* Ruling 14: 'Yes, it can be deleted in one go, or we can strangler fig it.' *If wrong:* For a strangler, add a deletion chunk after each wave's cutover window and make GEN-ROLLBACK refuse generations that need the deleted code.
- **A15-COMMS.** Telegram, Slack, Teams, email and SMS ship in 1.0 on one adapter contract, each verified first; Discord ships if its live test-guild test passes; iMessage is after 1.0; gobby_chat is dropped. *Basis:* Ruling 12 ('a unified gobby-comms interface that works with Telegram, Slack, Teams, email, SMS, iMessage, etc.'; gobby_chat 'Might be legacy code'); ruling 13. *If wrong:* If iMessage is in 1.0, add a spec-first iMessage adapter to COMMS-2, ported from its integration's published contract and verified with a live round trip on a test account, as D28 does for failed adapters; if gobby_chat stays, restore it in COMMS-1 and COMMS-2.
- **A16-POSTCLEAN.** POST-CLEAN stays as a full cutover after CP-NODE-CUT for what no earlier cutover could drop, and it reuses CP-NODE-REVIEW's go for its irreversible steps, whose rollback is its own backup restore (D22). *Basis:* Ruling 17 asks for a backup at every cutover; D22 makes every drop an irreversible step with Josh's go, at CP-FINAL-CUT and POST-CLEAN only; CP-NODE-REVIEW's packet names POST-CLEAN's planned drops and carries POST-CLEAN's own cutover plan (its trigger table, fix-forward bound, pinned generation and recipe). *If wrong:* If nothing remains, remove POST-CLEAN and close the port epic at CP-NODE-CUT; if Josh wants POST-CLEAN to have its own go, add a POST-CLEAN review after CP-NODE-CUT's window.

After TPL, each such edit also bumps gdaemon and is a prepared commit that the next checkpoint cut lands in its step 6, after the backup and the rehearsal, and that cut's activation promotes it (ruling 20); between cuts only an emergency cutover on Josh's word promotes one. *Basis:* Ruling 15 ('That means no template moves or edits until retirement'); ruling 6 (bug and friction fixes continue); D33 (the bundled patterns need a form Rust's engine accepts); the live daemon loads each template edit at its next restart or reload_cache. *If wrong:* If Josh means no edits at all, RULE-1A leaves the YAML unchanged and the Rust engine compiles those patterns with an exact-pinned fancy-regex dependency for them only, a new dependency for Josh as in D8; the rewrites land in S3-DELETE, and bundled-template friction fixes need Josh's go until then.

## Checkpoint and cutover model

Checkpoint model (rulings 14 and 16, confirmed by Josh). A checkpoint is a review chunk (kind checkpoint, category manual, following the manual protocol in its goal: escalate_task, then de_escalate_task after Josh's go, then close_task) followed by one cutover chunk, or four for CP-TEMPLATE. The order: CP-RUNNER, CP-MCP, CP-TEMPLATE, CP-WAVE1 to CP-WAVE5, CP-PREDELETE (its cutover makes the live generation Python-free), S3-DELETE, CP-FINAL (the final post-deletion checkpoint), then CP-NODE for Stage 4 and POST-CLEAN. A review records a packet, escalates to Josh and closes only on his go. A cutover is category code: it owns the activation commit, which gets the code-reviewer seat, together with the prepared deactivation commit, the prepared commits it lands and its approved picks, before the hold is set. Every cutover goal carries nine steps in this order: (1) one global send_message before anything else, naming the backup's restart, the activation restart, the window, its triggers, the landing freeze, the loss window and how a session waits to land; (2) a live read of project_policy.quiet_hours, never copied, starting only when the backup, the rehearsal and the whole window end before the next quiet hours, and a direct read of the protected-runs route that continues only on a 200 answer listing no run; (3) the activation and deactivation commits prepared and given the code-reviewer seat, then GEN-ROLLBACK's hold set, the installed generation pinned by its manifest, the landing freeze set and bound to this task, the cutover branch rebased onto the frozen 0.9.0, then the approved plain picks landed with their pick-ledger update (D40), and the window plan recorded with its trigger table; the pinned generation is the previous cutover's last promotion, which is its activation commit or the last fix-forward or deactivation commit its window promoted, because between checkpoints only an emergency cutover on Josh's word promotes, besides GEN-ROLLBACK's one landing drill (D39); (4) a verified backup with gobby hub-backup, whose stop runs the same protected-run admission as cutover's; (5) a rollback rehearsal of exactly those reviewed commits in an isolated home on a fresh dedicated database, scrubbed of live channels, servers, webhooks and cron jobs, pointed at scratch Qdrant and FalkorDB containers and run on a loopback-only network, where the pinned generation is installed, the reviewed activated build promoted over it, the pinned generation restored and the reviewed deactivation build promoted over that, and where the restored generation serves on the unchanged schema, or on the migrated rehearsal hub when the cutover carries an expand step, and reads back the Rust-written rows, or, for a drop, starts on the restored backup; (6) the activation commit, after the live reads again and with the hold and the pin extended to the window's real end, landed right after the cut's prepared commits (schema inputs, post-TPL templates and the picks that carry either or a gcode or ghook version), which land only here, after the backup and the rehearsal (D22): it flips only that stage's code defaults and carries one 0.0.1 bump per shipped binary whose fingerprint changed since its last bump, gcode and ghook included, with Cargo.lock, the managed pins and the gcode floor in step, is landed under the freeze by the hold's owner, checked against 0.9.0 HEAD, and promoted with gobby cutover --hold-token from an unspawned, operator-opened session through the main checkout's CLI, which also promotes gmcp and gterm when they changed; (7) a bounded window with named triggers, held with a background watch and wait_for_coordination; (8) the outcome, recorded on the task and chosen by the trigger table: it works, and the commit that step 6 promoted is tagged port/<checkpoint id> for A to adopt (D40); it works well enough to debug, so the session fixes forward with the pin and the hold extended, for at most two fix cycles, the last landing within 24 hours of the first outcome-2 decision, unless Josh's go set another bound, and once the clean window after the last fix passes, the last promoted commit is tagged the same way; or it rolls back and Josh reassesses, while in-flight dependent chunks stop at their next checkpoint; (9) the rollback recipe: gobby rollback restore of the pinned generation with its named members (gdaemon alone by default, the stamped set after a schema step), then the prepared deactivation commit, which also reverts the cut's schema inputs, landed under the freeze and promoted, so an expand step is undone with no backup restore (D22); a backup restore comes first only for a drop (CP-FINAL-CUT, POST-CLEAN) or CP-WAVE3-CUT's relocation, after every live agent seat is ended, with the seats relaunched once the restored daemon is healthy. Every recipe names only install-local state, so A runs it unchanged if its own adoption of a checkpoint rolls back; A adopts by running the cutover's steps on its own install, with its main checkout moved to the tag in step 6's place after its own backup and rehearsal (D40). Post-deletion cutovers (CP-FINAL-CUT, CP-NODE-CUT and POST-CLEAN) run the same steps through V1A's Rust verbs. Windows are serialized: each cutover depends on the one before. The template fan-out waits on CP-TEMPLATE-CUT; each later wave's first chunks wait on the previous wave's review, so building overlaps the previous window. The landing freeze holds their landings only from that cutover's step 3 to its close; a landing outside that span lands dormant (D37), and on outcome 3 the cutover's project message stops them (A7-WAVES). Per-checkpoint scope, switches, rollback targets and windows are in the checkpoint table.

## Python strategy

(1) Python edits on 0.9.0 (D4): tests/ and scripts/ for recording, and scripts/port/ for the port's checks; the R0-R6 worker package and runner edits; GEN-ROLLBACK's promotion, rollback, landing-freeze-owner, hub-backup admission and protected-runs answer modules; R-RETIRE's runner refusal; one-line allow-listed worker-op registrations for single-owner services, added by the Rust caller's chunk; TERM-1's dormant terminal route helper; GW-2's dormant loopback compatibility endpoint; SCHEMA-WINDOW's preflight edit, a prepared commit that CP-RUNNER-CUT lands; S3-NAME's dormant gobby-name installer constant, which CP-PREDELETE-CUT's commit A turns on, and its packaging edit in commit B; S3-DELETE; and bug fixes and friction fixes (ruling 6), which land on 0.9.0 like everything else (ruling 15). Every edit other than a bug fix, TMUX-PURGE's purge (D129), R-RETIRE's refusal and GEN-ROLLBACK's generation-retaining promotion is dormant (D4): behaviorally inert at landing, because new CLI processes and lazily imported modules run it at once. GEN-ROLLBACK's retention is live at landing, so the generation each cutover pins is already retained. No per-family deletion, no Python client of a Rust endpoint, no modernization. (2) Still-Python families calling a ported family keep calling the Python implementation in-process over the shared tables, and differential replay of each family's corpus proves the two equivalent. Rust reaches a still-Python family only through its existing HTTP or MCP surface or an allow-listed worker op; Python never calls Rust. (3) Shared tables (D19): one schema chain, the same lock keys and notify channels, Rust tolerates every Python-written row. Coexistence is live from CP-RUNNER-CUT on (runner job, recovery and lease rows), and from CP-MCP-CUT for the gateway's schema lease rows. A value gdaemon hands to Python, such as GOBBY_TERMINAL_ROUTE, is set only by gdaemon's compiled defaults, and Python follows the latched value (TERM-1's helper), so an activation flips only gdaemon's default. (4) Worker ops: the Rust side stops calling an op at the activation that replaces it, and no registration is removed before S3-DELETE, because pinned and retained generations still call it. S3-FREEZE asserts that the activated build calls none. (5) Deletion (D14, ruling 14): Python stays whole until S3-DELETE, which runs after CP-PREDELETE-CUT has made the live generation Python-free; until then every retained generation still finds its Python worker code in the checkout. (6) Live-checkout constraints: no template moves before S3-DELETE; a template edit only as A17-TEMPLATES allows, with its rule-17 bump and, after TPL, a gdaemon bump and a landing inside the next checkpoint cut, as a prepared commit in its step 6; expand-only migrations, as prepared commits that the cut which activates their chunk lands in its step 6 (D22 as resolved); Python edits dormant, with D4's exceptions; 0.9.0 restartable at every landed commit and promoted only at checkpoint cuts (D39 as resolved).

## Branching (ruling 15)

0.9.0 is the integration branch on the port machine (P), and P's main checkout sits on it (D40). Each chunk works in its own task worktree off 0.9.0 (for example 0.9.0-rust) and lands with ordinary land_commit. Nothing merges into 0.9.0 from another branch, and D1's option A is not built. Python fixes, POST-CLEAN and Stage 4 all land on 0.9.0. 0.5.0 freezes at the cut SHA (ruling 15). The other machine (A, the Game Goblins machine) runs that SHA from a restored copy of P's hub and makes no gobby edits (ruling 24), so no branch forks from 0.9.0, no fix flows from A, and the pick steps that every review and cutover carries have nothing to list (D40 item 3). A adopts a checkpoint when Josh decides, in checkpoint order, by running that cutover's steps on its own install with its main checkout fast-forwarded to the port/<checkpoint id> tag in step 6's place, after its own backup and rehearsal (D40 item 4). The start gate moves project_policy's integration branch to 0.9.0 on P; it rewords AGENTS.md rule 15's prose (AGENTS.md:146) while its dated operator ruling stays verbatim, rewords rule 10, and makes the 0.9.0 runs of ci.yml and rust-ci.yml required on push and on pull requests (D34, D85).

## Live-checkout constraints

The live daemon runs from the 0.9.0 checkout, so every landed commit must keep it working:

- No template moves before S3-DELETE.
- A template edit lands only as A17-TEMPLATES allows: a ruling 6 bug or friction fix, or a rewrite that preserves behavior on Python's engine, such as RULE-1A's. The live daemon must accept it unchanged, it carries its rule-17 bump, and once TPL declares the template tree as an embedded input it also bumps gdaemon and is a prepared commit that the next checkpoint cut lands in its step 6, under that cut's backup, and that cut's activation promotes it (ruling 20).
- Migrations are expand-only until CP-FINAL-CUT (D22). A chunk's schema inputs (its migrations with their assets.rs entries, and the tests that need the new schema) form one prepared commit on the append-only branch port/prepared/<chunk id>, reviewed with the chunk and recorded by SHA at its close; the first checkpoint cut whose activation needs that schema lands it in its step 6, after the verified backup and the rehearsal and immediately before the activation commit, under the same freeze. Between cuts no landing changes the schema pin, because gobby restart and hub-backup refuse while the checkout's pin differs from the installed identity (src/gobby/storage/schema_divergence.py:251-265, via src/gobby/cli/daemon_preflight.py:68-78). The preflights accept a cut's migrations only with a pin generated from a real build, a regenerated catalog manifest, transactional migrations inside the 5 s lock and 60 s statement limits, serial numbers and no edited applied migration. From CP-RUNNER-CUT on every retained generation accepts a hub ahead by expand-only receipts (SCHEMA-WINDOW), so a rollback across an expand step is the binary restore plus the deactivation commit; only a drop, at CP-FINAL-CUT or POST-CLEAN, needs the backup restore.
- Python edits are dormant (D4), except bug fixes, TMUX-PURGE's purge (D129), R-RETIRE's refusal and GEN-ROLLBACK's generation-retaining promotion. That promotion is live at landing, so the generation each cutover pins is already retained.
- Every later pinned generation finds its Python worker code in the checkout, because nothing in Python is deleted before S3-DELETE, no worker-op registration is removed before it, and worker protocol changes are additive.
- 0.9.0 stays restartable at every landed commit and promotable at every checkpoint cut: a landing bumps only gdaemon, between checkpoint cuts no landing changes the schema pin, the gcode or ghook floor or, after TPL, a template, and only a checkpoint cut promotes (D39).

## Rollback and packaging

Families are library crates on gcore inside one gdaemon (D36). GEN-ROLLBACK keeps three generations, each with a manifest (D38). A cutover sets a hold whose token every promotion and restore in it must pass (gobby rollback hold set, then --hold-token on gobby cutover, gobby install and gobby rollback restore), pins the generation installed at that moment, and sets a landing freeze bound to its own task, so land_commit admits only that task's session. gobby cutover also promotes gmcp and gterm when their versions changed. A restore names its members (--bin, gdaemon alone by default, and always the stamped set gcode, gdaemon and ghook for a cut that changed the schema identity) and burns the activated versions, never the restored target's own. Dormancy is code defaults only (D37). From CP-RUNNER-CUT on, every retained generation accepts a hub ahead by expand-only receipts (SCHEMA-WINDOW), so a rollback across an expand step is the binary restore plus the deactivation commit, which reverts the cut's schema inputs with its activation, and loses no write. A rollback across a drop (CP-FINAL-CUT and POST-CLEAN only), or across CP-WAVE3-CUT's attachment relocation once it ran, is a backup restore first, after every live agent seat is ended, with the seats relaunched once the restored daemon is healthy, and it loses every write made after the backup. Every cutover recipe uses only install-local state (its own verified backup, the same schema inputs, its own pin, hold and generations), so A runs that whole cutover on its own install when it adopts a checkpoint, with its main checkout moved to the tag in step 6's place after its own backup and rehearsal (D40).

## Chunk protocol

1. Run step 3's gport start check first, from the main checkout, and claim nothing while it refuses. Then claim the chunk task in a default-agent session, spawned by the port dispatcher or operator-opened (D39, D116), in a task worktree off 0.9.0 at the launch base that check recorded. An operator-opened session makes that worktree with gobby-worktrees:create_worktree(branch_name=<branch>, base_branch='0.9.0', task_id=<task>), because git worktree add and the provider's own worktree tool are refused in it (src/gobby/install/shared/workflows/rules/worker-safety/block-git-worktree-mutations-interactive.yaml:5; src/gobby/install/shared/workflows/rules/worker-safety/block-native-enter-worktree.yaml:5); its own directory stays the main checkout, so it works in the worktree by absolute path and names that path in every Workflow agent's prompt. A session the dispatcher spawned finds this check done and this claim made, and starts at step 2. If get_worktree_by_task (gobby-worktrees) finds a worktree for this task, an earlier session on it stopped or died. The stale claim sweep releases a dead session's claim (src/gobby/storage/tasks/_automation.py:89); until it has, get_task names the owner, and claim_task(force=true) takes the claim once get_session shows that owner is no longer active. Reuse that worktree, settle its uncommitted files, and resume after the branch's last checkpoint commit, rebuilding any lost scratch report from the branch. If that session's candidate already landed, only step 8's close remains.
2. Merge 0.9.0 into the worktree, and rerun differential replay for every touched family that is ported or in flight. From P0-RECORD's landing on, read docs/port/record.md next: this chunk's Found Work section, its family's debt-not-to-port list and owned rows, the frozen seam contract section and the known-bad index, because step 4 builds on them. Read this chunk's Found Work section again after every later merge of 0.9.0: a seam change or a fix task may have added a line to it (step 9, D40 item 3), and this chunk handles that line before it lands.
3. gport start <chunk id>, run before the claim as step 1 says: every depends_on chunk's Gobby task is closed with closed_reason done, and for every kind except checkpoint its linked commit is an ancestor of 0.9.0 HEAD; it records the launch base. Until P0-RECORD lands gport, check the same rule by hand with get_task. gport is never promoted, so it is not on PATH: run it as cargo run --locked -q -p gobby-port -- <arguments>, in the main checkout for start and in the worktree for check-slice and ledger, because a path-invoked ./target/debug/gport counts as script execution, which the task gate refuses a session with no claim (src/gobby/install/shared/workflows/rules/task-enforcement/require-task-before-edit.yaml:18). A task outside the map, such as a review's no-go fix or a fix or port between reviews (D40 item 3), is filed as a child of #21542, so the port dispatcher starts it (D116). It has no chunk id, so gport start and gport check-slice refuse it: it checks its dependencies by hand with get_task, skips check-slice at step 6 and follows every other step. A fix that completes a closed chunk's row updates that chunk's docs/port/status/<chunk id>.json with its evidence line, because D17's rate reads that file.
4. Run one ultracode Workflow (at most 16 subagents): the debt-not-to-port pass, the oracle recording first when the brief says so, adversarial design review, tests rewritten from contracts, implementation, adversarial code review.
5. Use 1-3 checkpoints, each a commit on the chunk branch plus a scratch report. A chunk with ledger rows keeps docs/port/status/<chunk id>.json, one entry per row (P0-RECORD); a row marked done names a red commit and a later green commit on this branch, so commit each failing test before the code that passes it, because gport check-slice refuses a done row without both SHAs in its range. While the Workflow runs, the session yields with wait_for_coordination(background_task_id=<the Workflow's provider task id>, timeout=3600), omitting owner_session (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/coordination.py:45-49), and registers it again after every timeout wake and after every prompt; after a compaction it fetches the wait tool's schema again first. A stop message that names this chunk, from a review's no-go or a cutover's outcome 3, holds the session at its next checkpoint, landing nothing, until the matching release message arrives; it waits with wait_for_coordination(owner_session=<the dispatcher>, reply=true, timeout=3600), registered again after every timeout and every prompt. It does not wait on the sender, because a review's fixes outlast the session that sent the stop, and a wait on a session that has ended returns owner_ended at once and leaves this run to the idle check (src/gobby/agents/idle_check_handler.py). The release is a project send with wake=true, which reaches a session holding a claim whichever session it waits on.
6. Validate locally: cargo tests, the isolated full-daemon harness (never the live hub, never ~/.gobby/bin), the dormancy proof (code defaults replay every existing corpus unchanged), gport check-slice <chunk id> --task <this task's ref>, and gport ledger, or scripts/port/check_coverage.py until gport ledger's diff is 0. Managed SRT changes what some checks prove inside a spawned session: a test that launches an agent under SRT fails there, because macOS refuses a nested profile (tests/e2e/conftest.py:490-498); a process check can miss what it may not inspect (docs/guides/gterminal-development-guide.md:445-453); and a proof that a non-loopback connection fails passes there whatever the code does. Docker is refused there too (src/gobby/agents/srt_settings.py:63-64). Send such a check's test command and this worktree's path to the port dispatcher with send_message(target='parent'), register wait_for_coordination(owner_session=<the dispatcher>, reply=true, timeout=3600) as step 8 does, and cite the reply in the validation attestation (D116).
7. Spawn the independent code-reviewer seat on the task worktree with spawn_agent(agent='code-reviewer', worktree_id=<this worktree's id, from get_worktree_by_task>, claim=false, prompt='Review <full SHA> of <task ref> in <worktree path>. Send your verdict and findings with send_message(target=parent). No pipeline, lead or claim hand-off applies here; land, merge and close nothing.'). It takes no task_id, as Josh's 2026-11-03 rule says, so the claim stays with this session, and claim=false joins the tree at its HEAD, because without it the spawn merges the base into the tree, which moves the candidate, and refuses a tree that a live session has claimed (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/spawn_agent/_implementation.py:470, 512-529; src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/spawn_agent/_worktree_reuse.py:57-116, 119-149; tests/mcp_proxy/tools/spawn_agent/test_associated_worktree_join.py:28). The seat starts on the provider project_policy names, whose CLI must be on P (D119). Wait with wait_for_coordination(owner_session=<the seat>, reply=true, timeout=3600), registered again after every timeout and every prompt. When a wait ends without a reply and gobby-agents:list_running_agents no longer shows the seat, spawn it once more with the same arguments; a seat still listed after three such waits counts as lost once stop_agent ends it. A second loss escalates the task to Josh, and once he says the seat can start, run de_escalate_task and claim_task and resume at this spawn. Fix and recheck, stop it, then record the seat's result and the candidate SHA on the task as an attestation. Send nothing to a session on A: the coordinator that Josh's 2026-11-03 rule names, gobby#19309, has expired, the fleet seats beside it ended before the cut, and no chunk depends on cross-machine messaging (D40 item 5). If Josh opens a coordinator seat on P, send the SHA to it as well; the security-auditor seat on P takes only the candidates named below. A candidate whose changed paths match project_policy.security_paths, whose task carries the security-review label or whose brief names a security review, a gated chunk under D106 among them, also waits for the security-auditor seat that Josh opens on P (D115), because D115 asks for that seat's independent approval of the exact SHA. When this map was approved, land_commit refused that SHA without the seat's approved security-review attestation and a spawned default-agent session could not spawn the seat itself; since #25900 default's capabilities ['*'] waive those rules for a default-definition caller and cover the seat's in spawn-capability-authority, the rule that refused the spawn, so the wait is this protocol's own rule (src/gobby/install/shared/workflows/rules/task-closure/security.yaml:25-60; src/gobby/workflows/agent_models.py:37-51; src/gobby/install/shared/workflows/agents/default.yaml:5). The wait runs as follows: after step 8's merge and version bump and before land_commit, send it the task ref and the resulting commit's full SHA, with target='session' and the session ref that gobby-agents:list_running_agents gives, then register wait_for_coordination(owner_session=<the seat>, reply=true, timeout=3600) and register it again after every timeout and every prompt. On a rejection, fix, rerun the code-reviewer seat and send the new SHA; every changed SHA needs its own approval. If a landing during the wait changed a path this candidate also changes, and the gdaemon version line usually is one, merge 0.9.0 again, bump again and send the new SHA before land_commit, because land_commit refuses that candidate (step 8). When list_running_agents shows no live seat, at the send or after a wait that ends without a reply, escalate the task to Josh, who reruns D115's command, and land nothing until the seat has approved. Escalation releases the claim, so once Josh says the seat is live, run de_escalate_task and claim_task and resume at the send.
8. Merge 0.9.0 into the worktree again. A chunk session lands and bumps, and never promotes (D39): on P it never runs gobby install, gobby cutover or gobby rollback restore (GEN-ROLLBACK's live drill and TMUX-PURGE's leaves are the planned exceptions, D39 and D129), because gobby install rebuilds and promotes gdaemon whenever its managed pin is above the installed version, which every landing's bump makes true (src/gobby/cli/install_setup_gdaemon.py:79-112, 141-170), and rebuilds gclient, gmcp and gterm on every run; its landing bumps gdaemon by 0.0.1 when its fingerprint changed since its last bump, and leaves gcode, ghook, gmcp, gclient and gterm to the next activation commit, because the gcode and ghook pins are runtime floors (src/gobby/code_index/gcode_versions.py:5-6; src/gobby/hooks/runtime_compat.py:17, 28). A chunk that carries schema inputs or, after TPL, a template change lands its dormant code here and puts those inputs and its own tests that need them, validated with that code in the isolated harness, in one prepared commit on port/prepared/<chunk id>, recorded by SHA at close, which the checkpoint cut that needs it lands in its step 6 (D22). A chunk whose code or tests need a schema that a depends_on chunk's prepared commit carries, and that lands before the cut that lands that commit, applies the upstream prepared commit (its SHA is on that task's close record) only to its isolated harness tree, which for a spawned session is a local scratch branch in this worktree because its write scope stays on this worktree, never to its landing candidate, and puts its own tests that need that schema in its own prepared commit on port/prepared/<chunk id>, based on the upstream one and recorded by SHA at close; the same cut lands it right after the upstream commit. CI on 0.9.0 never runs a test that needs a schema 0.9.0 does not carry. During a landing freeze, send the cutover session a direct message, then register wait_for_coordination(owner_session=<cutover session>, reply=true, timeout=3600) and register it again after every timeout and every prompt; the cutover session messages back when the freeze clears. The merge and the bump make a new candidate SHA, and land_commit refuses a candidate whose implementation, test-after and validation attestations name another SHA (src/gobby/install/shared/workflows/rules/task-closure/coding.yaml:116-127). So commit them, link that commit, rerun step 6's checks on it, and record those three attestations on its full SHA, implementation before test-after (:86-93). No coding rule reads a self-review attestation since #25852, so the session records none, and step 7's attestation of the seat's result stays the record of the review. The seat runs again only when the merge resolved a conflict outside the version lines. Then land_commit onto 0.9.0 and push 0.9.0. A spawned session can neither push nor read CI, because spawn_agent runs it under managed SRT with no git network and no git or gh credentials (src/gobby/agents/sandbox_gate.py:22-33; docs/guides/sandboxing.md:245-249), so it sends the landed SHA to the port dispatcher with send_message(target='parent'), registers wait_for_coordination(owner_session=<the dispatcher>, reply=true, timeout=3600), sends again after a timeout with no reply, and registers the wait again after every prompt; the reply is its CI result (D116). Check the pushed commit's CI, then record the closing attestation and close_task with that attested SHA, never a generated land merge's, because a validation attestation takes the landing-receipt exception only from a receipt that carries land_commit's own verified version bump (src/gobby/install/shared/workflows/rules/task-closure/coding.yaml:95-114), which land_commit generates only when the landing branch is named 0.5.0 (src/gobby/tasks/land_commit.py:750-774; src/gobby/tasks/closure_snapshot.py:37-70). If land_commit refuses with base_update_required or merge_conflict, because another landing moved 0.9.0 through a path this candidate also changes, it has also escalated the task and released the claim (src/gobby/tasks/land_commit.py:469-484, 714-727, 742-744; src/gobby/storage/tasks/_transitions.py:417-456), so this session resumes it itself: de_escalate_task, claim_task, then this step again from its merge, with the attestations the new SHA needs.
9. Found work follows AGENTS rule 4. From P0-RECORD's landing on, a line goes under the Found Work section of the chunk it concerns in docs/port/record.md, in the commit that fixes it; gport check-slice passes a Python or frozen seam path outside this chunk's slice only when a Found Work line under this chunk names that path. A seam contract change is found work of this kind: it lands on 0.9.0 in the owning seam file, with any landed caller it breaks fixed in the same commit so that 0.9.0 stays green, and in-flight chunks pick it up when they merge 0.9.0 (steps 2 and 8).

A checkpoint review instead follows the manual protocol in its goal (escalate_task, then de_escalate_task after Josh's go, then close_task), and a cutover chunk follows its nine steps. A corpus or golden case that a plan gives a waiver citation keeps its recording until the activation commit that flips its surface, which lands the citation: a citation makes the case fail while the old answer serves, so it would fail step 6's dormancy proof. Until then the chunk's own replay reads a fixture copy of the entry and citation in its tests, which tells the cut what to land (D48). Where a family plan, a task card or other pre-map text disagrees with a map decision or a chunk's explicit text, the map wins; docs/port/plan-drift.md lists the disagreements known at approval, and a chunk that finds another records it under Found Work. Where the map is silent, the plan applies. A map choice that proves broken is a gap: report it through Found Work instead of working around it from the plan. No chunk landing adds an entry to docs/contracts/parity-waivers.json or changes the parity ledger, even where a family plan's leaf says it appends its entry: the entry lands with its citation in the activation commit that flips its surface, because each entry writes a Waived note on a ledger row that the old answer still serves (scripts/generate_parity_ledger.py:190-194) and gdaemon embeds the manifest (crates/gdaemon/src/front_door/waivers.rs:12) (D84). A CI run that a later push to 0.9.0 cancelled (.github/workflows/ci.yml:16-18) is superseded, not red: step 8's check records that and goes on, because the later push's run covers the commit, and a red result there is found work for the session that landed it (D85). Plan short names in briefs: s2-11 is .gobby/plans/s2-11-hub-hooks-rules.md; S2.7 is .gobby/plans/s2-7-hub-attention-dispatch.md; sessions, the sessions plan and sessions-family are .gobby/plans/sessions-family.md; memory and the memory plan are .gobby/plans/memory-family.md; code-index is .gobby/plans/code-index-family.md; agents-family is .gobby/plans/agents-family.md; tasks-family is .gobby/plans/tasks-family.md; the AI plan is .gobby/plans/gdaemon-ai-providers-family.md; the Projects plan is .gobby/plans/gdaemon-projects-files-docs-family.md; the multiplexer plan is .gobby/plans/external-mcp-transport-multiplexer.md; gmcp-stdio is .gobby/plans/gmcp-stdio.md; hub-mode is .gobby/plans/hub-mode.md; DR1-DR8 are in .gobby/plans/rust-rule-evaluation.md; and #25341's numbered sections are in .gobby/plans/task-25341.md. A plan's text that a later Python fix changed does not apply: on that point the port follows Python at the chunk's base, because its corpora record that behavior, and the session notes the plan's stale text under Found Work. A usage limit or a provider outage is not a red result and closes nothing, and the branch stays. A spawned session that one stops loses its pane and its claim once the watchdog ends the run with a provider terminal reason (src/gobby/agents/lifecycle_monitor.py:668-688; src/gobby/agents/idle_check_handler.py:386-395), and the replacement the port dispatcher starts afterwards resumes under step 1 (D116). An operator-opened session keeps both: a usage limit holds its pane on the provider's menu, where no wake lands until Josh submits a prompt there after the reset (src/gobby/hooks/event_handlers/_misc.py:81-85, 415-416), and after an outage its next wake or prompt reaches it. Whichever session resumes reruns the stopped Workflow from the branch's last checkpoint commit (step 5). crates.io or GitHub down is an outage too, so retry after the next wait. A brief over 15,000 characters comes back from get_task as an offload envelope whose preview holds only its first 2,000: read the whole brief with gobby-results:get_tool_result, following next_offset until it is null, and call get_task again after the 7-day retention (src/gobby/config/features.py:127-143; src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/results.py:149-188). A port carries every trust check in the module it ports, named in its brief or not: whatever refuses, bounds, redacts or confines untrusted input, with Python's negative tests replayed as native cases, because a recorded corpus holds no attack and a missing check passes replay. A native HTTP client keeps its Python client's policy: httpx follows no redirect by default and reqwest follows ten, so each client sets redirect::Policy::none() unless its Python source sets follow_redirects=True, and trust_env=False becomes .no_proxy(). A native route that reads a body states its limit, because axum's body extractors stop at 2 MiB by default and Starlette has no limit. A native child whose Python spawn passes env= calls env_clear() and sets that map, because Rust's Command inherits gdaemon's environment (D124). A chunk that reuses existing native code lists Python's steps on that path against the native code's before its oracle runs, and ports each missing step or reports it under Found Work, because an oracle that compares native output with native output proves nothing about parity (D124). Josh approved this map on 2026-11-05 with every default (ruling 23), so a decision status that waits on his word at map approval is settled.

### GEN-ROLLBACK: Generation-retaining promotion, the window hold and gobby rollback

- **kind:** infra
- **goal:** D38, the first 0.9.0 chunk after TMUX-PURGE (D129). It must land before any promotion but TMUX-PURGE's, so that the first promotion through it retains the generation that the purge left installed; today promotion replaces binaries in place (bin_set_coherence.py:88-153). gport does not exist until P0-RECORD builds it, so this chunk checks protocol step 3's start rule by hand with get_task: its one dependency is TMUX-PURGE, so it confirms that TMUX-PURGE closed as done, with its commit an ancestor of 0.9.0 HEAD, and records the launch base. (a) Generation store: before every promotion of the stamped set, copy the outgoing files (gcode, gdaemon and ghook, the identity stamp, the release-identity receipts, version stamps, sidecars and source-sha files) into ~/.gobby/bin/generations/<seq>-<utc>/ with a manifest of the source commit, versions, source identities, schema identity, promotion time and the promoting session and task. Copies, never links, because the installers re-sign, chmod and rewrite sidecars in place (install_setup_gdaemon.py:115-138, 173-178). Keep three generations and never prune the installed one or a held or pinned one. The hook point is inside promote_workspace_binary_set after the locks and the second preflight (bin_set_coherence.py:128-134); gclient, gmcp and gterm get the same snapshot in their own promotion paths (install_setup_gclient.py:168-189; cutover.py:439-446; install_setup_gmcp.py:180-263; install_setup_gterm.py:345-432), and gclient's snapshot includes bin_dir/gobby whenever that name is installed. gobby cutover already builds gmcp and gterm, proves both with the stamped set before its stop, so a changed source under an unbumped version refuses the whole cutover, and promotes each after the daemon is back (src/gobby/cli/cutover.py:174-192, 329-347, 391-436; d7998bb304). This chunk adds the hold token and the snapshot to those promotions, so an activation commit's gmcp and gterm bumps go live inside its window. A retention preflight (free space, a writable directory) runs before cutover's stop, so a retention failure never leaves the daemon stopped. The release fingerprint also covers the paths a crate declares as embedded inputs under [package.metadata.gobby] embedded in its Cargo.toml, which _closure reads (bin_release_identity.py:111-137, 162-204). affected_binaries, which picks the binaries a landing bumps (src/gobby/tasks/landing_versions.py:110), does not see such a path today: it returns early unless a changed path is a root input, Cargo.lock or under crates/, and _touches_closure matches only paths inside the closure's crate directories (bin_release_identity.py:328-369); no crate declares one until TPL does, so this is inert at landing. (b) The window hold and burned versions live in check_binary_release (bin_release_identity.py:234), the single choke point that component installs also reach (bin_freshness_promotion.py:168-171). While a hold is set, every promotion without its token is refused, including another session's cutover and gobby install. A burned version is refused for good, which closes the version-reuse hole after a restore. A hold records the cutover task, the session, the token and an expiry at the planned end of the window. The landing freeze is bound to the hold's task: set_landing_freeze records that task (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/tasks/_landing.py:35-72), and while the freeze is set land_commit admits only that task's session and refuses every other with landing_frozen (src/gobby/tasks/land_commit.py:710-712; src/gobby/tasks/landing_policy.py:115-140); set_landing_freeze likewise refuses a clear or a new set while a freeze is bound, from any session but the one that holds the bound task's claim, and gobby rollback hold clear (Josh's crash path) clears the bound freeze together with the hold; B0-CLOSE carries the same rule natively. (c) A new src/gobby/cli/rollback.py: gobby rollback list; pin, pin extend and unpin (a checkpoint's pinned generation, held until its window closes); hold set, which prints the token, hold extend --hold-token <token> --until <time>, hold status and hold clear; burn <generation>, which burns that generation's gdaemon version so restore refuses it; and restore <generation> --bin <members> --hold-token <token>, gdaemon alone by default, or --all for the stamped set with that generation's gclient, gmcp and gterm snapshots. The gclient restore member includes bin_dir/gobby: the restore puts back the retained copy when the restored generation had one, and removes the name when it had none. gobby cutover and gobby install take --hold-token <token> and pass it to check_binary_release. Restore runs the agent and node refusals, restart_start_refusal with the retained gdaemon and stamp (its schema plan refuses a hub newer than the target, runner_plan.rs:156-160, until SCHEMA-WINDOW, promoted at CP-RUNNER-CUT, makes the plan accept expand-only receipts above the target's head), the stop admissions and the stop, which writes restart intent as cutover's stop does (src/gobby/cli/cutover.py:490-497), so the daemon sends its DAEMON HOLD before the stop and DAEMON BACK after the restored generation's healthy start (src/gobby/sessions/daemon_notices.py:82-92; src/gobby/runner_lifecycle.py:72-84). It moves aside an installed binary that cannot print --version, calls promote_workspace_binary_set with the retained paths and receipts (the guard accepts them, because downgrades pass at bin_release_identity.py:266-267), burns the outgoing versions, never a version equal to the restored target's own, checks the restart target and starts. Its legitimate bypasses are exactly three: no build, no catalog freshness test and no unchanged-sources check, because the retained bytes were proven when first promoted. Every other guard runs. (d) hub-backup's stop gains the protected-run admission that cutover's stop runs (src/gobby/cli/cutover.py:258-283; src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/cli.py:228-240), a ruling 6 bug fix, because hub-backup stops the live daemon today with no protected-run check; the same stop also runs that admission's pending-handoff guard (src/gobby/cli/cutover.py:276-282) and writes restart intent, as cutover's stop does (src/gobby/cli/cutover.py:490-497), because hub-backup starts again the daemon it stopped (src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/cli.py:266-267) and the daemon sends DAEMON HOLD only before a restart-intent stop (src/gobby/sessions/daemon_notices.py:82-92), while today its stop_daemon call runs no handoff guard and writes stop intent (src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/cli.py:240; src/gobby/cli/utils_shutdown.py:45-51, 149-155); and fetch_protected_runs reports an answer from a running daemon other than a 200 with a runs list as unknown, which every Python stop admission (src/gobby/cli/cutover.py:273; src/gobby/cli/daemon_lifecycle.py:266, 580; and this hub-backup admission) refuses without --force, while a transport error still reports no runs, matching V1A's rule. Josh confirms the class of both edits at map approval. (e) Docs: AGENTS.md Architecture Facts, crates/AGENTS.md, docs/guides/admin-operations.md, and the daemon.md skill reference with a rule-17 version bump. Rehearse in an isolated home first. After landing, unless Josh refused the drill at map approval (D38), run a live drill outside quiet hours with a global announcement, from an unspawned, operator-opened session, because activation refuses spawned agents (src/gobby/releases/activation.py:21-32), and after one verified gobby hub-backup (ruling 17); this drill is a planned exception to promoting only at checkpoint cuts (D39). First compare each installed .<binary>-release-identity.json source identity with 0.9.0 HEAD's; if any differs, promote a bumped build through the normal path first, which this chunk retains. Then land a no-op gdaemon version bump and promote it, run gobby rollback restore to the retained pre-bump copy, which burns the no-op version, and land a second bump and promote it, so the installed gdaemon matches HEAD again. Protocol step 6 reads differently here, because no gport and no harness exist yet and this landing is live under D4: validation is this chunk's oracle on temp homes, focused pytest of the modules it edits and scripts/port/check_coverage.py, with no dormancy proof. The drill runs before this task closes, so the session that claims this task is the unspawned, operator-opened session the drill needs (start gate item 14); if Josh refused the drill, protocol step 1 applies instead. Drill mechanics: run gobby rollback hold set, naming this task, before the first promotion, with an expiry at the drill's planned end; promote with gobby cutover --path <main checkout> --hold-token <token> through the main checkout's CLI, because a linked worktree's CLI is refused (src/gobby/utils/dev.py:134-153), and pass the same token on gobby rollback restore; run gobby rollback hold clear once the last promotion is healthy. Each bump commit changes only version files, is linked to this task and lands with land_commit, after its own reviewer seat (protocol step 7) and its own implementation, test-after and validation attestations on its SHA, because land_commit blocks a candidate whose latest attestations name another SHA (src/gobby/install/shared/workflows/rules/task-closure/coding.yaml:95-127); its validation is tests/install/test_version_pins.py. Record the isolated rehearsal and the drill as attestations on this task, the drill's with each promotion's and the restore's generation, version and burned version: CP-RUNNER-REVIEW's oracle reads them, and CP-RUNNER-CUT's pin check compares against the last promotion. Close this task after the drill, with close_task on the last landed SHA; the final message then asks Josh to prompt the port dispatcher, because an operator-opened session's close does not wake it (D116).

Generations promoted before CP-RUNNER-CUT boot the Python runner: CP-RUNNER-CUT's close burns their gdaemon versions with gobby rollback burn, so restore refuses them at once, and R-RETIRE then makes that refusal structural.
