- **goal:** Josh item 1. gport does not exist until this chunk builds it, so it checks protocol step 3's start rule by hand with get_task (GEN-ROLLBACK closed as done, with its commit an ancestor of 0.9.0 HEAD), and it runs its own new gport start, ledger and check-slice at protocol step 6. Commit docs/port/record.md, generated from Gobby at Phase 0: direction; decision record (every decision with Josh's answers); Josh's rulings pulled from memory with their when: clauses; per-family debt-not-to-port lists and owned ledger rows (from this map's selectors); the frozen seam wave contract section (filled by SEAM-FAMILY, SEAM-CALLERS, SEAM-WS, GW-1/GW-2); the known-bad index (P0-DECISIONS); a Found Work section per chunk that every chunk reads first and writes back to. Build crates/gport (package gobby-port, binary gport, publish=false, never promoted, so every session runs it as cargo run --locked -q -p gobby-port -- <verb>). gport start <chunk id> (protocol step 3): every depends_on chunk's Gobby task is closed with closed_reason done, and for every kind except checkpoint its linked commit is an ancestor of 0.9.0 HEAD; it records the launch base by printing it and writing no tracked file, because it runs from the main checkout before any claim and needs no worktree. gport ledger: frozen ledger plus map selectors to owner column and exit-rule check; replaces scripts/generate_parity_ledger.py and tests/test_parity_ledger.py, and, once its diff is 0, the scripts/port/check_coverage.py and scripts/port/check_dispositions.py checks that the start gate commits (it then reads the open-node snapshot and the disposition files as well as the ledger). gport check-slice <chunk id> --task <ref> re-cuts .gobby/plans/task-25341.md 0.2 for this map, which has no slice files. Its range is git log --no-merges 0.9.0..HEAD for commits and git diff --name-status from git merge-base 0.9.0 HEAD for paths, because protocol steps 2 and 8 merge 0.9.0 into the worktree, so the launch base gport start records is not the range's start; it reads its authority as bytes at that merge base: the map's chunk fields and the record's frozen list. A chunk's items are the ledger rows its selectors own, and a chunk with no rows has none. Each chunk with rows keeps docs/port/status/<chunk id>.json, one entry per row with that plan's status vocabulary, plus delegated and dropped for a row this map delegates or drops (D5), and, for done, its evidence line (red <sha> green <sha> test <command>); a refusal names the file and the vocabulary, so a chunk session learns the format from the tool. It refuses a .py path under src/gobby/ when the chunk's python_edits field starts with None, tests/ only or tests/ and scripts/ only, except src/gobby/install/version_pins.py, which every landing's gdaemon bump edits (tests/install/test_version_pins.py:23-40), and a file the record's frozen seam contract section lists, each unless a Found Work line under this chunk names that path; a registration-protocol violation; a commit whose subject does not start with [gobby-#N] for a ref passed with --task, which a session repeats for each subtask it made; a row at todo or specced, or a missing, duplicated or foreign row; and a done row whose red and green SHAs are not both in the range with red an ancestor of green. A non-Python file under src/gobby/ passes the path rule, because RULE-1A, PIPE-2, MUX-2 and V1A edit templates and skill references with python_edits None; A17-TEMPLATES and protocol step 8 govern those edits. gport check-slice --report <chunk id>... prints the rate D17 reads, (partial+stub)/(done+partial+stub) over the named chunks, leaving out needs-local, deferred-local, blocked, delegated and dropped rows, and exits 1 with no attempted items when that denominator is 0. gport census: per family, Python in-process callers by module, writers by table, Python caches over each table with their invalidation channel, and single-owner services with their Python callers, plus each retained generation's worker protocol version; built from the import graph plus gcode call sites, refreshed at CP-TEMPLATE-REVIEW and CP-WAVE3-REVIEW. The census also lists what the ledger cannot see: routes mounted only under non-default config (the web UI serving in src/gobby/servers/_app_ui.py, with no row among the 1,094) and any Python surface that has no row when the census runs, so S3-FREEZE's closure covers them. gport shapes: per-tool call counts and argument-key sets mined read-only from local CLI transcripts and the live daemon's tool metrics, with no values kept. It runs from an unspawned session, the review that needs it, because a managed run's bearer is refused the metrics routes (src/gobby/servers/auth_service.py:101-148) and its sandbox denies other providers' transcript roots (docs/guides/sandboxing.md:238-243). On P it reads the transcripts of P's own sessions and the hub's tool_metrics rows; after the port moves (D128), the laptop's transcripts stay behind and the restored hub brings the rows. Either way, a root it cannot read or does not find is recorded in its output and skipped, not an error. Freeze the ledger at the cut commit. Census targets also include the in-memory registry readers (running agents, terminal ownership through TerminalRuntimeRegistry, session caches, and CompletionEventRegistry's 24 references under hooks, workflows and mcp_proxy) and a per-package size table (582,631 src lines in 2,159 files, 1,056,889 test lines, 108,445 template lines) that sizes every brief. The record also carries the chunk protocol, copied verbatim from the map's chunk_protocol key; the registration protocol that gport check-slice enforces (the family list, workspace members, gdaemon dependencies, nextest overrides and the gclient verb table are append-only; Cargo.lock is regenerated after merging 0.9.0; migrations and node-commands contract versions take the next free number at landing; edits to serve.rs, the front_door/websocket refactor and front_door/auth.rs are serialized; version bumps follow the version rule, under which a landing bumps gdaemon when it changed its fingerprint and never promotes, while gcode, ghook, gmcp, gclient and gterm are bumped only in a cut's shipping commits (its activation commit, each outcome-2 fix commit and its deactivation commit) and in emergency cutover commits, and only checkpoint cuts promote (D39)); the pushed cut SHA every brief records as its reference base, while gport start records each chunk's own launch base (protocol step 3); and the D31 disposition of every open node. gport ledger also writes docs/contracts/parity-ledger.md as scripts/generate_parity_ledger.py does, with each docs/contracts/parity-waivers.json entry's note on its row (scripts/generate_parity_ledger.py:190-194), because CP-FINAL-CUT's and POST-CLEAN's activation commits add waiver entries after S3-DELETE removes that script (D47, D48). P0-HARNESS has not landed when this chunk validates, so its protocol step 6 is cargo tests for crates/gport, this chunk's oracle, scripts/port/check_coverage.py and its own gport start, ledger and check-slice as built, with no harness and no dormancy proof. gport start finds a chunk's task as the direct child of #21542 whose description starts with that chunk's brief heading, # <chunk id>: (scripts/port/render_briefs.py, which start gate item 10 uses), listing the children and reading each description through the daemon's task routes (src/gobby/servers/routes/tasks.py:227-248, 334; the list answers brief rows) with the operator token (crates/gcore/src/local_token.rs:25-44), and it refuses an id with no such child. So gport start runs only in an unspawned session, the port dispatcher's or an operator-opened one: a spawned session's run-scoped bearer is refused every /api/tasks route with route_not_permitted (src/gobby/servers/auth_service.py:101-148, 594-614), and a managed run cannot read the operator token. When this chunk's own session is spawned, it sends gport start's real-tree run through protocol step 6's route. gport check-slice and gport ledger read only git and files and make no daemon call, so they run inside a spawned session, and check-slice takes the task ref from its session, which has it from get_task, instead of reading #21542's tree. A task outside the map, such as a pick or a schema fix between reviews (D40 item 3), has no chunk id, so it skips gport start and check-slice and follows the rest of the protocol.

### P0-HARNESS: Corpus v3, replay driver and full-daemon test harness

- **kind:** oracle
- **goal:** Extend tests/contracts/http_corpus.py (schema v2, 16 cases) to v3: HTTP, MCP tool calls through POST /api/mcp/{server_name}/tools/{tool_name} with the operator credential, WS messages and CLI invocations; seeded state; DB-delta assertions (normalized row diffs); side-effect captures (pg_notify channels, WS publishes, files_home writes); per-field normalizers. The recorder runs only against isolated Python daemons built from the worktree (temp state and ports, gobby_test hub) and refuses any other DATABASE_URL. Rust side: one shared test-support crate (replaces the four test-DB env vars); a full-daemon harness (gdaemon plus the Python worker from the worktree on temp ports); and a replay driver that extends crates/gdaemon/tests/http_contracts.rs beyond proxy-only, with per-family proxy, native or compare backends, a differential mode (same case on proxy and native, responses and DB deltas compared), a soak loop (corpus in seeded random order for N hours in Compare mode) and a summary over front-door-compare.jsonl via gdaemon compare-report. Proxy self-replay is the fixture-validity gate. The /api/admin/test/* seeding routes become a test-only harness feature, and their rows are dropped as non-product (D20). Guard: the harness asserts that DATABASE_URL names the isolated test hub (gobby_test at 127.0.0.1:60892) before it sets GOBBY_ALLOW_WORKTREE_DAEMON=1, and gives every harness run its own database, so the worktree-daemon override can never reach the live hub; the e2e harness's existing override (tests/e2e/test_daemon_lifecycle.py:428, test_composer_live_proof.py:159) moves behind the same guard. It starts after #25599 is fixed (start gate). The harness also provides the dormancy proof that every later chunk runs (D37): the full-daemon harness on code defaults replays every existing corpus unchanged, and a test selects another backend only through front_door.routes in its temporary home or a constructor parameter. It also gives the harness a loopback-only network mode for daemons started on restored copies of live data, which every cutover rehearsal uses: outbound connections other than loopback fail, proven by a test in which a fixture daemon's outbound connection to a non-loopback address fails. The map names no egress control that exists in the tree today, so this chunk chooses and proves the mechanism. The waiver match extends with the schema: surface_matches accepts only HTTP surfaces in both loaders today (scripts/parity_waivers.py:123-139; crates/gdaemon/src/front_door/waivers.rs:77-97), so a cited MCP, WS or CLI case would raise a WaiverError, and family plans carry entries on those surfaces. Schema v3 matches each case kind to its exact ledger key (MCP <server>:<tool>, MCP HTTP gobby:<tool>, MCP stdio gobby:<tool>, WS message <type>, CLI gobby <verb>), and the classify rule holds on all four kinds: a cited case asserts its native answer and an uncited one its recording (D84). The guard also accepts a rehearsal stack's gobby_test database on that stack's own port when a rehearsal profile names it (src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/rehearsal.py:211-233), because every cutover rehearsal starts its daemons there; the live hub still fails it. The harness drops each run's database at teardown and, at its start, sweeps any database of its own name pattern whose pid is dead, as tests/fixtures/postgres.py:51-53 and 346-369 do for pytest, because the test hub's data sits on a 3 GB tmpfs (docker-compose.test.yml:26-27) that every chunk session's runs share.

The loopback-only mode adds one case: an outbound connection to a non-loopback address fails. A fixture entry cited by one case of each kind replays as Waived on its native answer and fails on any other, and a citation whose surface differs from its case raises WaiverError on both engines. Inside a spawned session managed SRT fails every non-loopback connection by itself, so the loopback-only case proves nothing there: it carries a control in which the same connection succeeds with the mode off, and it runs through protocol step 6's route, outside the sandbox. A run's database is gone after its teardown, and a database left by a dead pid is swept at the next start.

A static audit of every bundled command_pattern and rule regex for Rust-regex incompatibility (backreferences, lookaround), each with its rewrite or an explicit engine decision. The regex audit covers the 76 lookaround and backreference matches in at least 10 bundled rule files (tool-hygiene/require-uv.yaml and worker-safety/no-force-push.yaml among them): each gets a proposed linear-time rewrite that both engines accept and an equivalence case, and a pattern with no equivalent goes to Josh (D33). No case asserts a bundled rule's behavior: bundled YAML is validated against the engine schema and loader only (Josh's 2026-10-27 ruling on #25256; s2-11 Decision 11), and the regex audit's equivalence cases test a pattern's rewrite on both engines, not a rule. The committed corpus has three layers, each schema-versioned with a manifest, a loader, a coverage check and a README that names the record and replay commands and the re-record obligation when the engine changes (s2-11 1.1, 1.3 and 1.4). Rule-pass cases (tests/contracts/rules/): synthetic definition_json rows with priority and project id, the session facts and pre-pass variables, the normalized event, an ordered script of every seam and external-effect call with its recorded result or failure, the helper family or observer the case exercises, and an expect block holding every HookResponse field _assemble_response fills, the eager variable delta, the staged on_receipt payload, the ordered effect log with the engine's workflow_audit_log and rule_eval metric writes, record_rule_evaluation's audit records and the outcome class (zero_match, matched_allow, mutating or block). The required scenarios are s2-11 1.1's: all 15 RuleEffect types and both delivery classes, ordering, aggregate blocking, the agent-scope, audience and active-rule filters, project scoping, a skipped parse failure, a condition error in a block and in a non-block rule, one failing call per seam kind, the blocking deadline, F4's rewrite recheck, every hardcoded behavior and every response field, one allow, one block and one seam-error case per helper family and per observer, and three event-sequence transitions. The exporter seeds rows through RuleDefinitionManager in the isolated test hub and runs RuleEngine.evaluate with each seam-backed helper, effect executor and direct store call the engine makes (WorkflowAuditManager, MetricsEventStore, CoordinationWaitManager, CompletionSubscriberManager, InterSessionMessageManager and ToolResultStore) wrapped in a pytest recorder, so no production Python changes. Adapter cases (tests/contracts/adapters/): one adapter call per case, a raw provider payload with its delivery origin and the expected HookEvent, or a HookResponse and the expected provider JSON, replayed from tests/fixtures/provider_contracts/ plus synthetic payloads, covering every hook type each of the five adapters accepts and every response field it emits, with node-origin no-file cases for Site rows 20 and 28-30 (s2-11 Site Disposition). Pipeline cases (tests/contracts/pipeline/): HookManager.handle with every collaborator call recorded and the real rule engine, one case per EventHandlers.get_handler_map entry and event type, session start for a new, resumed, cleared and compacted session, a node session missing its row, a deferred activation, a blocking webhook, a rule block that short-circuits the handler and one failing collaborator per collaborator kind. The regex audit also covers the rule files this repository keeps outside the bundled tree (.gobby/workflows/rules/), because they sync to the same rows on every restart (src/gobby/runner_init/storage.py:82): the lookbehind of quiet-hours.yaml:23 gets the same linear-time rewrite and equivalence case (D33, D77). The registry holds a Python defect shown below any one ledger surface, in a vector or in a flow across surfaces; a difference that one case shows on one exact surface takes a docs/contracts/parity-waivers.json entry instead (D84). ### R0: R0: worker boundary and frozen lifecycle contract

- **kind:** runner
- **goal:** #25468 per .gobby/plans/task-25468.md (M1 8877284c44). 1.1: static inventory of every startup job and service owner, identity and error. 1.2: runtime census. 1.3: versioned private worker protocol (handshake; Rust-assigned generation and op IDs; fail-closed auth; a lost reply on an effectful call is an unknown outcome to reconcile, never blind-retry). Protocol changes are additive: HEAD's worker accepts every protocol version that a retained or pinned gdaemon speaks, with a test per version, because a restored gdaemon boots the Python worker from HEAD's checkout; old versions are removed only at S3-DELETE. 1.4: facade over GobbyRunner.create's five phases in a new src/gobby/worker/ package, plus the allow-listed domain-invocation op table (one registration line per op) that later chunks extend for single-owner services. The brief pins runner_lifecycle*.py (10 files, 3,839 lines, run_daemon in runner_lifecycle.py included), not the plan's runner_lifecycle_*.py glob; the needs-planning label is stale (M1 8877284c44), and the brief points at .gobby/plans/task-25468.md. #25582's criterion is met, so R0's session closes it with the review and validation attestations. Its Rust path runs only when gdaemon's compiled runner default is Rust, which CP-RUNNER-CUT's activation commit sets; until then gdaemon starts Python without the worker marker and Python boots its full runner, so this landing replays every existing corpus unchanged. The 65,536-byte request bound of .gobby/plans/task-25468.md (Decision 11) covers the handshake and construction commands. A domain op's request takes the hook route's 16 MiB bound (crates/gdaemon/src/nodes/hooks/ingress.rs:25), because GW-2's preflight and after phase and CHAT-2's lifecycle op carry tool arguments and outputs that exceed 64 KiB (D81, D82); a request over it fails as any failed call does. Domain ops run concurrently on the worker's event loop, so an async op such as HOOK-3's Telegram question, bounded at 110 seconds, holds up no other op and resolves on the loop its pending-interaction manager uses. R0's session also closes #25468 after #25582, because D31's pass at chunk-task creation cannot close a parent whose child stays open. P0-HARNESS need not have landed when this chunk validates. If it has not, protocol step 6's harness and dormancy proof mean crates/gdaemon/tests/http_contracts.rs's proxy replay, the e2e lifecycle tests on their temp-port daemon (tests/e2e/test_daemon_lifecycle.py) and focused pytest of the runner modules, all on code defaults; CP-RUNNER-REVIEW's packet replays this chunk's fixtures on the harness in any case. The op table encodes an op's return value as canonical JSON: a dataclass through dataclasses.asdict with its class name under a _type key, a datetime or Path as its string form, and anything else fails the call as any failed call does. So a one-line registration on a function that returns a plain dataclass, such as read_composer (src/gobby/terminals/composer_ledger.py:585) or send_keys_target_refusal (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/sessions/_terminal_send_keys_gate.py:69-78, 274), needs no shim. The encoder also takes the shapes that registrations return or hold: an Enum as its value, a set or frozenset as a sorted list, and an exception instance returned as a value, such as IndeterminateWrite (src/gobby/terminals/runtime.py:137-142; src/gobby/terminals/write_coordinator.py:629), as its class name under _type plus its attributes. So recipient_policy's RecipientPolicy (src/gobby/agents/team_communications.py:26-28) and WriteCoordinator.write's WriteOutcome (src/gobby/terminals/write_coordinator.py:196-232) also need no shim, and only a shape outside these fails the call. A registration line also names the decode of a parameter JSON cannot carry, a datetime from its ISO string or a dataclass from its fields, as record_composer_local_command's row_at (src/gobby/terminals/composer_ledger.py:649-652), record_queued_submit's consumed_at (src/gobby/hooks/event_handlers/_base.py:236-246) and WriteRequest (src/gobby/terminals/write_coordinator.py:74-94) need. A worker op binds no caller and no daemon-owned execution, so require_machine_owned returns at once (src/gobby/hub/caller_scope.py:54-69) and is_daemon_execution reads false (src/gobby/utils/session_context.py:148-160): a native route makes any caller ownership check before its op call.
- **ledger_selectors:** (none)
- **engines:** runner (runner*.py, runner_init, runner_lifecycle*.py), worker protocol
- **depends_on:** P0-RECORD
- **oracle:** Recorded first: the 1.1 inventory and 1.2 census are committed as fixtures before the facade, and the facade tests replay them. Both fixtures keep every recurring task with its creator, target and cadence, because the chunk that owns #25472 diffs them against its loop list before it lands. The monitors that src/gobby/servers/_app_lifecycle.py starts and the services outside runner_lifecycle*.py appear only in 1.2, and a library's worker thread is recorded under the service that started it. An op that returns a dataclass answers its fields and _type, and an op that returns anything else JSON cannot hold fails as a failed call. An op that returns a frozenset, an Enum or an exception instance answers those forms, and a registered datetime parameter reaches the function as a datetime.
- **size:** M, 2 checkpoints. Python in scope: runner*.py 8,389, runner_init 4,190 and runner_lifecycle*.py 3,839 (read); ~600 new lines in src/gobby/worker/.

### SEAM-FAMILY: Seam: the family contract (routing tier, context, lifecycle API, jobs API, pool, logging, encoder, errors, crate template)

- **kind:** seam
- **goal:** Frozen seam wave contract, part 1 (Josh item 3). One routing tier: the 8 hand-wired FrontDoor::handle surfaces become families, and families can claim WS upgrades, pre-auth and loopback-only routes. FamilyContext carries the broker publisher, lease and backend status, the budgeted pool, the config epoch, a logger and the resolved caller identity. Lifecycle hooks (start, stop, drain, lease-scoped activation) serve R2-R6. The job-registration API shape is implemented by R4. One shared pool budget fixes 4 pools x max 8 against a budget of 8. Routed logging replaces 70 eprintln! calls. One json.dumps-compatible encoder replaces five. DomainError (7 classes) becomes the error envelope. Per-route claims let a family leave routes proxied. The family-crate template and the activation runbook (#24477) ship here, and HealthFamily moves onto the contract. Dormancy is structural (D37): a family's constructor does no work, because RouteTable::new builds every family's router even while it is proxied (crates/gdaemon/src/front_door/routes.rs:89-109); its jobs register only when the family is active, because ActiveServices runs its jobs unconditionally (crates/gdaemon/src/state_services.rs:27-93); and only a checkpoint's activation commit changes its compiled default. Writes the contract section of the project record; gport check-slice freezes the files. FamilyContext's logger comes with the routed telemetry that GW-2, HOOK-3 and OBS name: named counters and histograms in the shape of Python's inc_counter and observe_histogram (src/gobby/telemetry/instruments.py:486, 506), held in one in-process registry with no exporter and no new crate. GW-2 and HOOK-3 publish to it, and OBS's reads merge its values from CP-WAVE1-CUT. Routed logging also keeps the documented log surfaces when S3-DELETE removes Python's (src/gobby/telemetry/logging.py; docs/guides/observability.md:50-92; src/gobby/install/shared/skills/gobby/references/observability/diagnostics.md:19-23). A record goes to exactly one primary file under logging.dir, whose default resolves under the Gobby home (src/gobby/config/logging.py:126-130), by its target's surface: hooks.log, llm.log, mcp.log, automation.log or daemon.log, as classify_log_surface assigns Python's namespaces (src/gobby/telemetry/logging.py:33-59, 91-103). A WARN or higher record also goes to errors.log, except a WARNING carrying the pipeline_guard_refused field (:177-184), and a target that names a CLI's parser goes to that CLI's <cli>-parser-error.log with the message alone (:409-411, 436-464). The writer follows logging.level, logging.format (Python's text line or JSON fields, :321-357, 402-406), logging.dir, logging.max_size_mb, logging.backup_count, logging.llm_max_size_mb and logging.llm_backup_count through the config epoch, because all are live keys that the settings page draws (web/src/components/settings/sections/ObservabilitySection.tsx), on the tracing crates the workspace already locks for gclient (crates/gclient/Cargo.toml:45-46; crates/gclient/src/logging.rs), so no new third-party crate. While gdaemon's compiled backend default starts the Python worker, both processes append to one file, so gdaemon opens each with O_APPEND, reopens when the path's inode changes and leaves rotation to Python's handler. CP-PREDELETE-CUT's commit A flips that default, and from then on gdaemon rotates by size with numbered backups as RotatingFileHandler does, with no edit in that cut. A record before the config is readable, and a panic, still go to stderr, which the launcher captures in runtime.log. Each record counts in logging_records_total{surface,severity} on the routed telemetry (src/gobby/telemetry/health_metrics.py:40-47). FamilyContext also carries one degraded-service set, the successor of runner.degraded_services (src/gobby/runner_init/services.py:59-65), which any family marks by name and OBS's health and status read. A start hook's error takes one of two forms. The ordinary form marks its family's name there and logs, and the daemon keeps serving, as Python does for each optional service (src/gobby/runner_init/cron.py:52; src/gobby/runner_init/orchestration.py:364, 374, 468). The fatal form stops the start with its message and says whether a relaunch could clear the cause, which R2's start form acts on, and a family uses it only where its goal says the failure stops the start. The shared pool budget reads database_concurrency.pool_max_size, coverage_max_concurrency and executor_max_workers through gobby_core::database_concurrency (crates/gcore/src/database_concurrency.rs:106), as src/gobby/runner_init/storage.py:95-107 does, because nothing in gdaemon calls it today and those three restart_required keys would otherwise do nothing once Python's pool is gone.

### R2: R2: initialization and readiness

- **kind:** runner
- **goal:** #25470: Rust sequences the phase calls and exposes startup outcomes; Python constructs domain services only; content refusal happens before publishing; the config initial epoch precedes service construction; HTTP readiness stays distinct from recovery. Owns the startup-progress row. Its Rust path runs only when gdaemon's compiled runner default is Rust, which CP-RUNNER-CUT's activation commit sets; until then gdaemon starts Python without the worker marker and Python boots its full runner, so this landing replays every existing corpus unchanged. The worker's startup_content phase runs five steps in one call (src/gobby/runner_init/storage.py:62-91, 299-314): the bundled sync, the import of landed files, the project skill sync (sync_project_skills, :84; src/gobby/skills/project_sync.py:31), migrate_rule_delivery_dispositions and manager construction. R2 gives that phase's initialize body two optional members, sync_bundled and import_landed, each true when absent, so TPL's and PIPE-1's native steps can replace the first two at their cuts while the other three keep running, and a retained gdaemon that sends neither keeps the whole phase (D83). The bundled step runs today only in dev mode, and with sync_bundled false the phase still sets runner._dev_mode, because manager construction reads it (src/gobby/runner_init/storage.py:73-78, 305). Python's route cannot serve the startup-progress row under the Rust runner: its tracker is created only inside run_daemon (src/gobby/runner_lifecycle.py:154-155), which R0's facade never calls, so it would answer done true at once (src/gobby/servers/routes/admin/_health.py:399-407). So the row registers on SEAM-FAMILY's registry with an exact GET claim, selected by the compiled default that CP-RUNNER-CUT's activation commit flips, as R6's rows are, and the deactivation commit gives it back to Python's route. It answers Python's body from the Rust phase outcomes (src/gobby/runner_lifecycle_startup.py::StartupTracker.to_dict, plus restart_recovery_pending), with no credential (src/gobby/servers/middleware/auth.py:43), and while the worker is still starting. From CP-RUNNER-CUT's activation its Rust path also runs Python's datastore readiness check natively, because only run_daemon calls it (src/gobby/runner_lifecycle.py:212-214; src/gobby/runner_service_readiness.py:27-115): after R6's startup gate and before R3's other pre-spawn steps and the worker spawn, as Python runs the gate and then this check (src/gobby/runner_lifecycle.py:183, 212), it requires PostgreSQL, Qdrant and FalkorDB through gcore's postgres, qdrant and falkor modules and its config resolvers (crates/gcore/src/config/resolve.rs:169, 182), with Python's 30-second deadline, 1-second retry, messages and test_mode skip, and a failure ends the start with Python's message as a failed step. R2 also builds gdaemon serve's no-worker start form on a hub, behind gdaemon's compiled backend default and dormant while that default starts the worker, so CP-PREDELETE-CUT's commit A activates it with no code of its own. Nothing else would apply or verify the schema from then on: Python's gobby start applies it under the singleton (src/gobby/cli/daemon_start.py:266; src/gobby/cli/utils_config.py:92-108), the runner verifies it (src/gobby/runner.py:457) and construction applies it with retries (src/gobby/runner_init/helpers.py:27, 107, 141-162), all in Python, while gclient opens no datastore connection (D69) and R6's restart re-executes gdaemon with no client in between. So under the singleton serve already holds (crates/gdaemon/src/lifecycle/pid_file.rs:50-94) and before any door admits, this form connects with Python's startup retry delays, runs SchemaRunner's apply and then verify_database_identity (crates/gdaemon/src/main.rs:172, 276-297), in that order because verify refuses a pending migration, and upserts the _personal row (src/gobby/storage/projects.py:135-166) through a gobby-core function that V1B's gdaemon content-sync also calls. It then runs the three identity steps that init_storage runs at each start and nothing else would from commit A (src/gobby/runner_init/storage.py:203-211), through gobby-core functions that V1B's install identity and local API key steps also call: the machine row's upsert under the sole user, which refreshes the row and allocates its node ref (src/gobby/runner_init/helpers.py:126-138; src/gobby/storage/machines.py:115-150); the local API key's adoption, whose failure logs and the start continues (src/gobby/storage/api_keys.py:129-174); and ensure_system_session, which creates the root session that a cron session's parent and a system send name, and which AG-3's send also calls (src/gobby/storage/sessions/_constants.py:137-206; src/gobby/scheduler/executor.py:325; src/gobby/sessions/mailbox.py:268-269). It records this work as the startup-progress row's hub step, which V1A's gobby start prints. R6's gate, the readiness check and R3's other pre-spawn steps then run in that order, then R2's content phase with TPL's native sync and PIPE-1's native import, then the family start hooks, and only then do the doors admit, so a hook that must come before admission, as A1-CONFIG's first publish does, can. A hook with slow work runs it on its own task. A schema refusal, which StartRefusal makes exit 78 for a worker today (src/gobby/runner.py:457-459, 649-651), takes that exit's sticky state with no worker: gdaemon sets BackendStatus::Refused with the refusal text, starts no services, holds no database ownership and stays up (crates/gdaemon/src/lifecycle/backend.rs:318-327; crates/gdaemon/src/state.rs:245-253), because launchd and systemd would relaunch a failed exit (src/gobby/install/shared/services/com.gobby.daemon.plist.j2:38-46; src/gobby/install/shared/services/gobby-daemon.service.j2:20-23). The doors then open in that state, the front door answers 503 backend_refused on every row (crates/gdaemon/src/front_door/mod.rs:202-227), gobby start's poll prints the reason (src/gobby/cli/daemon_start.py:236-248), and only a full restart retries. A hub with no sole user takes the same state with Python's message, run gobby install to repair identity (src/gobby/storage/users.py:125-132). A connection that still fails after the retry delays ends the start nonzero, so the service manager relaunches it. A start hook's fatal error takes that state when a relaunch could not clear its cause, and that exit when one could (SEAM-FAMILY). SCHEMA-WINDOW's rule still covers a hub ahead, and CP-FINAL-CUT's drops and every later migration apply at the start they ship in. A family's start hook may also record a named step and its outcome on the startup-progress row, as Python's tracker does (src/gobby/runner_lifecycle_startup.py::StartupTracker). Between the config phase's initial epoch and service construction, Python now installs agent_build.build_root, and an invalid root raises StartRefusal (src/gobby/runner.py:304-309; src/gobby/agents/build_root.py:24-35; 0892e316b4), which ends the worker with exit 78 as the schema refusal does (src/gobby/runner.py:457-459, 650-652). ### R3: R3: ordered recovery

- **kind:** runner
- **goal:** #25471: Rust drives a durable, resumable recovery order (hook barrier; sessions, handoffs and wakes; agents and pipelines), and Python performs the domain transactions. Native families register their recovery steps in the same order. No replay or cron runs before its prerequisites, and retained backlog never blocks listener readiness. Its Rust path runs only when gdaemon's compiled runner default is Rust, which CP-RUNNER-CUT's activation commit sets; until then gdaemon starts Python without the worker marker and Python boots its full runner, so this landing replays every existing corpus unchanged. One recovery step runs inside a construction phase today: memory's interrupted dream-run reconcile in init_orchestration (src/gobby/runner_init/orchestration.py:554-567). In worker mode init_orchestration skips it, as Python's loops do not start in worker mode (R4), and R3's order calls it as a worker recovery entry point before any cron or dream admission. At CP-WAVE3-CUT MEM-3's native reconcile takes that slot and the Rust side stops calling the entry point (D4), because a Python worker start that still ran it would mark a live native dream run interrupted (memory 7.3). Its recovery order carries the hook barrier's outcome between steps, which Python holds in one local today (src/gobby/runner_lifecycle_subsystems.py:672-683). The barrier step has two entry points: the drain (drain_hook_inbox_barrier, src/gobby/runner_hook_replay.py:39-46) and the classification that follows it (:47-164), which takes the drain's result fields as input, writes reconciliation_pending on each unresolved active run (the fence the agent-run step reads, src/gobby/runner_lifecycle_agents.py:293-328) and returns the outcome. The session reconciliation step (src/gobby/events/wake.py:194-214) takes that outcome's excluded session ids and recovery-safe flag as arguments. So HOOK-3's native startup pass replaces only the drain entry point at CP-WAVE4-CUT, with no further Python edit, and AG-WAIT's native recovery takes the classification and the steps that consume it at CP-WAVE5-CUT (s2-11 D2.1). The lifecycle monitor's reclassification of fenced runs runs the same barrier and then the agent-run step for its fenced run ids (src/gobby/runner_lifecycle_reconcile.py:443-483), so whichever side runs its iteration calls these entry points until the same activations replace them. The feedback review store's orphaned-run mark in init_cron, which init_orchestration calls (src/gobby/runner_init/cron.py:195; src/gobby/runner_init/orchestration.py:552; src/gobby/feedback/storage.py:333) moves as that reconcile does: a worker recovery entry point runs it, and at CP-WAVE5-CUT AG-WAIT's native mark takes that slot, because a Python worker start that still ran it would mark a live native review interrupted. A native step may declare itself pre-spawn, which R3 runs before gdaemon spawns the worker for that start or respawn, so no Python request can race it, or once per process, which a backend respawn skips, because native work outlives the worker. Every other step runs at each whole start and each respawn. Three native owners take slots this way: AG-2's sandbox pass in the sandbox_reaping slot (src/gobby/runner_lifecycle_subsystems.py:715) from CP-WAVE2-CUT; CHAT-2's pending-interaction expire pass, pre-spawn, from CP-WAVE3-CUT; and PIPE-2's hub-only, once-per-process recovery in the pipeline_recovery slot (:750) from CP-WAVE4-CUT. Admission runs after the front door's authenticate and before any other check or effect, in this order. (1) A bearer that starts with gobby-agent-v1., read as the front door's authenticate reads it (a case-insensitive scheme and a trimmed token, crates/gdaemon/src/front_door/auth.rs:129-142), is refused by presence, unverified, even with a valid break-glass header: restart and shutdown answer 403 with Python's managed_activation_refused detail (src/gobby/servers/routes/admin/_lifecycle.py:99-112; tests/servers/routes/admin/test_managed_activation_refusal.py), and lease handoff answers Python's 401 route_not_permitted, because only the other two are in Python's agent matrix (src/gobby/servers/auth_service.py:145-147). (2) A resolved API key (x-gobby-key-id, crates/gdaemon/src/front_door/auth.rs:125-163) is an operator. (3) A loopback peer whose X-Gobby-Break-Glass header matches the break_glass file is an operator, through a constant-time verifier that this chunk adds to gobby-core (src/gobby/servers/auth_service.py:498-507; src/gobby/utils/break_glass.py:89-94) and SES-2 reuses. (4) A gobby_session cookie with the browser-testing. prefix is refused with 403 browser_authority_refused, whether or not it is live. This check comes before step 5 because GET /api/auth/status answers true for a live one (src/gobby/servers/browser_sessions.py:81-87; src/gobby/servers/auth_service.py:287-304). (5) Any other gobby_session cookie goes to a one-method cookie port. Its interim adapter sends Python's existing GET /api/auth/status to the worker with only that cookie (src/gobby/servers/routes/auth.py:194-198): true admits, false answers Python's 401 session_invalid body, and an unreachable worker, any other answer or a 5-second deadline answers the typed 503 and admits nothing. No second verifier is written (D3). AUTH binds the port to SEAM-CALLERS' verifier and these POST rows to its shared CORS layer (#24964) in CP-WAVE1-CUT's activation commit, and S3-DELETE removes the adapter. (6) Anything else answers 401 missing_auth with Python's body (src/gobby/servers/middleware/auth.py:77-187). Each handler then keeps Python's order, parameters, status values and bodies (src/gobby/servers/routes/admin/_lifecycle.py:128-338). Restart answers already_restarting from the moment another restart takes this gate until that restart's stop closes admission. Until CP-WAVE1-CUT the handler reads them from Python's existing GET /api/admin/cron/protected-runs with the admitted caller's own credentials, because only Python's scheduler holds its owner id (src/gobby/scheduler/scheduler.py:73, 120-130), and any answer but a 200, or a 5-second deadline, answers the typed 503 and stops nothing. R0's facade never calls run_daemon, so the startup predecessor gate (src/gobby/runner_gate.py; src/gobby/runner_lifecycle.py:183) is this chunk's from CP-RUNNER-CUT's activation, as the first pre-spawn step in R3's order on a hub: it takes the terminal fence exclusively, terminates every backend under the hub lifecycle prefix outside this start's own application-name family (src/gobby/runner_gate.py:47-72) and verifies each gone, within Python's 60-second deadline, and a failure ends the start as Python's exit 1 does. The fence key is deployment_advisory_key("agent-terminal-transition") (src/gobby/storage/agents/_lifecycle.py:31-33), in a gobby-core helper that AG-2's native terminal transitions take shared. On the Rust proof, with the op unregistered in the test, a mixed installed set, a refused schema plan or preflight and a failed SRT verify with a sandbox on each answer 409 start_refused with Python's message and stop nothing, force included, and a proof past its bound does the same. ### SCHEMA-WINDOW: Expand window: retained generations start on a hub ahead by expand-only receipts

- **kind:** runner
- **goal:** Ships dormant before CP-RUNNER-REVIEW and goes live at CP-RUNNER-CUT, so that every retained generation from then on starts on a hub that is ahead by expand-only receipts (D22). (1) A destructive migration's filename ends in _destructive.sql, and the file carries the -- gobby:destructive directive. That directive was retired as an inert comment (decision 14 of .gobby/plans/completed/memory-access-semantics.md; crates/gcore/src/schema/runner_tests.rs, directive_marked_migration_executes_on_fresh_lineage), keeping only the non-transactional check at crates/gcore/src/schema/runner_plan.rs:281-288, and 421, 427, 439, 450, 451, 454, 455, 462 and 472 drop objects without it; only 426 carries it. This chunk revives it as a classification label with execution unchanged, as ruling 19 directs. The test floor is the highest migration number in the directory when this chunk lands. For every migration above the floor, a test enforces the directive and filename pairing in both directions, and a content lint requires both for any statement outside D22's expand set, statements built inside DO blocks with EXECUTE format(...) included: DROP, RENAME, ALTER COLUMN ... TYPE, SET NOT NULL, DROP DEFAULT, ADD CONSTRAINT on an existing table, a unique index on an existing table, ADD COLUMN ... NOT NULL without a DEFAULT, DELETE, TRUNCATE, an UPDATE of a column that existed before the file, a REVOKE on an object that existed before the file, CREATE OR REPLACE of an existing function or trigger, and any statement the lint cannot classify. A GRANT or REVOKE on an object that the same file creates needs no marker of its own, because the repository's migrations revoke PUBLIC's privileges on each new table in the file that creates it (crates/gcore/assets/schema/migrations/470_validation_run_records.sql:26-29; crates/gcore/tests/catalog_manifest_freshness.rs:639-646 asserts that table has no PUBLIC grant). Files at or below the floor keep their names and bytes, 426_retire_legacy_wiki.sql included, because resolve_pending_migrations and verify_receipts match each receipt's filename and checksum exactly ('receipt mismatch for schema asset v{version}'; crates/gcore/src/schema/runner_plan.rs:231-291; crates/gcore/src/schema/verify.rs:468-527) and an applied migration is never edited (D22); the window judges only receipts above the code head, so their names never decide a rollback. (2) Every gate accepts a hub head newer than the code head when each receipt above the code head has a non-destructive filename and each receipt at or below it matches the embedded assets as today; a destructive receipt above the head still refuses and names its version and filename. schema_migrations already stores (version, filename, checksum) (crates/gcore/src/schema/runner.rs:329; resolve_pending_migrations in crates/gcore/src/schema/runner_plan.rs), so no new column is needed. (3) The runner never applies or repairs a receipt above its own head. (4) The chunk inventories every gate that compares a hub head with a binary, a pin or a checkout, citing each from code: gdaemon's identity check, verify_database_identity (crates/gdaemon/src/main.rs:276-297), with its version comparison (main.rs:286-291) and the exact SchemaRunner::verify call after it (main.rs:292-296), which every Python start runs through gdaemon schema verify (src/gobby/runner.py:456-459; src/gobby/storage/schema_contract.py:236-239), as sweep-test-schemas does (main.rs:166); validate_lineage (crates/gcore/src/schema/runner_plan.rs:153-169); resolve_pending_migrations ('receipt v{version} has no matching embedded schema asset'); the Python hub-ahead check (src/gobby/storage/schema_divergence.py:267-274, 'live hub schema v{live} is newer than this checkout') with its four callers (src/gobby/cli/daemon_lifecycle.py:499, src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/cli.py:232, src/gobby/cli/pack.py:368 and src/gobby/servers/routes/admin/_lifecycle.py:94); the cutover preflight (src/gobby/cli/daemon_preflight.py:119-137; src/gobby/cli/cutover.py); GEN-ROLLBACK's restore preflight, which compares the retained gdaemon with its own stamp and never with the checkout pin; and any other the inventory finds, among them every gate that R2's Rust startup adds. Under the window, verify_receipts (crates/gcore/src/schema/verify.rs:468-527) accepts exactly the receipts above the head that the predicate accepts, and verify_schema (verify.rs:175-198) still requires every catalog-manifest entry to be present and equal, accepts catalog entries absent from the manifest only while such a receipt exists, and checks seed rows as today. gdaemon schema apply, which the start also runs (src/gobby/storage/hub/postgres.py:407), reaches only validate_lineage and the pending-migration plan (crates/gcore/src/schema/runner.rs:108-124). The installed-identity check (src/gobby/storage/schema_divergence.py:251-265, via src/gobby/cli/daemon_preflight.py:68-78) stays exact: a checkout pin that differs from the installed generation's identity still refuses, which is why schema inputs land only in a cut's step 6 (D22). The rollback path it makes true: after a cut applies an expand migration, restoring the pinned generation (GEN-ROLLBACK's restore) plus the deactivation commit starts and serves with no database restore. The deactivation commit reverts the cut's schema inputs together with its activation, so the checkout's schema identity matches the restored generation and only the hub is ahead, which the window covers; a later cut re-lands the same migration file in its step 6 (the retry after Josh's reassessment, or the next cut that needs it), byte for byte and under its number, whose receipt then matches. Its Rust is dormant until promotion. Its Python preflight edit is in a checkpoint-only module (src/gobby/storage/schema_divergence.py, reached through src/gobby/cli/daemon_preflight.py only at restart, cutover, hub-backup and pack), so it forms one prepared commit on the append-only branch port/prepared/SCHEMA-WINDOW, reviewed with the chunk and recorded by SHA at its close, which CP-RUNNER-CUT lands in its step 6, before its activation commit. The chunk changes no schema-identity input: no migration, no rename or edit of an existing asset (426_retire_legacy_wiki.sql keeps its name and bytes), no baseline, catalog or seed manifest change, and RUNNER_PROTOCOL_VERSION stays 1 (crates/gcore/src/schema/assets.rs:3, 584-600). So CP-RUNNER-CUT's activated build keeps its pinned generation's identity, its gdaemon-alone restore passes the partial-promotion check, and its rollback target never meets a newer hub: CP-RUNNER-CUT carries no schema step.

### CP-RUNNER-REVIEW: Checkpoint review: the Rust runner

- **kind:** checkpoint
- **goal:** Review pause before the Rust runner goes live. Ruling 14 names 'after we port the daemon runner' as the first checkpoint, and ruling 16 makes its cutover a one-way switchover with three outcomes. Packet: R0-R6 landed and validated on the full-daemon harness with the Rust runner: R0's lifecycle fixtures, R3's crash-point corpus, R4's fake-clock corpus and R6's shutdown-ordering corpus, plus the restart, shutdown and lease-handoff cases; the dormancy proof, in which the same harness on code defaults replays every existing corpus unchanged (D37); SEAM-FAMILY's lifecycle and job contracts that R2-R6 implement; SCHEMA-WINDOW's schema-gate tests and Python preflight test, with its prepared commit's SHA; each prepared commit and each pick that carries a schema input, listed as deferred to the next cut that lands schema inputs, because CP-RUNNER-CUT lands none (D40 item 3); GEN-ROLLBACK's isolated rehearsal and, unless Josh refused it at map approval (D38), its live drill; and the three outcomes, stating that the first or second retires the Python runner for the rest of the build (R-RETIRE), so nothing can fall back to it afterwards. On no-go, after the de-escalation, send one project send_message with wake=true naming the in-flight gateway and pilot chunks (PROJ-1, SEAM-CALLERS, SEAM-WS, GW-1, GW-2, A1-RUNTIME, A1-CONFIG, A1-SECRETS, B0-READ, B0-WRITE and B0-CLOSE): they stop at their next checkpoint and land nothing until the fixes Josh names close. When those fixes close, the session Josh opens for this review sends a second one that releases them, before it builds its new packet. R4's diff of R0's fixtures against its loop list, and R4's fake-clock case for each op on the list. R6's three rows go Native at this cut (D68), so the packet lists each admission case, the presence refusal of an agent bearer, the cookie check through Python's status route, the guard cases against Python's staging and the security review's record. R2's startup-progress row goes Native with R6's rows at this cut, so the packet also lists gobby start's poll against the native row. Before writing the packet, this review's unspawned session proves the hub rehearsal profile on a real stack, because its tests fake Docker (tests/cli/test_hub_backup_rehearsal.py:43-69), no commit since #21868 (2026-09-05) records a real run, and a failure first met at CP-RUNNER-CUT's step 5 would sit under that cut's landing freeze: it builds a fresh stack and isolated home as that step says in docs/port/map-v2.md, restores P's newest verified hub-backup (GEN-ROLLBACK's drill's or, if Josh refused that drill, the backup that start gate item 18 takes) through GOBBY_HUB_REHEARSAL_PROFILE, reads one row back with docker exec and psql on the stack's PostgreSQL container, starts no daemon on it, and removes the stack and its volumes. The packet names the result and the restore's elapsed time, which sizes step 5 in the window plan; a failure is a no-go fix. Every packet opens with a summary of at most one screen: what changed since the previous review, what needs Josh's call, and any check that did not pass. Every packet also carries the cutover plan for CP-RUNNER-CUT: the window length and the named triggers; the trigger table, which gives each trigger its default outcome (2 or 3) and who decides; the fix-forward bound (at most two fix cycles, the last fix landing within 24 hours of the first outcome-2 decision, each followed by its own clean window, then outcome 3), which Josh may change in his go; the pinned generation (the one installed when the cutover sets its hold) and the restore members; the recipe; and the loss window: the writes made after the backup, through the rehearsal and the window, which only a backup restore would lose (a drop, or CP-WAVE3-CUT's relocation once it ran; an expand-only rollback loses none, D22), plus every live agent seat's credentials if the recipe restores the backup. It lists, by SHA, every prepared commit that the cutover lands in its step 6 (each schema-carrying chunk's commit on port/prepared/<chunk id>, each dependent chunk's schema-test commit and each post-TPL template commit), and the pending fixes (D40 item 3: none while ruling 24 stands), each with a proposed disposition: pick; skipped; ported by <chunk id>; or dropped, with its reason. A pick that carries a schema input, a gcode or ghook version or a template is a prepared commit too. Josh's go approves both lists. It also lists, by SHA, every chunk candidate landed since the previous review, each with its code-reviewer attestation and, where protocol step 7 required one, its security-review attestation. It lists every irreversible step that needs Josh's explicit go, every drop the cutover carries among them; an expand step is not one, because the restore plus the deactivation commit undoes it (D22). Until Josh has given one, it also asks for a standing ruling on an emergency rollback restart during quiet hours, proposing this default: a health or start proof failure, data loss or a schema verify failure rolls back at once, after the protected-runs read and with its global send_message, and any other outcome-3 trigger waits for quiet hours to end, with the hold and the pin extended. At once means the binary restore, because the project's quiet-hours rule refuses gobby stop and gobby cutover in every hooked session and lets gobby rollback restore through (.gobby/workflows/rules/quiet-hours.yaml:15-24), so the deactivation build's promotion waits for them to end, and so does a backup restore unless Josh runs its gobby stop from his own shell. The packet also lists by waiver id every docs/contracts/parity-waivers.json entry and case citation that the cut's activation commit lands, as planned changes and not as mismatches, because until then the chunks' replays read fixture copies and a live Compare record never cites a waiver (D84). It also names, for the workflow named CI, for .github/workflows/rust-ci.yml and for the workflow named Release Branch CI (.github/workflows/postgres-pgsearch-smoke.yml), the newest run on 0.9.0 that ran to a result, with its commit and result; a run that a later push cancelled has no result. The first two must be green (D34). The third is advisory, but a red run is found work fixed before the cut, and when it has no such run since the previous review, this review starts one through workflow_dispatch and names its result, or names it superseded if a later push cancels it (D85). Before writing the packet, fetch origin and list the pending fixes as D40 item 3 defines them, which is none while ruling 24 stands; the review commits nothing, and its cutover cherry-picks and lands the picks that Josh approves. Category manual: escalate_task, then de_escalate_task after Josh's go, then close_task. Record the packet as a review-packet attestation and keep it out of the checkout. Call escalate_task(reason='needs_human: go or no-go for CP-RUNNER; packet in attestation <id>'), present the packet and the question in the final message, and end the turn. Josh answers in that terminal. If that session is gone, he answers in any later default session, or with gobby tasks de-escalate, or in the web UI. On go: de_escalate_task(reason='GO from Josh <timestamp>: <his words>'), claim_task, an approved implementation attestation quoting him, then close_task(reason='done', preview=true) and the same call without preview, with no commit; the final message then asks Josh to prompt the port dispatcher, because a review's close does not wake it (D116). On no-go: de_escalate_task(reason='NO-GO from Josh ...: <his words>'). Keep the task open. Link the fixes Josh names with add_dependency(task_id=<review>, depends_on=<fix>). File any new filing as a child of #21542, so the port dispatcher starts it, and label it operator-directed, which the found-work gate exempts (src/gobby/install/shared/workflows/rules/stop-gates/enforce-found-work-ladder.yaml:67). A no-go holds no claim, because escalate_task released it, so this session ends its turn with the task open and its blockers linked, and its final message asks Josh to prompt the port dispatcher, which starts the fixes (D116). When they close, the task shows ready again, the dispatcher names it in its final message, and Josh prompts this session or opens a new one, which claims it, builds a new packet and escalates again. Never close a no-go. If Josh abandons the direction, re-plan the downstream edges before any wont_do close, because that close releases them too.

### CP-RUNNER-CUT: Checkpoint cutover: the Rust runner goes live

- **kind:** cutover
- **goal:** Category code: this task owns the activation commit, which gets the code-reviewer seat, with the deactivation commit, before the hold is set (step 3). Run the schema-identity comparison that ends step 3 as soon as that seat passes and before setting the hold, so that a difference stops this cut before anything is held, pinned, frozen or landed. Ruling 16: a one-way switchover with three outcomes. #25475, R7's runner landing, is this chunk's activation commit. (1) Announcement: Send one global send_message before anything else. It names the checkpoint, the backup's daemon restart, the activation restart, the window and its triggers, the landing freeze and the loss window (the writes made after the backup, through the rehearsal and the window, which a backup restore would lose). It also tells every session how to wait: a session ready to land during the freeze sends this session a direct message, then registers wait_for_coordination(owner_session=<this session>, reply=true, timeout=3600) and registers it again after every timeout and every prompt (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/coordination.py:52-59); this session messages each of them when the freeze clears. The announcement also names the window's two deliberate restarts: a plain gobby restart and one gobby restart --full. (2) Restart timing: Read project_policy.quiet_hours live at that moment, never from a brief, and start only when the backup, the rehearsal and the whole window, at their planned lengths, end before the next quiet hours. (7) Observation window: Hold it in this session with a provider background watch that samples the triggers into a log, plus wait_for_coordination on that watch, registered again every 3,600 seconds or less, after every timeout wake and after every prompt; after a compaction, fetch the wait tool's schema again first (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/coordination.py:42). The window ends before the next quiet hours. Length and named rollback triggers: from the restart until the next quiet hours begin, and at least 8 hours. It includes a deliberate plain gobby restart (a backend respawn under the Rust runner), one gobby restart --full, one run of every periodic job class and a refused stop during a restart-protected cron run. Triggers: health or start proof failure; an error rate above the baseline recorded in the window plan; a recovery step out of order, or one that blocks listener readiness; a periodic job lost, run twice or fired by both schedulers; a restart or shutdown over the child budget; terminal processes lost across a plain restart; a spawn or terminal attach failure; a schema verify failure. Job triggers: an op on R4's loop list that misses its cadence or errors on every fire, or a recurring task the rerun of R0's runtime census finds that the list does not name. A 24-hour op that has not come due inside the window is recorded as pending for the next cut's window. The window also drives R6's native rows: the web UI's restart command with a session cookie; an agent bearer on restart, shutdown and lease handoff, refused with the daemon still running; and a restart refused for a pending handoff. Further triggers: an agent bearer that reaches a stop; a live session cookie refused, or a dead or browser-testing cookie admitted; a stop or restart that proceeds past a pending handoff or a protected run without force. Restoring its gdaemon drops the worker marker, so the Python child boots its full runner, which is still in the checkout because R-RETIRE has not landed. The restore members are gdaemon alone. The deactivation commit flips the runner default back. This cutover carries no schema step: its pinned generation predates SCHEMA-WINDOW and could not start on an expanded hub (D22). So it lands no schema input: SCHEMA-WINDOW's prepared commit carries only its Python preflight edit and that edit's preflight test, and any prepared commit or pick that carries a schema input waits for the next cut that lands schema inputs; the review packet lists each one as deferred. The deactivation commit also reverts SCHEMA-WINDOW's prepared commit.

- **depends_on:** CP-RUNNER-REVIEW

- **decision_refs:** D37, D38, D22, D4, D39, D40, D65, D48, D68, D96, D115, D118, D1, D23, D34, D85, D116

Step 6 lands SCHEMA-WINDOW's prepared commit just before the activation commit, which also bumps gcode and ghook (D39). The same compiled default claims R6's three POST rows (D68). It also claims R2's GET /api/admin/startup-progress row.

A first or second outcome makes the switch one-way for the rest of the build (ruling 16). An emergency rollback during quiet hours needs the standing ruling the review asked for.

### R-RETIRE: Retire the Python runner launch path

- **kind:** retire
- **goal:** Ruling 16. It starts only after CP-RUNNER-CUT closes with outcome 1, or with outcome 2 once fix-forward is done, and it closes the runner epic #25467. Remove gdaemon's legacy spawn branch, the one that starts Python without the worker marker, so that gdaemon always boots Python as a worker under the Rust runner. Python's full-runner boot without the marker now refuses with exit 78, the existing sticky refusal (backend.rs:318-326), so a stale launcher cannot start the old runner. GOBBY_BACKEND_COMMAND and the plist keep -m gobby.runner (plist.j2:23-24), which now always boots the worker. CP-RUNNER-CUT's close already burned the gdaemon version of every generation promoted before its activation, so restore refuses them. This chunk makes that refusal structural: GEN-ROLLBACK's restore also refuses any generation whose manifest predates CP-RUNNER-CUT's activation, and a Python full-runner boot without the marker refuses, so every later rollback target is a Rust-runner generation. Python's runner orchestration modules stay in the checkout, unreachable, until S3-DELETE (D14). A manifest predates that activation when its source commit does not contain the port/CP-RUNNER-CUT tag's commit (git merge-base --is-ancestor), the last commit the cut promoted, which also refuses a window generation that an outcome-2 fix replaced, and which holds on machine A too once it has adopted that tag (D40 item 4). A missing tag or an unknown source commit fails closed, and restore refuses.
- **ledger_selectors:** (none)
- **engines:** Python runner launch path removal
- **depends_on:** CP-RUNNER-CUT
- **oracle:** CP-RUNNER-CUT's window evidence; R0's lifecycle fixtures replayed against the worker-only boot; a case that boots Python without the marker and asserts exit 78 and gdaemon's sticky Refused state. Restore refuses a generation whose manifest's source commit does not contain the port/CP-RUNNER-CUT tag's commit, with no tag, and with an unknown source commit, and admits one that contains it.
- **size:** S, 1 checkpoint. Python in scope: runner.py main and the launcher argv (~0.3K edits); Rust: ~0.3K removed from gdaemon lifecycle.
- **decision_refs:** D4, D37, D38, D14, D40
- **seam_gaps:** (none)
- **tree_nodes:** #25467
- **python_edits:** Runner class: Python's full-runner boot refuses without the worker marker (exit 78), and GEN-ROLLBACK's restore refuses any generation whose manifest predates CP-RUNNER-CUT's activation. It is live at landing for any process that starts Python directly; gdaemon always passes the marker after CP-RUNNER-CUT.
- **registration:** gdaemon lifecycle/ backend spawn only; no serve.rs slot.
- **risks:** The Windows direct path launches Python itself (daemon_start.py:290-295; serve.rs:358-363) and stops working; Windows stays post-1.0 (83a9445f). End-to-end tests that boot Python directly must pass the marker. After this lands, no rollback can return to the Python runner, by design (ruling 16).

PROJ-1 also lands the one project metadata guard that every native reader of project.json policy outside gprojects uses (D63): crates/gcore/src/project_metadata.rs opens the sidecar .gobby/.project.json.lock as Projects plan 4.5a specifies, takes its exclusive flock within at most two seconds, checks .gobby/.project-update-recovery/ under the lock, and returns the committed object, absent metadata, or a distinct refusal for malformed or non-object metadata, an unreadable file, a lock deadline or pending evidence. It has no default: with no journal it only takes the flock that Python's project initialization already takes.

### SEAM-WS: Seam: WS handler registry and in-process publish

- **kind:** seam
- **goal:** Frozen seam wave contract, part 3: families claim WS message types through a handler registry; FamilyContext gets an in-process publish handle, so the broker stops being private; unclaimed message types are forwarded to Python over the existing bridge. Owns the WS transports and subscribe and unsubscribe (already delegated) and ping. A claim takes effect only while its family's backend is Native, so a dormant family's types keep reaching Python (D37). The publish handle carries both operations Python's publisher sends: a filtered publish and a server-side subscribe for one connection (docs/contracts/native-ws-transport.md, Publish; src/gobby/servers/websocket/native_bridge.py:250-261), which TERM-2 and CHAT-2 use. The contract also carries what Python's connection handler does outside its message table (src/gobby/servers/websocket/server.py:357-445). Each claimed handler receives the connection's id and its SEAM-CALLERS Admitted value (#25046), taken at the upgrade on a connection with a private leg as on one without (crates/gdaemon/src/front_door/mod.rs:241-261), because the bridge's ready frame carries only admitted and confined (crates/gdaemon/src/websocket/transport.rs:115-128). The registry dispatch holds the confinement gate, because a claimed frame no longer reaches Python's: on a confined connection a frame whose type is off Python's allow-list, or whose project or session selector at any depth differs from the signed claims, answers Browser message refused and reaches no handler (src/gobby/servers/websocket/server.py:499-513; src/gobby/servers/browser_sessions.py:90-124). A claim declares whether its handler runs on the read loop, as src/gobby/servers/websocket/message_classes.py:18-55 classifies Python's: an on-loop handler finishes before the connection's next frame is read, and a disconnect cancels the connection's off-loop handlers (src/gobby/servers/websocket/server.py:436). A connect event runs once the welcome frame has reached the socket, and a disconnect event runs exactly once when the socket closes or a send fails, on a connection with a private leg as on one without. TERM-1's attachment finalization, CHAT-2's reconnect rebroadcast and VOICE's attached-session speech cleanup bind those events, so no family edits the frozen transport for them. This chunk also builds the leg-free connect path (D102), dormant behind one compiled default that CP-WAVE5-CUT's activation commit flips. Today NativeWs::accept refuses without Python's binding and opens one private leg per connection, and Python's end of that leg admits the client, sends the welcome and answers ping (crates/gdaemon/src/websocket/transport.rs:237-255, 452-465; src/gobby/servers/websocket/native_bridge.py:216-236), so without this path every WebSocket client is refused from CP-PREDELETE-CUT's commit A, when no worker exists. With the default on, accept needs no binding and opens no leg, and a connection stays open when the worker exits; shutdown still closes it with 1001. Its bounds come from a constructor parameter holding what Python's bind sends: the configured ping interval and timeout, and WebSocketConfig's 5 MiB message limit (src/gobby/servers/websocket/native_publish.py:177-183; src/gobby/runner_init/servers.py:306-312; src/gobby/servers/websocket/models.py:40-42). That activation commit fills it in serve.rs from the DaemonConfig that A1-CONFIG moves to gcore::config, and websocket.enabled false keeps today's no-binding refusal. Admission runs after the front door's authenticate, on SEAM-CALLERS' verified-admission type, with the answers of each entry's Python owner (src/gobby/servers/websocket/native_bridge.py:159-177): a direct refusal keeps its status and body (src/gobby/servers/websocket/auth.py:27-90), and a browser refusal keeps 101 then close 4401 (src/gobby/servers/auth_service.py:287-311). The first frame is the welcome, with Python's fields in Python's wire format (src/gobby/servers/websocket/server.py:393-405): a new client_id, user_id as Python's adapter sets it (src/gobby/servers/websocket/native_bridge.py:209; src/gobby/servers/websocket/auth.py:79-80), latency 0.0 (src/gobby/servers/websocket/asgi_adapter.py:19) and conversation_ids through a one-method port with an empty default, which CHAT-2's runtime implements. Dispatch keeps what crates/gdaemon/src/websocket/subscriptions.rs already answers (subscribe, unsubscribe and the parse refusals) and adds the confinement gate, the claimed handlers, ping, and Unknown message type for anything else (src/gobby/servers/websocket/server.py:589-591). A handler failure answers Internal server error (src/gobby/servers/websocket/server.py:422-424). ping answers {"type": "pong", "latency": 0.0} (src/gobby/servers/websocket/handlers/core.py:164-171). Until the flip ping stays forwarded, so nothing changes before CP-WAVE5-CUT. A binary frame takes the same dispatch, as Python's json.loads reads it. This chunk documents the form in docs/contracts/native-ws-transport.md, and S3-DELETE removes the legged form.
- **ledger_selectors:** ^WS transport /ws(/\{path:path\})?$, ^WS message (subscribe|unsubscribe|ping)$
- **engines:** WS server dispatch
- **depends_on:** SEAM-FAMILY, SEAM-CALLERS
- **oracle:** Existing: ws_envelope_golden, terminal_ws_golden and the delegated rows' tests. Recorded first in this chunk from Python, through P0-HARNESS's WS case kind with the entry and the connecting credential as case inputs: ping's answer; the welcome on each entry, with client_id and the generated user_id normalized; the admission matrix on both entries (no credential, a wrong scheme, an invalid token, an API key, a live and an expired cookie, a live browser-testing cookie and an agent token), with each direct status and body and each browser close; and the frames for an unknown type, a confined session's refused type and a mismatched selector. With the default off these replay unchanged, a fixture family's claimed type reaches its handler only on a Native backend and reaches Python on Proxy, and on a confined connection a claimed type off the allow-list or with a mismatched selector answers Browser message refused with no handler call. A test that turns the default on through a constructor parameter (D37) and binds no worker replays the same cases, and also shows that no leg opens, that the claimed type reaches its handler, that the connect event follows the welcome, that the disconnect event runs once on a close and once on a failed send, that a connection outlives a worker's exit, that shutdown closes it with 1001, and that websocket.enabled false refuses as it does today.
- **size:** L, 3 checkpoints (registry, publish handle, Admitted value, confinement gate and connection events; the recorded WS cases; the leg-free path). Python in scope: servers/websocket (~6K, read); about 1.5K new Rust.

- **registration:** gdaemon websocket/ modules, not gcore (the .gobby/plans/task-25341.md R1 rejection of a WS registry in core stands); no registry line. The leg-free form is one compiled default in crates/gdaemon/src/websocket/, which CP-WAVE5-CUT's activation commit flips, with the settings parameter filled in serve.rs (D102). The one edit outside websocket/ is the accept call in crates/gdaemon/src/front_door/mod.rs:261, which passes the Admitted value; if the record's frozen list holds that file, a Found Work line under this chunk names it.
