### GW-1: GW-1: native /mcp gateway with per-tool routing

- **kind:** seam
- **goal:** #24884 under runner-first (D26): native policy, discovery and dispatch at /mcp and the gobby meta-tools call_tool, get_tool_schema and list_tools (HTTP and stdio), with schema leases shared with Python through the DB. Every server:tool resolves to its own backend: Native, Compare or Proxy, where Proxy forwards to Python through the backend proxy with an internal caller class: to Python's own /mcp until GW-2 adds the loopback compatibility endpoint, and to that endpoint from GW-2 on, because the gateway owns the single policy pass (D26); an unknown tool falls to Proxy. gcore's ToolRegistry gains a composition rule: several family crates may contribute tools to one server, and only a duplicate tool name is rejected, which replaces ToolRegistry::new's DuplicateServer refusal (gcore mcp.rs:186-241) and lets the pilot's gobby-tasks tools go to Compare and then Native at the CP-TEMPLATE cutovers while the agents, plans and team tools on the same servers stay proxied. Compare reads run dual-leg and writes go to Python once. #24841 is the plan: map approval approves it as amended here against runner-first (the worker boundary replaces runner_backend.front_door_secret; amendments 2.1.8 and 2.1.9 fold into this brief), which settles its criterion 3. #24884's edge on #24151 narrows to GW-2's preflight worker op (s2-11:264). #24884's edge on #21566 is cut: MUX-1 reaches this chunk through GW-2 and lands after it (D26), so GW-1 resolves an external server's tools to Proxy like any other tool and builds only the parts of #24884's multiplexer criteria that need no Backend. It builds the native cancel route (#24884's 2.1.9; .gobby/plans/external-mcp-transport-multiplexer.md 2.2): POST /api/mcp/tools/cancel {call_id}, which admits the callers POST /api/mcp/tools/call admits and takes the caller's session from the front door's identity, where call_id is the x-gobby-call-id header gmcp sent on that call (MCP-CRATE). A caller-scoped registry holds the calls that reach Backend, so it stays empty until MUX-1 binds it. A registered call answers {cancelled:true}. Any other id leaves a tombstone in the caller's scope (kept 600 seconds, at most 4,096, oldest evicted first) and answers {cancelled:false}, so another session's cancel leaves a call running, and a late or duplicate cancel changes nothing. The call entry checks the caller's tombstones before it dispatches on any backend, and a hit answers the ordinary failure payload with error_code CANCELLED and dispatches nothing. A call already running on Native or Proxy is never interrupted, so until CP-WAVE5-CUT an in-flight external call runs to its own end. What needs Backend is MUX-1's: external dispatch behind the same policy pass (2.1.6), and forwarding an external cancel, the external tool-inventory cache, the passive GET /api/mcp/tools read and the external schema_hash (2.1.9), with their two tests. The gateway also keeps Python's per-call metrics (the MCP metrics of the multiplexer plan's Decision 3), which OBS's gobby-metrics tools read: a call it dispatches to a Native handler, and from CP-WAVE5-CUT to Backend, writes the tool_metrics aggregate and the tool_call event that MetricsManager.record_call writes (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/metrics.py:54-96; Python's two call sites are src/gobby/mcp_proxy/services/tool_execution.py:650-672 and src/gobby/mcp_proxy/client_manager/invocation.py:121-136). A Proxy call and Compare's Python leg are recorded by Python's dispatch behind the compatibility endpoint, and Compare's native leg records nothing, so each call counts once. The gateway classifies tool results with a native port of src/gobby/hooks/tool_outcomes.py, whole, at crates/gcore/src/tool_outcomes.rs (normalize_tool_outcome, classify_raw_tool_result, tool_outcome_from_data and hook_event_tool_outcome; the Python module imports only the standard library), because its /mcp and REST answers read classify_raw_tool_result from CP-MCP-CUT, before RULE-N2 and HOOK-2 land; both reuse this port (D99). Its /mcp call_tool keeps GobbyDaemonTools.call_tool's behaviours (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/server.py:234-387): canonicalize_call_tool_wrapper's refusals as is_error results, the caller-session refusal, the client guard, the wait heartbeat with its timeout cap (crates/gmcp/src/call_tool.rs is the Rust reference for the cap), the failure flattening and the stripped success field. A result under enforcement whose error_code is INVALID_ARGUMENTS and that carries a schema appends that tool to the unlocked_tools session variable, on every backend (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/services/tool_execution.py:223-234; src/gobby/mcp_proxy/services/schema_guidance.py:44-65). ToolProxyService's tool filter has no production setter (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/services/tool_proxy.py:75-93; src/gobby/mcp_proxy/server.py:123-130), so its branches (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/services/tool_execution.py:478-480; src/gobby/mcp_proxy/services/tool_discovery.py:44-57, 103-105) are debt and are not ported. A Native handler that fails with an error answers the payload of Python's except path (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/services/tool_execution.py:743-809), with fallback_suggestions [] until MCP-FLIP binds the native resolver, and on a Compare leg that field is triaged as an accepted contract change until then (D17). A failure payload a handler returns carries no such field, and a Proxy failure carries Python's own. Output repair, the after phase, result offload and the outcome tracker (D99) stay in Python's own /mcp path while this chunk's Proxy forwards there; GW-2 builds them at the gateway when it moves Proxy to the compatibility endpoint, so this chunk leaves one hook point after dispatch on every backend. The caller-session refusal treats daemon-owned execution as speaking for its caller (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/server.py:471-490). The /mcp mount keeps Python's transport guards, which Python gets from the MCP SDK and a native mount must build, because replay sends no attack (src/gobby/servers/app_factory.py:100-136, 160; docs/guides/configuration.md:351-358, 395-417; D124). Bearer auth runs first. On a loopback bind the Host must match a loopback host or an mcp_allowed_hosts entry, its port wildcard form included, else 421, and an Origin, when sent, must match a loopback origin or a configured host's https origin, else 403; off loopback neither check runs. A POST needs a JSON Content-Type, else 400, and a body over the SDK's 4 MiB limit gets 413 (mcp.server.transport_security). While MCP exposure is on, the admitted hosts add this node's Tailscale name, with its port unless that is 443, read when the listener starts, never persisted, and left out with a warning when Tailscale cannot answer. These keys need a restart (src/gobby/config/registry.py:619, 626), so the family reads them once at start through FamilyContext's config epoch. The Tailscale read (src/gobby/ui_exposure.py:218) goes in gobby-core, which V1A's exposure reconcile and V1B's ui verbs reuse.
- **ledger_selectors:** ^HTTP \* /mcp$, ^MCP (HTTP|stdio) gobby:(call_tool|get_tool_schema|list_tools)$

The multiplexer plan's 2.2.4 gateway orderings on each backend: a cancel before the call's POST and a cancel while the gateway resolves the call's context each end the call CANCELLED with nothing dispatched; a cancel before an internal call starts skips it, while one already running completes; a late or duplicate cancel changes nothing; and another session's cancel returns {cancelled:false}. A Native call adds one tool_metrics count, and a Proxy or Compare call adds one through Python's dispatch, never two. The vectors of src/gobby/hooks/tool_outcomes.py in tests/contracts/rules/normalize_vectors.json, which P0-DECISIONS writes, replay equal through crates/gcore/src/tool_outcomes.rs. An INVALID_ARGUMENTS answer on each backend keeps the lease and adds Python's unlocked_tools delta. REC-PILOT's completion cases replay here only on Proxy, through Python's own /mcp, because this chunk builds no completion pipeline (see its goal). tests/servers/test_mcp_allowed_hosts.py and tests/servers/test_mcp_admitted_hosts.py replay natively on /mcp: an unlisted Host with a bearer gets 421, a listed one without a bearer gets 401, an empty list keeps loopback and refuses a tailnet Host, a port wildcard accepts any port, a configured host's Origin must be its https origin, and exposure admits only the node's name. A body over 4 MiB gets 413 and a POST without a JSON Content-Type gets 400.

Python in scope: mcp_proxy dispatch, discovery and lease code ~9K of 67.3K (read); Rust ~6K. The cancel route and the metrics writes add about 0.4K. The tool_outcomes port (505 lines of Python) and the wrapper behaviours add about 0.7K.

The compatibility endpoint answers only on loopback with the backend secret, so nothing else reaches it without the gateway's pass. The single pass is a before phase and an after phase: a call the before phase denies runs no after phase, and the after phase never redispatches (D82). A native offload row that Python's reader cannot page would lose a result, so a case pages a gateway-written row through Python's gobby-results. A tracker failure must not change the answer: the shim logs it and the gateway returns the handler's result, as Python's try does (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/services/tool_execution.py:222-252). A result over R0's 16 MiB domain-op bound fails the after call like any after-phase failure: neither the pass nor the tracker reads it, and the gateway logs it, answers and offloads.

### CP-MCP-REVIEW: Checkpoint review: the native MCP gateway

- **kind:** checkpoint
- **goal:** Review pause before the native MCP gateway goes live. Ruling 14 names 'the mcp proxy' as the second checkpoint. Here that means the gateway built by GW-1 and GW-2: /mcp, the gobby meta-tools, the REST tool routes, per-tool routing, GW-2's loopback compatibility endpoint with no policy pass, and the single policy pass in the gateway (D26), with every tool still on Proxy. The external server pool (MUX-1 and MUX-2) and the removal of Python's MCP backend (MCP-FLIP) go live at CP-WAVE5: the pool is single-owner state that moves only after its last Python callers (rule preflight, pipelines, hooks) are native, and the flip needs every internal server native. Packet: GW-1's and GW-2's validation: REC-PILOT's gateway and REST tool cases and the gmcp wire contracts replayed with every tool on Proxy, then with fixture tools Native through a test family, with one case per backend (Proxy, Native and Compare) asserting that exactly one policy pass runs, in the gateway; the dormancy proof; R-RETIRE's landing; CP-RUNNER-CUT's window record. On no-go, after the de-escalation, send one project send_message with wake=true naming the in-flight gateway and pilot chunks (PROJ-1, SEAM-CALLERS, SEAM-WS, GW-1, GW-2, A1-RUNTIME, A1-CONFIG, A1-SECRETS, B0-READ, B0-WRITE and B0-CLOSE): they stop at their next checkpoint and land nothing until the fixes Josh names close. When those fixes close, the session Josh opens for this review sends a second one that releases them, before it builds its new packet. The packet also carries GW-2's after-phase cases (D82): on every backend the after phase runs exactly once after each dispatched call, and an after-phase failure keeps the handler's result. The packet also carries GW-2's Proxy cases for an external fixture server and a gobby-namespace tool (D26) and GW-1's cancel orderings. The packet also carries GW-2's completion cases (D99): offload envelopes and the rows Python's gobby-results pages, a repaired openapi result on Proxy, the open_tool_errors and unlocked_tools deltas and the REST shape of a failed external result. It states the accepted difference that Python's /api/metrics stays flat for gateway-served REST calls until OBS at CP-WAVE1-CUT. Every packet opens with a summary of at most one screen: what changed since the previous review, what needs Josh's call, and any check that did not pass. Every packet also carries the cutover plan for CP-MCP-CUT: the window length and the named triggers; the trigger table, which gives each trigger its default outcome (2 or 3) and who decides; the fix-forward bound (at most two fix cycles, the last fix landing within 24 hours of the first outcome-2 decision, each followed by its own clean window, then outcome 3), which Josh may change in his go; the pinned generation (the one installed when the cutover sets its hold) and the restore members; the recipe; and the loss window: the writes made after the backup, through the rehearsal and the window, which only a backup restore would lose (a drop, or CP-WAVE3-CUT's relocation once it ran; an expand-only rollback loses none, D22), plus every live agent seat's credentials if the recipe restores the backup. It lists, by SHA, every prepared commit that the cutover lands in its step 6 (each schema-carrying chunk's commit on port/prepared/<chunk id>, each dependent chunk's schema-test commit and each post-TPL template commit), and the pending fixes (D40 item 3: none while ruling 24 stands), each with a proposed disposition: pick; skipped; ported by <chunk id>; or dropped, with its reason. A pick that carries a schema input, a gcode or ghook version or a template is a prepared commit too. Josh's go approves both lists. It also lists, by SHA, every chunk candidate landed since the previous review, each with its code-reviewer attestation and, where protocol step 7 required one, its security-review attestation. It lists every irreversible step that needs Josh's explicit go, every drop the cutover carries among them; an expand step is not one, because the restore plus the deactivation commit undoes it (D22). Until Josh has given one, it also asks for a standing ruling on an emergency rollback restart during quiet hours, proposing this default: a health or start proof failure, data loss or a schema verify failure rolls back at once, after the protected-runs read and with its global send_message, and any other outcome-3 trigger waits for quiet hours to end, with the hold and the pin extended. At once means the binary restore, because the project's quiet-hours rule refuses gobby stop and gobby cutover in every hooked session and lets gobby rollback restore through (.gobby/workflows/rules/quiet-hours.yaml:15-24), so the deactivation build's promotion waits for them to end, and so does a backup restore unless Josh runs its gobby stop from his own shell. The packet also lists by waiver id every docs/contracts/parity-waivers.json entry and case citation that the cut's activation commit lands, as planned changes and not as mismatches, because until then the chunks' replays read fixture copies and a live Compare record never cites a waiver (D84). It also names, for the workflow named CI, for .github/workflows/rust-ci.yml and for the workflow named Release Branch CI (.github/workflows/postgres-pgsearch-smoke.yml), the newest run on 0.9.0 that ran to a result, with its commit and result; a run that a later push cancelled has no result. The first two must be green (D34). The third is advisory, but a red run is found work fixed before the cut, and when it has no such run since the previous review, this review starts one through workflow_dispatch and names its result, or names it superseded if a later push cancels it (D85). Before writing the packet, fetch origin and list the pending fixes as D40 item 3 defines them, which is none while ruling 24 stands; the review commits nothing, and its cutover cherry-picks and lands the picks that Josh approves. Category manual: escalate_task, then de_escalate_task after Josh's go, then close_task. Record the packet as a review-packet attestation and keep it out of the checkout. Call escalate_task(reason='needs_human: go or no-go for CP-MCP; packet in attestation <id>'), present the packet and the question in the final message, and end the turn. Josh answers in that terminal. If that session is gone, he answers in any later default session, or with gobby tasks de-escalate, or in the web UI. On go: de_escalate_task(reason='GO from Josh <timestamp>: <his words>'), claim_task, an approved implementation attestation quoting him, then close_task(reason='done', preview=true) and the same call without preview, with no commit; the final message then asks Josh to prompt the port dispatcher, because a review's close does not wake it (D116). On no-go: de_escalate_task(reason='NO-GO from Josh ...: <his words>'). Keep the task open. Link the fixes Josh names with add_dependency(task_id=<review>, depends_on=<fix>). File any new filing as a child of #21542, so the port dispatcher starts it, and label it operator-directed, which the found-work gate exempts (src/gobby/install/shared/workflows/rules/stop-gates/enforce-found-work-ladder.yaml:67). A no-go holds no claim, because escalate_task released it, so this session ends its turn with the task open and its blockers linked, and its final message asks Josh to prompt the port dispatcher, which starts the fixes (D116). When they close, the task shows ready again, the dispatcher names it in its final message, and Josh prompts this session or opens a new one, which claims it, builds a new packet and escalates again. Never close a no-go. If Josh abandons the direction, re-plan the downstream edges before any wont_do close, because that close releases them too.

Then clear the freeze, the hold and the pin, and message each session that asked to land that the freeze is clear, saying whether it is among the chunks that outcome 3 stops. Every name in this recipe is install-local (this install's own backup, pin, hold and generations), so A runs it unchanged on its own install if its own adoption of this checkpoint rolls back, with its main checkout moved back to the commit it ran before in place of a deactivation commit (D40 item 4). The pinned target is the generation installed at step 3, a Rust-runner generation that proxies /mcp. Restoring its gdaemon sends /mcp back to Python whole, and Python's own /mcp runs its own policy pass again. The restore members are gdaemon alone.

### A1-RUNTIME: A1-RUNTIME: runtime handshake and managed principals (#21559 P4)

- **kind:** family
- **goal:** Josh's A1, first part (#25341 D1; D25). #21559 P4 (#24439) in the existing runtime family crate (crates/gruntime): the managed challenge route (#24453), credential issuance (#24454), rotation with the grant.json rewrite (#24455), the native managed handshake (#24456), grant presentation (#24457) and GET /api/runtime/config. #24456 follows Python's current in-request retry (0.25/0.5/1.0 s delays; a lost race reuses the competing successor; runner_init/servers.py:425-486, 047fa598a7), not the leaf's credential_issuance_failed. #24453-#24455 are re-verified against the P4 Python drift since the plan stamp (#24816, #24675, #25264; +129/-28). D12 and ruling 16: materialize_managed_launch becomes a gruntime service, and rotate_due's native iteration is written and registered here on R4's scheduler, active only once the runtime family is (CP-TEMPLATE-READS-CUT). Capability-token verification (#24452) is built earlier, in SEAM-CALLERS. The family claims only the paths it implements: A1-RUNTIME claims /api/runtime, A1-CONFIG and A1-SECRETS extend the claim, and A1-SECRETS lands the family's default flip dormant for CP-TEMPLATE-READS-CUT to activate. This chunk also carries #25068 (closed as superseded by this chunk's task, D31), which moved here because #24457 blocks it and this chunk depends on SEAM-CALLERS. SEAM-CALLERS lands the leaf's agent-token class. This chunk adds its runtime-grant class to #25046's admission type: a grant that meets the route's RequiredCapability as Python's _GRANT_ROUTES declares it (src/gobby/servers/grant_auth.py:85-170: mode=daemon on the compute routes, a bare capability name on the status routes, a broker operation on the code-index routes), through #24452's token verification and #24457's managed grant presentation, with no second verifier. A missing, insufficient, revoked or wrong-mode grant is Rejected, and unavailable authority is a typed 503. Each family declares its own route's capability and binds the class at its own activation: AI-1B (#25106), VOICE and CIX-1 for their grant routes, and code-index 1.9's grant checks converge on it. #25264's renewal is this chunk's too, though its leaf and plan name neither it nor the notice: an expired seat's POST to the handshake passes only on a validly signed expired token with an agent_run_id, a live run and a matching identity, and the grant it renews has no token_exp (src/gobby/servers/auth_service.py:339-353, 614-644; src/gobby/servers/routes/runtime_handshake.py:183-186; src/gobby/runtime_grants/handshake.py:154-178). When a renewal fails with credential_issuance_failed, the route still answers Python's 403 (src/gobby/servers/routes/runtime_handshake.py:130-139, 234-235) and, when the run has a parent, writes one agent_recovery row for that parent: event capability_expired, the token's exp as dedupe_key, Python's text and its deterministic id under ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING (src/gobby/servers/routes/runtime_handshake.py:99-127; src/gobby/agents/resume_finalization.py:144-199). No run or no parent means no row, and a failed write is logged and never changes the answer. The notice has no wake and takes no lock, so it is a shared-row write under D19 and needs no worker op: gruntime declares a one-method notice port with an interim adapter that writes that row, until AG-3's agent_recovery writer replaces the adapter in CP-WAVE2-CUT's activation commit (D29). The bearer-to-grant match changed: the machine key presents only an interactive grant that names no session, and a session-bound credential presents only the interactive grant bound to its own session (src/gobby/servers/grant_auth.py:235-276; 827d857bba, 248032ae05); gcore's presentation_bearer picks the bearer the same way on the client side (crates/gcore/src/grant/bearer.rs:23-37). This chunk's selector also matches POST /api/runtime/signed-request/nonce, a route Python already had at 08f709e822 (21167ac07f) and a row the ledger gained after this brief (89afd0e993): a public route that issues a single-use nonce bound to the presented capability payload from an in-process store, valid 30 seconds, at most 256 at once, answering 400 for a payload that does not decode to a capability object and 503 when the store is full (src/gobby/servers/routes/signed_request.py:37-52; src/gobby/servers/middleware/auth.py:46; src/gobby/runtime_grants/signed_request.py:24-26, 92-131). AuthService.admit_signed_request spends that nonce for exactly two routes, POST /api/admin/restart and GET /api/admin/cron/protected-runs, after it verifies the payload and the request MAC (src/gobby/servers/auth_service.py:497-537; src/gobby/runtime_grants/signed_request.py:28-35). The store is one in-process singleton (src/gobby/runtime_grants/signed_request.py:131), so a Python consumer cannot spend a nonce that a native issuer issued.
- **ledger_selectors:** ^HTTP \S+ /api/runtime(/|$)

Renewal and notice cases are recorded here from Python before the port (tests/servers/routes/test_runtime_handshake_renewal.py:152, 241, 291): a renewal issued, an expired token refused, one credential_issuance_failed 403 with one agent_recovery row byte-equal to Python's, id and metadata_json included, a repeat for the same exp adding none, a run with no parent adding none, and a failed write leaving the 403 unchanged.
- **size:** M, 2 checkpoints (challenge, issuance and rotation; handshake, presentation, materialize_managed_launch and #25068's runtime-grant class). Python in scope: runtime_grants 1.3K, managed credentials and handshake ~2.5K, runner_init managed issue ~0.6K; Rust ~3K in gruntime. Renewal and the notice add about 0.2K.

### A1-CONFIG: A1-CONFIG: config model, reads and writes (#21559 P5a)

- **kind:** family
- **goal:** Josh's A1, second part. #21559 P5 config routes (#24440): GET /api/config/schema (#24458), the active-state reads of values, UI settings and global tool approvals (#24463), GET /api/config/effective, YAML template read and export (#24462), per-key and complete-candidate validation (#24464, #24465), PATCH /api/config/values (#24466), YAML 1.2 reading in Rust (#24468), and PUT /api/config/template with POST /api/config/import (#24469). DaemonConfig's model moves to gcore::config under SEAM-FAMILY's config epoch, and every write publishes a new epoch that R2's worker reconciliation applies to Python. The brief starts from today's counts: 87 validator decorators, not the plan's 78 (new: validate_accept_band, validate_api_base, validate_decisions, validate_mcp_allowed_hosts, two app.py model validators, validate_roots, drop_unset_entries, validate_routes, require_context_limit_floor), and a schema contract of 514 exact keys (512 public, 2 machine) plus 11 patterns, 474 properties. For #24468, crates/gruntime/src/yaml.rs reads the YAML documents that PUT /api/config/template and POST /api/config/import receive as YAML 1.2 core, and crates/gruntime/src/pyyaml.rs keeps an exported string plain only when PyYAML's 1.1 resolver and the 1.2 reader both read it as a string, so every Rust export reads back unchanged through yaml.safe_load. The plan's Python Yaml12Loader and Yaml12SafeDumper (gdaemon-runtime-family plan 5.11) are not built (D4), so Python's YAML 1.1 readings of imported documents, and its plain export of 0o17, 1e5, 1.5e5, 1E+5 and .5e3, which the 1.2 reader reads as numbers, are D18 known-bad rows. #24466's 5.9.10 (one project-scoped secrets set) is met in MUX-1, whose multiplexer-plan 1.4 absorbs the secrets set this chunk lands into SecretStore::set_in. Nothing publishes config_active_state once commit A stops Python's ConfigRuntime, and that row is what every native read serves (crates/gruntime/src/config.rs:61; crates/gruntime/src/grant.rs:68-84; crates/gruntime/src/handshake.rs:95-98; crates/gruntime/src/verify.rs:60-66; src/gobby/config/runtime_active_state.py:53-75). An existing hub would keep a frozen row, so every PATCH /api/config/values would commit and then answer reconcile_failed after 65 seconds, and a fresh hub would have no row, so GET /api/config/effective and GET /api/runtime/config would answer 503 and the managed handshake would refuse. So this chunk builds a native publisher on a hub, behind gdaemon's compiled backend default and dormant while that default starts the worker, and commit A activates it with no code of its own. It reads config_store and config_state, builds the same document (src/gobby/config/runtime_active_state.py:15-50), with secret bindings sealed under Python's associated data (crates/gruntime/src/secrets.rs:123), and upserts the same row: first at start before any door admits, as ConfigRuntime.start publishes before ready (src/gobby/config/runtime.py:176-219), then on each native write's commit, on gobby_config_changed and on a 30-second poll that retries a failed upsert (src/gobby/config/runtime.py:806-865). Before its first publish it does reconcile_registry's work, as src/gobby/runner_init/storage.py:236 does before ConfigRuntime starts: it deletes stored rows of removed config, repairs each row's is_secret from the contract and refuses a residual key (src/gobby/storage/config_repository.py:175-202; src/gobby/config/registry.py:612). Each failure is a fatal start hook error with Python's message: a residual key, which a relaunch would not clear, takes R2's refused state, and a failed first publish ends the start nonzero. Activation is per key from runtime_config_contract.json: a live key moves to active at once, a managed key through the port of managed_embedding_projection (src/gobby/runner_init/storage.py:249; src/gobby/config/runtime.py:727-733), and a restart_required key stays at its boot value and is listed in pending_restart_keys until the next start. Native has no prepare step, because a family reads a key per call or through FamilyContext's config epoch, so failed_live_keys stays empty, and each successor of a stateful subscriber (src/gobby/runner_init/config_subscribers.py:153-205) rebuilds when the epoch moves. Each published revision moves the epoch and goes out as config_event on the broker (src/gobby/runner_init/servers.py:68-79; src/gobby/servers/websocket/broadcast.py:307), which web/src/hooks/useConfiguration.ts listens for. A write of agent_build.build_root also checks the host's filesystem: the value must be an existing, canonical, absolute directory that is neither a filesystem root nor an account home, and the write is refused otherwise with the validator's message (src/gobby/storage/config_mutations.py:414-420; src/gobby/config/agent_build.py:26-48; 0892e316b4). The native PATCH keeps that check, and R6's start proof reads the same rule.
- **ledger_selectors:** ^HTTP \S+ /api/config/(?!(prompts|secrets)(/|$)|validation-detection/preview$|generation-endpoints/)

- **oracle:** REC-PILOT's config cases (recorded with the pilot corpus; the #25599 start-gate fix makes config_values replay clean) and the checked-in runtime config contract (gcore/assets/config); differential replay asserts DB deltas and config-file deltas on a temp HOME. An accepted contract change named in this chunk's python_edits is recorded the same way: an entry and citation in a fixture copy, which the activation commit that flips the family lands (D84). Publisher vectors recorded from Python before the publisher commit: for a fixture store the native document equals Python's, sealed values compared by opening them. With the worker default off on an isolated hub, a stored row of a removed key goes at the first boot, a row whose is_secret disagrees with the contract is repaired, a residual key answers 503 backend_refused with Python's message until a full restart, a first boot with no row publishes before admission, GET /api/config/effective answers 200 and the managed handshake succeeds; a PATCH of a live key commits with no failed key and publishes config_event; and a PATCH of a restart_required key lists it in pending_restart_keys with its active value unchanged until the next start.

### CP-TEMPLATE-REVIEW: Checkpoint review: the first route family (A1 and the tasks pilot), with the pilot calibration

- **kind:** checkpoint

This review also runs the pilot calibration: D17's gate, the resizing of every remaining chunk and the census refresh. Packet: The calibration measurement: three passes of P0-HARNESS's soak loop over the committed REC-PILOT corpus, weighted by the gport shapes census, then differential replay and dual-run write replay of the whole corpus in the full-daemon harness, with tasks and the runtime family in Compare. Reads run dual-leg and writes go to Python once with B0-CLOSE's check_proxied. The diff source is front-door-compare.jsonl through gdaemon compare-report (D13). D17's gate result, which decides the go. The calibration report: tokens, wall time, checkpoints, the D11 stub rate, Rust test lines per checkpoint, recording cost per case, and a cost-versus-relief column for every remaining chunk (relief's friction scores: hook ingress 13.3, Python runtime 11.5, rule engine 9.5, restart holds 8.0 of 81.6 points). The session cap for after CP-TEMPLATE-CUT, at most 4 (D23): the measured provider quota, landing-lock wait and code-reviewer throughput (and security-auditor throughput, protocol step 7), and P's CPUs, memory and free disk, with the proposed cap kept within them. The resizing of the remaining chunks: sizes and splits only, applied with update_task and create_task on the chunk tasks, with gport ledger (or scripts/port/check_coverage.py until its diff is 0) and the disposition check rerun after any split; a scope or order change is a question for Josh in this packet. Each split writes its parts into a scratch copy of docs/port/map-v2.json under ~/.gobby/port/CP-TEMPLATE-REVIEW/: new chunk ids whose depends_on, ledger_selectors and tree_nodes divide the split chunk's, with every chunk that depended on the split chunk depending on all of its parts. The parts get one blocks edge per depends_on entry, the dependents' edges move from the split task to the parts, and the split task closes as superseded by them only after its edges have moved. The ledger check, the disposition check and mapcheck run against that scratch map. The refreshed census and the regenerated project record, written under ~/.gobby/port/CP-TEMPLATE-REVIEW/, outside the checkout and outside any session scratchpad or /tmp, and named in the packet attestation; CP-TEMPLATE-CUT lands them as its first, docs-only commit. The template fan-out (TERM-1, TPL, SRC, AI-1A, OBS, PROJ-2, AUTH, RULE-1A and HOOK-ENV) starts only after CP-TEMPLATE-CUT's Compare day closes. A 72h soak runs only if Josh asks, as a detached process between chunks with no claim held; the real-data snapshot stays off unless Josh approves it. Fixed by D4 bug-fix commits on 0.9.0, with their cases re-recorded (D18): the prompt save's reset of description, version and variables, the hash-ordered default_mode, unset and secret-category messages, the feature-candidate re-raise, the host-dependent time-zone check, the generation-endpoint 500s and the lax validation-detection preview. Every packet also carries the cutover plan for CP-TEMPLATE-CUT and its three follow-on cutovers (CP-TEMPLATE-READS-CUT, CP-TEMPLATE-WRITES-CUT and CP-TEMPLATE-CLOSE-CUT): the window length and the named triggers; the trigger table, which gives each trigger its default outcome (2 or 3) and who decides; the fix-forward bound (at most two fix cycles, the last fix landing within 24 hours of the first outcome-2 decision, each followed by its own clean window, then outcome 3), which Josh may change in his go; the pinned generation (the one installed when the cutover sets its hold) and the restore members; the recipe; and the loss window: the writes made after the backup, through the rehearsal and the window, which only a backup restore would lose (a drop, or CP-WAVE3-CUT's relocation once it ran; an expand-only rollback loses none, D22), plus every live agent seat's credentials if the recipe restores the backup. Before writing the packet, fetch origin and list the pending fixes as D40 item 3 defines them, which is none while ruling 24 stands; the review commits nothing, and its cutover cherry-picks and lands the picks that Josh approves. Category manual: escalate_task, then de_escalate_task after Josh's go, then close_task. Record the packet as a review-packet attestation and keep it out of the checkout. Call escalate_task(reason='needs_human: go or no-go for CP-TEMPLATE; packet in attestation <id>'), present the packet and the question in the final message, and end the turn. Josh answers in that terminal. If that session is gone, he answers in any later default session, or with gobby tasks de-escalate, or in the web UI. On go: de_escalate_task(reason='GO from Josh <timestamp>: <his words>'), claim_task, an approved implementation attestation quoting him, then close_task(reason='done', preview=true) and the same call without preview, with no commit; the final message then asks Josh to prompt the port dispatcher, because a review's close does not wake it (D116). On no-go: de_escalate_task(reason='NO-GO from Josh ...: <his words>'). Keep the task open. Link the fixes Josh names with add_dependency(task_id=<review>, depends_on=<fix>). File any new filing as a child of #21542, so the port dispatcher starts it, and label it operator-directed, which the found-work gate exempts (src/gobby/install/shared/workflows/rules/stop-gates/enforce-found-work-ladder.yaml:67). A no-go holds no claim, because escalate_task released it, so this session ends its turn with the task open and its blockers linked, and its final message asks Josh to prompt the port dispatcher, which starts the fixes (D116). When they close, the task shows ready again, the dispatcher names it in its final message, and Josh prompts this session or opens a new one, which claims it, builds a new packet and escalates again. Never close a no-go. If Josh abandons the direction, re-plan the downstream edges before any wont_do close, because that close releases them too.

### CP-TEMPLATE-CUT: Checkpoint cutover 1 of 4: the pilot families go to Compare

- **kind:** cutover
- **goal:** Category code. The first of the pilot's four cutovers: the runtime family (A1) and the tasks family go from Proxy to Compare, which is D13's live Compare day. Callers still get Python's answer (crates/gdaemon/src/front_door/routes.rs:186-254), so this step changes what is observed, not what is served. Before step 1, this session copies the census, the project record and the split map that CP-TEMPLATE-REVIEW wrote to the directory named in its packet attestation into its worktree, and lands them as a docs-only commit. (1) Announcement: Send one global send_message before anything else. It names the checkpoint, the backup's daemon restart, the activation restart, the window and its triggers, the landing freeze and the loss window (the writes made after the backup, through the rehearsal and the window, which a backup restore would lose). It also tells every session how to wait: a session ready to land during the freeze sends this session a direct message, then registers wait_for_coordination(owner_session=<this session>, reply=true, timeout=3600) and registers it again after every timeout and every prompt (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/coordination.py:52-59); this session messages each of them when the freeze clears. (2) Restart timing: Read project_policy.quiet_hours live at that moment, never from a brief, and start only when the backup, the rehearsal and the whole window, at their planned lengths, end before the next quiet hours. Query the protected-runs route directly, GET http://localhost:<daemon port>/api/admin/cron/protected-runs with the bearer header that daemon_auth_headers() builds (src/gobby/utils/local_token.py:460-475; src/gobby/servers/routes/admin/_lifecycle.py:116-126), and start only on a 200 answer whose runs list is empty; a 401, a 503 or a transport error is not clear, because fetch_protected_runs reports no runs on any error or non-200 answer (src/gobby/cli/_daemon_protected_runs.py:30-55). Every later restart, promotion or restore in this cutover repeats both reads and composes no restart notice by hand: the daemon sends its own HOLD before a restart-intent stop and BACK after every healthy start (AGENTS.md rules 4 and 12), and step (9) sends its own message before a rollback; the standing ruling that the review asks for covers only an emergency rollback during quiet hours. Whenever a pick, a prepared commit or the activation commit of this cutover changes a bundle source under web/, and again whenever a deactivation commit reverts such a change, run gobby ui build once that promotion's restart is healthy: the daemon serves web/dist from disk, web/dist is untracked (web/.gitignore:2), and no landing or promotion rebuilds it (D65). ### CP-TEMPLATE-READS-CUT: Checkpoint cutover 2 of 4: A1 goes live and the tasks reads go Native

- **kind:** cutover

The second pilot cutover, and the point where A1 goes live: the runtime family serves every route it claims natively (A1-RUNTIME, A1-CONFIG and A1-SECRETS), and A1-RUNTIME's rotate_due job replaces Python's one-iteration op on R4's scheduler. The tasks reads go Native too. #24474 (`runtime` defaults to native) is this activation commit. (1) Announcement: Send one global send_message before anything else. It names the checkpoint, the backup's daemon restart, the activation restart, the window and its triggers, the landing freeze and the loss window (the writes made after the backup, through the rehearsal and the window, which a backup restore would lose). It also tells every session how to wait: a session ready to land during the freeze sends this session a direct message, then registers wait_for_coordination(owner_session=<this session>, reply=true, timeout=3600) and registers it again after every timeout and every prompt (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/coordination.py:52-59); this session messages each of them when the freeze clears. (2) Restart timing: Read project_policy.quiet_hours live at that moment, never from a brief, and start only when the backup, the rehearsal and the whole window, at their planned lengths, end before the next quiet hours. Query the protected-runs route directly, GET http://localhost:<daemon port>/api/admin/cron/protected-runs with the bearer header that daemon_auth_headers() builds (src/gobby/utils/local_token.py:460-475; src/gobby/servers/routes/admin/_lifecycle.py:116-126), and start only on a 200 answer whose runs list is empty; a 401, a 503 or a transport error is not clear, because fetch_protected_runs reports no runs on any error or non-200 answer (src/gobby/cli/_daemon_protected_runs.py:30-55). ### CP-TEMPLATE-WRITES-CUT: Checkpoint cutover 3 of 4: the tasks writes go Native

- **kind:** cutover
- **goal:** Category code. The third pilot cutover: the tasks writes, claims, dependencies and lifecycle go Native (B0-WRITE). (1) Announcement: Send one global send_message before anything else. It names the checkpoint, the backup's daemon restart, the activation restart, the window and its triggers, the landing freeze and the loss window (the writes made after the backup, through the rehearsal and the window, which a backup restore would lose). It also tells every session how to wait: a session ready to land during the freeze sends this session a direct message, then registers wait_for_coordination(owner_session=<this session>, reply=true, timeout=3600) and registers it again after every timeout and every prompt (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/coordination.py:52-59); this session messages each of them when the freeze clears. (2) Restart timing: Read project_policy.quiet_hours live at that moment, never from a brief, and start only when the backup, the rehearsal and the whole window, at their planned lengths, end before the next quiet hours. Query the protected-runs route directly, GET http://localhost:<daemon port>/api/admin/cron/protected-runs with the bearer header that daemon_auth_headers() builds (src/gobby/utils/local_token.py:460-475; src/gobby/servers/routes/admin/_lifecycle.py:116-126), and start only on a 200 answer whose runs list is empty; a 401, a 503 or a transport error is not clear, because fetch_protected_runs reports no runs on any error or non-200 answer (src/gobby/cli/_daemon_protected_runs.py:30-55). Every later restart, promotion or restore in this cutover repeats both reads and composes no restart notice by hand: the daemon sends its own HOLD before a restart-intent stop and BACK after every healthy start (AGENTS.md rules 4 and 12), and step (9) sends its own message before a rollback; the standing ruling that the review asks for covers only an emergency rollback during quiet hours. Whenever a pick, a prepared commit or the activation commit of this cutover changes a bundle source under web/, and again whenever a deactivation commit reverts such a change, run gobby ui build once that promotion's restart is healthy: the daemon serves web/dist from disk, web/dist is untracked (web/.gitignore:2), and no landing or promotion rebuilds it (D65). (3) Hold, pin and freeze: Before anything in this step, prepare this cutover's branch off 0.9.0 HEAD, in a worktree made as protocol step 1 says for an operator-opened session, because the main checkout stays on 0.9.0: first the approved picks that carry no schema input, no gcode or ghook version and no template, each cherry-picked with git cherry-pick -x, and a docs-only commit that records in docs/port/picks.md, one line per full A SHA, every disposition the review packet approved that the file does not yet hold (each plain pick as picked as <new SHA>; each pick that lands as a prepared commit in step 6 as picked at <checkpoint id>, because this commit precedes it and cannot hold its SHA; each fix skipped, ported by <chunk id> or dropped, with its reason), made whenever that list is not empty, and adding a Found Work line in docs/port/record.md under each open chunk named as ported by, with the A SHA, so that chunk ports the fix or drops it before it lands (D40 item 3); before writing it, check each pick's (cherry picked from commit <A sha>) trailer and amend a missing one into that pick on this unlanded branch, because git cherry-pick -x documents the trailer only for picks without conflicts and a pick concluded with git commit -m or redone by hand has none (D40 item 3); then the activation commit, and the deactivation commit, which reverts the activation and every prepared commit. Then set GEN-ROLLBACK's hold with gobby rollback hold set, which prints the token that every later promotion and restore in this cutover passes as --hold-token, with an expiry at the planned end of the window, counting the backup and the rehearsal. Pin the generation installed now: it is the only rollback target during the window and any fix-forward, and its manifest (source commit, versions, schema identity) is recorded on the task; check its source commit against the last promotion that the previous cutover recorded at its close (for CP-RUNNER-CUT, GEN-ROLLBACK's landing drill on P, or, if Josh refused that drill at map approval under D38, P's installed .gcode-, .gdaemon- and .ghook-release-identity.json receipts; on A, its installed release-identity receipts, D40 item 4), and record any difference on the task. Nothing else lands before step 6. The rehearsal and step 6 use exactly these reviewed commits. Record the window plan as an attestation: start, end, each trigger with its baseline or bound, the trigger table (step 8), the restore members, the rollback commands and the hold token, because a replacement session reads them there. From here on nothing rolls back by itself if this session stops (D118). A usage limit or a provider outage leaves its pane and its claim, and the background watch keeps logging. An outage's next timeout wake reaches this session. A usage limit holds its pane on the provider's menu, where no wake lands until Josh submits a prompt there after the reset. Either way it then reads the watch's whole log since its last read and acts on any trigger it recorded. From step 3 on only this session lands or promotes, and it lands nothing more until step 6, so the backup, the rehearsal and the activation all start from the same generation and schema. hub-backup does not archive the task JSONL backup (~/.gobby/backups/<project-uuid>/tasks.jsonl), which native backup_tasks writes, so this session copies it into the backup directory with mode 0600 and records its sha256 in a window-plan attestation that supersedes step 3's (supersedes_id). The session keeps the stack, with every daemon in the isolated home stopped, because steps 6, 8 and 9 can rerun parts of this step on it, and removes the stack and its volumes when this cutover closes, finishes outcome 3's recipe or starts again from step 1. Install the pinned generation into the isolated home's bin directory, then build the cutover branch's reviewed activation commit, with the prepared commits under it, and promote it over the pinned one there, which retains the pinned one. Apply this cutover's schema step if it has one, and run the activated build over the stage's corpora so that it writes rows. Then run gobby rollback restore against the isolated home with the members that step 9 names for this cut (the stamped set when it carries a schema step), with the restored generation's Python started from a worktree at the activation commit, because that is the tree the live checkout will hold. If this cutover carries no schema step, prove that the restored generation serves on the unchanged schema and reads back the rows the activated build wrote, and that Python reads them back too while Python exists. If it carries an expand step, prove that the restored generation starts and serves on the migrated rehearsal hub, whose expand-only receipts sit above its head (D22), and reads back the rows the activated build wrote, and that it writes through every table the expand step altered (an insert and an update on its own code paths succeed). (6) Activation commit: Read quiet hours and the protected-runs route again, live, and continue only when the whole window, at its stated length from the end of this step's CI wait, ends before the next quiet hours; otherwise clear the freeze, the hold and the pin, message each waiting session, and start again from step 1 in a later span. Before landing, extend the hold and the pin to the window's end as it now falls (gobby rollback hold extend --hold-token <token> --until <end>, and pin extend), and record the actual start and end in a window-plan attestation that supersedes the latest one (supersedes_id) when this session wrote it, and with no supersedes_id when it did not (step 3). A red run takes an outcome-2 fix (step 8) before this promotion, within that outcome's two fix cycles. The promotion retains the outgoing generation and also installs gmcp and gterm when their versions changed. If the promotion refuses, or a run is still red past that bound, link the prepared deactivation commit to this task, first rebased, given fresh bumps and rechecked as step 9 says when a fix has moved HEAD past it, and land it under the freeze before clearing it, with no restore, because the pinned generation is still installed, and escalate to Josh as outcome 3 does. A corpus or golden case's citation of a docs/contracts/parity-waivers.json entry lands in the activation commit that flips that case's surface, with any of its entries not yet landed and the regenerated parity ledger, because a cited case passes only on its native answer and so fails while the old answer serves, and an uncited case passes only on its recording. The citation is the only change to each case, and the recording stays. The activated build replays those cases as Waived; any replay of them on the restored generation or the deactivation build reads them from the deactivation commit's tree and compares with their recordings; and the deactivation commit's revert takes them out (D48). This commit activates the following. The tasks family's claimed routes grow to its write, release-claim, dependency and lifecycle routes, and those tools' per-tool defaults flip from Compare to Native. The close route keeps reaching Python, and the close and landing tools stay in Compare. The prepared commit that lands before it is B0-WRITE's, with its schema inputs (D22). POST /api/tasks/{task_id}/claim keeps proxying until AG-3 binds the native AssignmentNotifier at CP-WAVE2-CUT (tasks-family Q11); MCP claim_task, which sends no assignment notice, flips here with the other tools. It also binds gtasks' ClosurePolicy port to B0-CLOSE's interim adapter, because a native reparent or delete that leaves a parent with no open child closes it through the policy (B0-WRITE), so each such ancestor close gets its decision from Python's evaluate_closure_policy through the closure-policy worker op (D41). B0-WRITE's stale claim sweep registers on R4's registry in place of Python's op. (7) Observation window: Hold it in this session with a provider background watch that samples the triggers into a log, plus wait_for_coordination on that watch, registered again every 3,600 seconds or less, after every timeout wake and after every prompt; after a compaction, fetch the wait tool's schema again first (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/coordination.py:42). The window ends before the next quiet hours. Length and named rollback triggers: 8 hours. Triggers: a write whose DB delta differs from Python's recorded delta; a claim, release or hand-off that leaves a task in a state Python's readers reject; a missed pg_notify or WS event that leaves a Python cache stale; a cycle check that differs; a task JSONL backup that Python cannot read; health or start proof failure. An ancestor auto-close after a reparent or delete that differs from Python's, or that stays open because the closure-policy worker op failed or timed out, is also a trigger (D41). Job triggers: a job this activation swapped in that misses its cadence, errors on every fire, or deletes or changes a row its Python op would keep. (8) Decision: Record the outcome on the task. Each trigger's outcome follows the trigger table in the window plan, which Josh approved with his go: health or start proof failure, any data loss and a schema verify failure are outcome 3 at once, decided by this session; every other named trigger defaults to outcome 2, decided by this session, unless the table names outcome 3; this session asks Josh only for a trigger not in the table, in its own terminal and keeping its claim, waiting as step 7 does, because escalate_task would release the claim that the landing freeze is bound to (GEN-ROLLBACK). Outcome 1, it works: an approved implementation attestation with the window evidence; tag the commit that step 6 promoted (0.9.0 HEAD at promotion) as port/<checkpoint id>, this cutover's id (for example port/CP-WAVE1-CUT), as an annotated tag whose message lists the SHAs of the prepared, regeneration and activation commits it landed, and push the tag, so that A can adopt this checkpoint when Josh decides, by running these steps on its own install with its main checkout moved to the tag in step 6's place, after its own backup and rehearsal (D40 item 4); clear the freeze and message each session that asked to land, clear the hold, release the pin, and close as done. Outcome 2, it works well enough to debug: fix forward on 0.9.0 with the pin still held, for at most two fix cycles, the last fix landing within 24 hours of the first outcome-2 decision, unless Josh's go set another bound (the clean window after each fix does not count toward the 24 hours); past that bound, outcome 3. Before each fix lands, extend the hold and the pin to the end of a new clean window of this cutover's own length (gobby rollback hold extend and pin extend). Give the fix commit, its version bumps included, the code-reviewer seat, fix and recheck until it passes, then stop it, and link its final SHA to this task, because land_commit lands only a SHA linked to the landing task; then land it under the freeze as the hold's owner, as a shipping commit: like the activation commit, it bumps by 0.0.1 every shipped binary whose fingerprint changed since its last bump, gcode and ghook included, with Cargo.lock, the managed pins and the gcode floor in step (D39); check HEAD and wait for its CI as step 6 does, rerun the restore half of the rehearsal against the new HEAD (the pinned generation's step-9 members, a Python start while Python exists, and one read-back), then promote under the token, with step 2's reads first. A fix that needs a schema step goes to outcome 3 or to Josh. After the clean window that follows the last fix, record the window evidence, tag the last commit this cutover promoted as port/<checkpoint id> the same way and push the tag (D40 item 4), then clear the freeze and message each session that asked to land, clear the hold, release the pin, and close as done. Outcome 3: run the recipe, which for a cut whose schema steps are expand-only is the binary restore plus the deactivation commit, with no backup restore, and for a cut that carries a drop, or CP-WAVE3-CUT once its relocation ran, starts with the backup restore. Keep the task open and escalate to Josh, who reassesses before any retry; close this task only as done, after a retry's clean window, and if Josh abandons the direction, re-plan the downstream edges (the blocks edges and docs/port/map-v2.json's depends_on) before any wont_do close, because any close releases blocks edges. Send one project send_message with wake=true naming the in-flight chunks that depend on this stage's review: they stop at their next checkpoint and land nothing until Josh's reassessment is recorded on this task; send a second one releasing them once that reassessment is recorded. A tag push that fails on a GitHub outage changes no outcome: clear the freeze, the hold and the pin as that outcome says, so that chunk sessions can land, retry the push on each later wake and close this task once it succeeds. On P, after closing as done, this session's final message asks Josh to prompt the port dispatcher, because a cut's close does not wake it (D116), and after CP-TEMPLATE-CUT or CP-WAVE3-CUT to name the cap his go at that cut's review set (D23). (9) Rollback recipe: Precede it with step 2's reads and one global send_message that names the rollback and the generation it restores and tells every session to pause task work until DAEMON BACK; for a backup restore it also says that every live agent seat ends and that every write made after the backup is lost, and it is the only notice before that stop, because gobby stop writes stop intent, for which the daemon sends no DAEMON HOLD; the standing ruling, or until Josh gives one the review packet's default, covers an emergency restore during quiet hours. During them the project's rule refuses gobby stop and gobby cutover in this session and lets gobby rollback restore through (.gobby/workflows/rules/quiet-hours.yaml:15-24): the restore runs at once, the deactivation build's promotion waits for the quiet hours to end with the hold and the pin extended, and a backup restore's gobby stop is Josh's to run from his own shell, which that rule does not reach, or waits for them to end too. An expand step needs no backup restore: the deactivation commit reverts this cut's schema inputs with its activation, so the checkout's schema identity matches the restored generation, and the restored generation starts on the hub's expand-only receipts above its head (D22); no write is lost. Every name in this recipe is install-local (this install's own backup, pin, hold and generations), so A runs it unchanged on its own install if its own adoption of this checkpoint rolls back, with its main checkout moved back to the commit it ran before in place of a deactivation commit (D40 item 4). The pinned target is the generation installed at step 3, CP-TEMPLATE-READS-CUT's last promotion. The restore members are the stamped set, gcode, gdaemon and ghook (gobby rollback restore <generation> --bin gcode,gdaemon,ghook), because this cut's schema inputs change the identity that all three embed.

### TERM-1: Terminal family: WS, inventory, viewports and operator input

- **kind:** family
- **goal:** Wave 1 (the richest oracle in the tree). #23206 M2, landed dormant and activated at CP-WAVE1-CUT: the native terminal WS connection and operation state machine (#24577), terminal inventory reads and HTTP handlers (#24575), the attachment viewports that terminal_set_viewport writes in the Rust lease registry for its sizing, with no viewport route (#24576, below), the bounded proxy relay and frame and lifecycle fanout (#24578), operator input under the route action hold (#24579), and family registration and activation (#24580); the capture_output, send_keys and terminate_terminal descriptors. The gterm host manager and composer ledger stay the single Python owner until TERM-HOST: Rust reaches host effects (spawn, write, resize, capture, terminate) through allow-listed worker ops, so the Python write and runtime clients planned in #24571 and #24574 are not built. #25201 (D21): the Rust write path keeps hub-mode's remote write branch. #24576 closes as superseded by #24797 (the team-lane runbooks it served are retired), and #24577's edge on it is dropped. #24579's test target becomes a Rust test, because #24571's Python client is not built. #24580 runs after R6 (its 2.13.3 restart test) and claims its WS message types through SEAM-WS's registry. Its activation keeps gdaemon handing Python the terminal route value that keeps Python's host manager running (crates/gdaemon/src/state.rs:162-171), because Python skips its host manager when that route is native (src/gobby/runner_init/terminal_wiring.py:63-71); only TERM-HOST's activation moves that value (D19). To keep it there, this chunk separates the two values that terminal_route() carries today (crates/gdaemon/src/front_door/routes.rs:59-75): the terminal family's route backend, whose compiled default this chunk's activation flips at CP-WAVE1-CUT, and a terminal ownership default that feeds RouteLatch, the supervisor mode and GOBBY_TERMINAL_ROUTE (crates/gterminals/src/family.rs:52-67; crates/gdaemon/src/state.rs:162-171), which stays Proxy until TERM-HOST's activation. RouteLatch's registration check keys off the routes the family claims. It also lands one dormant Python helper that both of Python's terminal route reads use (src/gobby/runner_backend.py:83; src/gobby/runner_init/terminal_wiring.py:64-68): it returns GOBBY_TERMINAL_ROUTE when gdaemon set it, and the bootstrap value (default proxy) otherwise, and the start refusal stays only for an explicit bootstrap terminal_ws entry that disagrees with the latched value (src/gobby/runner_backend.py:80-91). It is inert at landing, because gdaemon latches proxy and the bootstrap has no terminal_ws entry (D37). From then on Python follows the route gdaemon latches, so CP-WAVE5-CUT flips only gdaemon's compiled terminal ownership default and a gdaemon-alone restore hands the host back to Python in one restart. If Josh refuses this Python edit, CP-WAVE5-CUT's activation flips both Python reads with gdaemon's default, and its recipe lands the deactivation commit under the freeze, then restores the pinned generation, then promotes the deactivation build under the token (D19). #24573, the Rust runtime route, moved to TERM-HOST, because plan section 2.9 ties it to 2.8's single settler (#24572), which TERM-HOST builds. Its WS operator input (#24579) and its relay (#24578) report each admitted operator write and each output frame to one turn-observer trait in crates/gterminals, whose default does nothing, because Python's observer sees neither once this family is Native (src/gobby/servers/websocket/terminal_input.py:21; src/gobby/servers/websocket/proxy_relay.py:469). AG-3's native observer binds it at CP-WAVE2-CUT's activation (D73). From CP-WAVE1-CUT to CP-WAVE2-CUT a mediated interrupt of an AGY session, the only provider that observer serves (src/gobby/sessions/terminal_turn_observer.py:23), does not end its turn until later evidence arrives, and CP-WAVE1-REVIEW's packet records that. From this chunk's activation Rust's lease registry owns attachments, holders, generations, viewports and write admission, while Python's host manager, composer ledger and write coordinator stay live, so Python's registry holds no WS attachment until CP-WAVE5-CUT. The family builds that registry whenever the terminal route backend is Native, whatever the ownership default says, because with_write_route builds Registry::new and its coordinator only in Owner mode today (crates/gterminals/src/family.rs:103-124); the loopback write route itself stays Owner-only. Its Coordinator takes a Runtime over D103's op in place of NativeWrite and TmuxWrite (:115-120) until TERM-HOST. Only the operator write needs that op: Python's coordinator refuses an operator origin its own registry cannot vouch for (src/gobby/terminals/write_coordinator.py:575-580, 649-669) and returns at once for every other origin, so send_keys and the other host effects call their one-line ops directly and never pass the native Coordinator, which leaves Python's latch and quarantine as the only ones. The spawn op is a one-line registration on spawn_web_terminal (src/gobby/terminals/web_spawn.py:73) with the worker's terminal manager and resolved runtime; it serves terminal_create and TERM-2's pane spawns (src/gobby/servers/websocket/terminal_ws_create.py:48-127; src/gobby/terminals/workspace_ops.py:840). The native registry keeps each attachment's focus flag with Python's rules, which #25653 changed after this map: any live attachment's report holds the wake, lease or not, a displaced or releasing holder's flag clears, as does a finalized attachment's, and the release fires only when no focused attachment remains (src/gobby/terminals/leases.py:144-145, 448-469, 494-498, 519-522, 541-549), and D105's op keeps Python's wake reading it. #25653 removed input grants and the read-only pane mode after this map. The host checks no grant, a pane's keys reach it on the pane's own attachment, no grant_input or revoke_input exists in Python, crates/gterminals or the host protocol, and terminal_take_control carries no host_attachment_id (src/gobby/servers/websocket/terminal_ws_control.py:55-88). So ws.rs applies no grant, plan 2.2's applier text is stale (.gobby/plans/daemon-side-gterm-adoption-and-terminal-ws.md:2374-2385), and this chunk builds no ControlClient::grant_input or revoke_input and keeps no host_attachment_id on the attachment. 2.2's line that leases.rs needs no edit still does not hold, for a new reason: #25653 also removed take_control and release_control from crates/gterminals/src/leases.rs, which now only clears a holder at finalize and still checks a web viewer's write against holder and generation (crates/gterminals/src/leases.rs:462-473, 598-607), so no native path sets a holder. This chunk builds the registry's take and release for terminal_take_control and terminal_release_control with Python's rules (src/gobby/terminals/leases.py:471-529): every daemon WS attach is a web viewer whatever label it sends (src/gobby/servers/websocket/terminal_ws.py:252-261), only a web viewer takes the lease and any other answers not_web_viewer, a take against another holder without takeover answers held, a release by a non-holder answers released, and a write is checked against holder and generation only for a web viewer (src/gobby/terminals/leases.py:630-638). A proxied gclient pane claims the lease with a non-takeover take right after its attach, and a direct pane never claims (crates/gclient/src/frame_source/proxy.rs:59-86). There is one lifecycle sequencer, the family registry. gclient drops a terminal_event from another epoch until its next roster read, and a workspace_event from another epoch with no re-read at all (crates/gclient/src/app/live.rs:297-306; crates/gclient/src/app/workspace_ops.rs:54-60), and Python stamps its own epoch and sequence until CP-WAVE5-CUT (src/gobby/runner_broadcasting.py:97-106; src/gobby/servers/websocket/broadcast.py:476, 603). So while the family is Native the native publish path (crates/gdaemon/src/websocket/publish.rs:117-168) re-stamps each terminal_event and workspace_event frame Python publishes with the registry's epoch and next sequence, and sends it through the same ordered queue as the family's own lifecycle events (crates/gterminals/src/leases.rs:333-365), because gclient drops a sequence at or below its pin (crates/gclient/src/app/live.rs:450-454). A large workspace_event arrives as terminal_ws_fragment frames (src/gobby/servers/websocket/broadcast.py:478-502), so the path reassembles it, stamps it and fragments it again with the new sequence as message_seq (crates/gterminals/src/ws_protocol.rs:202). That path is a project_policy.security_paths entry, so this chunk's landing needs D106's seat. #25201 has two parts. Until TERM-HOST, D103's op carries node terminals as it carries local ones, so Python's _dispatch keeps the branch, its refusals and its ledger record (src/gobby/terminals/write_coordinator.py:763-771, 805-806). For TERM-HOST's activation this chunk builds the Rust branch, dormant because it serves only Owner mode: before the Coordinator resolves a backend's runtime (crates/gterminals/src/write.rs:382), a terminal whose machine_id is another machine goes to a node runtime over a port this crate declares and crates/gdaemon binds to the node registry's command sender (crates/gdaemon/src/nodes/registry.rs:230), with Python's refusals, ledger record, terminal.write payload and stage mapping (src/gobby/hub/remote_terminal.py:23-38; docs/contracts/node-commands.md:220), so such a write never reaches a local runtime. Two Python gates also came after the terminal plan (#24273, #24908) and move here, because a claimed frame no longer reaches Python's message gate (src/gobby/servers/websocket/server.py:499-513) and a worker op binds no caller, so Python's ownership check passes there (src/gobby/terminals/write_coordinator.py:841-854; src/gobby/hub/caller_scope.py:54-69). The WS connection takes its caller and any browser claims from SEAM-CALLERS's Admitted value at the upgrade (#25046; crates/gdaemon/src/front_door/mod.rs:241-261), because the bridge's ready frame carries only admitted and confined (crates/gdaemon/src/websocket/transport.rs:115-128), and that caller fills each Requester (crates/gterminals/src/leases.rs:14-19). A break-glass connection, which Python leaves unbound, takes the nil caller and no ownership check. The first gate is confinement. It sits in SEAM-WS's registry dispatch (D102), so this chunk, TERM-2 and every later claimer (SES-2, CHAT-2, VOICE and MUX-1) pass it: on a confined connection a claimed frame whose type is off Python's allow-list, or whose project or session selector at any depth differs from the signed claims, answers Browser message refused and reaches no handler (src/gobby/servers/browser_sessions.py:90-124). A confined terminal_list lists the claim's project alone, with no client project_id and no global project (src/gobby/servers/websocket/terminal_ws.py:402-407, 431-433). The second gate is machine ownership, with Python's rule that a bound caller with no user owns nothing. terminal_attach checks the row's machine once and refuses with Python's machine_not_owned, machine_not_found and machine_ownership_unavailable (:231-250), terminal_list answers an empty page (:421-429), and a bound caller's send_keys checks the terminal's machine before its write op call and answers as Python's refused write does (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/sessions/_terminal_send_keys.py:221-229; src/gobby/terminals/write_coordinator.py:796-838). D103's operator write takes no check, because its attachment vouches for it as Python's lease does (src/gobby/terminals/write_coordinator.py:773-794), and capture_output and terminate_terminal have none in Python. #25338 also came after the plan. send_keys passes a target gate before its write: it refuses a bare shell, a process that is no agent CLI, a composer that is not idle, a credential prompt and an unreadable pane, failing closed, and drains a held composer for a clear key (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/sessions/_terminal_send_keys_gate.py:225-252, 274-365). The gate reads the composer ledger, the detection registry and a pane snapshot, which stay Python's until TERM-HOST. #25901 and #25917 came after this map: the gate now confirms the foreground process by identity, not by name, reading the target session's recorded process (terminal_context), the terminal's foreground group, and the installed build that the worker's PATH resolves for each agent CLI (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/sessions/_terminal_send_keys_gate.py:109-131, 134-161, 225-252), which also stay Python's. So the native send_keys makes Python's first checks itself (the idempotency key, the caller and target, the speed command; src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/sessions/_terminal_send_keys.py:280-302), calls a one-line op on send_keys_target_refusal, bound to the worker's terminal manager and runtime registry (D4), whose request carries the session id, the clear flag and the target session row's terminal_context, which the function has taken since #25901 (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/sessions/_terminal_send_keys_gate.py:274-281; src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/sessions/_terminal_send_keys.py:164-171), answers its refusal or cleared result as _deliver does (:164-181), and only then makes its ownership check and write op call. A failed call or a lost reply answers send_keys_target_unconfirmed with no write, as the gate fails closed (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/sessions/_terminal_send_keys_gate.py:361-364). send_wake (#25720) came after this map's ledger; its row has since landed (docs/contracts/parity-ledger.md:906), and this chunk's selector names it. It types one fixed line and takes the same gate and write with no clear key, after its caller and target checks and the target's message_sender_capabilities admission, which it asks through a one-line op on recipient_policy, bound to the worker's database (D4), until CP-WAVE2-CUT's activation commit re-binds it to AG-3's native admission, refusing a withheld target as Python does (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/sessions/_terminal_send_keys.py:53-113, 130-142, 325-344; src/gobby/agents/team_communications.py:80). The write op's reply reads Delivered, Suppressed or AutomaticWriteQuarantined by its _type, and IndeterminateWrite as an unknown outcome that is never retried, as D103 reads a lost reply (src/gobby/terminals/runtime.py:137-142, 168). Two changes to Python's side of this chunk came after this map. #25575: a workspace_event now reaches the native publish endpoint as frames beside a routing filter that carries the event's scalar fields without workspace, tabs and panes; a small event is one frame, a large one its terminal_ws_fragment frames, and one above the reassembly limit a single frame with its rows emptied (src/gobby/servers/websocket/broadcast.py:478-516). A publish call splits into ops of at most 4 MiB, the filter repeated in each and a larger frame alone in its own op, and the sender posts at most 1 MiB of ops per request, a larger op alone (src/gobby/servers/websocket/native_publish.py:37-42, 231-253, 452-466, 692-716). So one event's fragments can arrive across several publish ops and several requests, the re-stamp path's reassembly holds across them in arrival order, and it reads the rows from the frames, never from the filter. #25924: capture_output answers dropped_bytes and total_bytes as null when the host's snapshot reply carries no integer for them, where it answered 0 and the text's byte length (src/gobby/terminals/native_runtime.py:476-485; src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/sessions/_terminal.py:766-773).

A workspace_event published as fragments reassembles at the client to the stamped event. The lease rules replay Python's cases natively: a take from an attachment that is not a web viewer answers not_web_viewer, an attach with no viewer label is a web viewer and takes the lease, a viewer label sent on the daemon WS types only under the lease, and an attachment that is not a web viewer writes without the lease (tests/terminals/test_lease_authority.py:96, 106; tests/servers/test_terminal_ws_input.py:526; tests/terminals/test_write_coordinator.py:603). #25201: with an Owner-mode coordinator and a node-command double, a write to a terminal on another machine sends terminal.write with Python's payload and reaches no local runtime, a refusal with a delivery stage and one with no stage map as src/gobby/hub/remote_terminal.py:23-38 maps them, and a local terminal takes its backend's runtime; with D103's runtime a node terminal's operator write calls the op like a local one. Ownership: a caller that does not own the machine gets Python's terminal_attach refusals and an empty terminal_list page (tests/servers/test_terminal_ws_input.py:457, 481; tests/servers/test_terminal_ws_list.py:343), a bound caller's send_keys to that machine is refused with no write op call (tests/hub/test_remote_terminal_write.py:210, 325), and a break-glass connection and an attachment's own write pass. Each gate outcome replays Python's code with no write op call: a refusal, a cleared result and a failed or lost gate call (tests/mcp_proxy/tools/sessions/test_terminal_send_keys_gate.py). send_wake refuses an unadmitted holder and a gate refusal with nothing typed (tests/mcp_proxy/test_sessions_terminal_tools.py:394, 431).
