The native drain, quarantine retention, receipt prune and hook-effect retirement jobs register on R4's registry, and the startup pass in R3's recovery order, all only while the family is active (D37), in place of Python's one-iteration ops and its drain entry point. HOOK-2's handoff dispatch recovery takes R3's handoffs slot, in place of Python's handoff recovery entry point, only while the compiled terminal ownership default is Native (D75). Its retention jobs register through R4's registry. The Codex thread-host prune registers with the other two session-expiry steps. The claim's tables are session_startup_marks' cli_pid and cli_create_time pins and codex_thread_hosts (migration 495_session_startup_pins.sql).
- **risks:** The hottest path in the daemon: it goes live only at CP-WAVE4-CUT, whose 12-hour window opens with the five-CLI smoke (Claude Code, Codex, Droid, Grok and AGY). A Python drain op left beside the native drain would deliver spooled envelopes twice: the swap is one registration on R4's registry, which never fires both schedulers, and per-file claims cover the restart between them (3.5.2). Hold-open is the one long path through the route: a web chat wait holds its response and lease for up to 300 seconds, as Python's does, and a Telegram ask holds one worker-op call for up to 110, which R0's concurrent domain ops carry without holding up any other op.

### PIPE-1: PIPE-1: pipeline definitions and the engine dry-run

- **kind:** family
- **goal:** #21567's definition half, and #25279's plan is this brief's first deliverable. Pipeline definition storage and CRUD, import, export, templates, duplicate, move and restore routes and the six definition tools in a new pipelines crate, plus the pipeline engine dry-run that the bundled-YAML validity test lacks (bundled agent definitions are already validated through AgentDefinitionBody and gobby agents check, which TPL ports). It starts after CP-WAVE3-REVIEW, whose resizing covers waves 4-5. The compact workflow-instance prune that #25279 was asked to absorb (src/gobby/storage/session_lifecycle.py:303, run from src/gobby/sessions/lifecycle.py:323-327) is this chunk's job on R4's registry at CP-WAVE4-CUT's activation, in place of Python's op, and S3-DELETE deletes the op (D14). Its #25279 work replaces the statements of SES-3B's transitional workflow_audit_log and agent_step_instances adapters with the workflows crate's reads and writes, behavior unchanged, so CP-WAVE4-CUT's promotion carries the change. PIPE-1 also owns the startup import of landed files, the native port of src/gobby/workflows/imports.py, because it is the last chunk whose code that import needs (D83). On every hub or standalone start, in dev and installed mode alike (src/gobby/runner_init/storage.py:80-82), after TPL's sync in R2's content phase, the import reads the rules, agents, pipelines and variables directories of the global workflows root (~/.gobby/workflows, src/gobby/paths.py:419) and of every registered project's main checkout (.gobby/workflows, with a linked worktree resolved to its main checkout and CHECKOUT_FREE_PROJECT_IDS excluded, imports.py:279-282, 285-356; src/gobby/storage/project_checkouts.py:379-396), and upserts each definition with Python's checks: the split between a rule file in the gobby rules import format and a single-definition file, validate_workflow_definition_data, the override conflict, validate_registry_regexes, the kind-change refusal, the reserved gobby pipeline tag, the bundled tag's preservation and the project-import tag (imports.py:56-79, 89-276, 359-389). A rule also goes through RULE-2's validate_rule dry run and lookaround refusal (D33) and TPL's persist preparation, so a rule file that either refuses is logged and skipped and its prior row stays. Each write advances its domain's revision and notifies as Python's writes do (src/gobby/storage/definitions/_shared.py:151). A malformed file is logged and skipped, never fails the start, and marks that scan incomplete; an orphan retires only after a complete scan of an available checkout, and an unavailable checkout is skipped and retires nothing (imports.py:285-356). The import's compiled default stays off until CP-WAVE4-CUT's activation commit, which also makes R2's content phase send startup_content with import_landed false, so exactly one importer runs at each start (D37). Until then Python's import keeps running in that phase, beside TPL's native sync and, from CP-WAVE3-CUT, RULE-2's native rule writes. The startup migrate_rule_delivery_dispositions (src/gobby/runner_init/storage.py:86) needs no port, because TPL's sync, RULE-2's writers and this import all prepare the rows they write; it stays in the worker's phase until CP-PREDELETE-CUT's commit A stops starting the worker. PIPE-1 also serves the gobby-workflows reload_cache tool and POST /api/admin/workflows/reload (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/workflows/_import.py:13-81; src/gobby/servers/routes/admin/_lifecycle.py:340-379), which flip at CP-WAVE4-CUT: this import, scoped by the call's project_path or project_id, then TPL's sync for Python's kind filter (_RELOAD_ONLY), with the same result keys, detection_manifests_reloaded among them, and the same refusal on a delivery-disposition error. Neither surface needs a worker op, because Python's loader clears on the revision notification (src/gobby/workflows/pipeline_loader.py:45-61) and its detection registry refreshes on its staleness clock (src/gobby/agents/detection/registry.py:189-192). The import's single-file entry also serves V5A's gobby rules import.

### PIPE-2: PIPE-2: pipeline executor, executions and approvals

- **kind:** family
- **goal:** #21567's execution half: run, status and step status, executions and search, approve and reject by token, resume, cancel, fail, evaluate, pipeline_eval and clear history; the executor with agent steps on AG-1 and AG-2 and MCP steps on GW-1's per-tool routing. Once PIPE-2 activates (CP-WAVE4-CUT), CRON no longer calls its pipeline-dispatch worker op, which S3-DELETE deletes. Its wait steps wait on AG-2's native completion waiters, never on Python's registry (src/gobby/workflows/pipeline_executor_steps.py:144-176). Its execution completions notify those waiters, and its agent steps end runs through AG-2's termination service (D71). An execution's completion also delivers that execution's durable completion_subscribers rows, as Python's executor does through its registry (src/gobby/workflows/pipeline_executor_events.py:73): each subscriber gets the persisted completion notification and a wake through AG-3's wake path, which reaches Python's dispatcher through AG-3's live-wake ops until CP-WAVE5-CUT, and the delivered rows are removed. Python's registry never registers an execution this chunk runs, so each row keeps one owner, the runtime that ran the execution (D19). Approval-timeout expiry (src/gobby/runner_maintenance/storage_hygiene.py:168, every 60 seconds) and SystemAutomationLoop's pipeline maintenance (src/gobby/system_automation.py:209-221: the stalled execution, stale task and running count passes of src/gobby/workflows/pipeline_heartbeat.py:98, :239, :292) are this chunk's jobs on R4's registry at CP-WAVE4-CUT's activation, in place of Python's ops, and S3-DELETE deletes the ops (D14). PIPE-2 also replaces the statement of SES-3B's transitional pipeline-execution adapter, which GET /api/sessions' resumability reads (src/gobby/servers/routes/sessions/core.py:157-233), with the pipelines crate's read, behavior unchanged, so CP-WAVE4-CUT's promotion carries the change. Restart recovery is this chunk's too. Python's (src/gobby/runner_lifecycle_subsystems.py:351-451, called at :750 as a hub-only phase) stays in R3's order until CP-WAVE4-CUT's activation, when this chunk's native recovery takes that slot and Rust stops calling Python's entry point, so one restart never runs both and an interrupted execution's subscribers are woken once. It is hub-only and declares itself once per process in R3's order, because native executions outlive a backend respawn, and a pass on a respawn would resume or interrupt executions that are still running; Python's may run on every start only because its executions die with its process. With the cutoff at this gdaemon process's start, it resumes RUNNING executions with resume_on_restart (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/workflows/_pipeline_execution.py:735), interrupts the other stale ones (src/gobby/runner_lifecycle_subsystems.py:416) and gives each durable subscriber of each interrupted execution created before the cutoff Python's interrupted notification (:456-511), through the delivery its completions use, which removes the rows. The first native pass, at CP-WAVE4-CUT's restart, recovers what the last Python generation left. AG-WAIT's take-over at CP-WAVE5-CUT covers this wake. The bundled expand-task pipeline's wait step waits on an expansion run id (src/gobby/install/shared/workflows/pipelines/expand-task.yaml:72-75), and PLANS' native run notifies only Python's registry until CP-WAVE5-CUT (D71). So this chunk's wait step passes AG-2's waiter a durable read that answers agent_runs rows through gagents, its own execution rows, and expansion run rows through PLANS' run outcome read. The step's output is the result Python's helpers notify for that status (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/tasks/_expansion_runtime.py:280-323; src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/tasks/_expansion_registry.py:598-603), because the pipeline's later steps read its status and error (expand-task.yaml:85, 90). An id with no row in any of the three fails the step at once, as Python's registry does (src/gobby/events/completion_registry.py:240-242). Each step runs under SEAM-CALLERS' daemon-owned execution with no request principal and its pipeline execution id, as src/gobby/workflows/pipeline/handlers.py:20-22, 66-72 does (#25416), and a step's tool that is still Python's reaches GW-2's compatibility endpoint with that scope (D121). Cancel keeps _require_pipeline_cancel_owned's caller check before the first write or kill (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/workflows/_pipeline_execution.py:234-254, 299). A guard refusal's WARNING carries the pipeline_guard_refused field, as src/gobby/workflows/pipeline_executor.py:829-833 does, which keeps it out of errors.log (SEAM-FAMILY). Pipeline webhooks (src/gobby/workflows/pipeline_webhooks.py:23-169; src/gobby/workflows/pipeline/gatekeeper.py:135; src/gobby/workflows/pipeline_executor.py:779, 871) call HOOK-3's webhook transport with private addresses refused (D124). The render context keeps Python's environment filter: sensitive names and underscore-delimited segments are withheld, case-insensitively, an allow list admits only its keys, and the database credential names stay withheld even when listed (src/gobby/workflows/pipeline/renderer.py:47-98, 142). The project_file_exists helper refuses an absolute path and any path whose resolved target leaves the checkout (src/gobby/workflows/pipeline/renderer.py:33-43).

- **kind:** family

Stage 4 builds the node side against these. Its POST /api/nodes/checkouts handler calls PROJ-2's native checkout registration service with the Projects plan's 4.5.5 contract: hub-only, the machine derived from the verified node key, any body or header machine identity refused, and the node listener refusing the route locally (.gobby/plans/gdaemon-projects-files-docs-family.md 4.5). That plan's transfer of the row to Projects (4.5.5, 6.3.5) is not followed (D11). #25269's third part, the run reconciler (src/gobby/hub/remote_reconcile.py::RemoteRunReconciler) with the node report inbox it drains (src/gobby/hub/node_reports.py:54-127), is built here too, and remote idle here means the reported idle facts this store serves (src/gobby/agents/idle_check_handler.py:276-293), on which AG-2's native idle check decides. POST /api/nodes/report and POST /api/nodes/runs/terminate write the store (src/gobby/hub/remote_pane.py:227-244; src/gobby/servers/routes/node_runs.py:278-331), so they activate with the store, the inbox and the reconciler at CP-WAVE5-CUT, not CP-WAVE4-CUT, behind a compiled reported-pane default that only those two routes' claims, the reconciler's job and the pane-read binding read (D37). Python's host and wake paths read the store in-process until then (src/gobby/hub/remote_runtime.py:32-58; src/gobby/events/wake.py:748-797), and single-owner state moves after its last Python in-process reader (D19). At that activation the reconciler swaps AG-2's reconcile op on R4's registry, the store serves AG-2's idle reads and TERM-HOST's node terminal reads, and AG-2's two store-read ops are no longer called; S3-DELETE deletes all three ops. From CP-WAVE5-CUT its report route's attention episodes go to AG-3's native attention family, which activates in the same commit (D72). Its three POST /api/nodes/runs routes admit only a verified node identity, as Python's _node_machine does: 403 node_identity_required without one and 403 machine_is_local for the hub's own machine. They read the caller machine from SEAM-CALLERS' bound Admitted value (#25046; agents-family Decision 11). Its run-outcome routes are run writes over the agents family's services (agents-family Decision 14). POST /api/nodes/runs/prompt-delivery-failure, native from CP-WAVE4-CUT, runs the run's failure transition and cleanup (src/gobby/servers/routes/node_runs.py:210-248) through AG-2's termination service, which hands the run to AG-1's deliver_completion (D71), and so do the terminate route and the native reconciler from CP-WAVE5-CUT. POST /api/nodes/runs/code-index-warning (:250-276) merges its warning variable through SES-2's variable service. The report route reaches the family's run records through two gagents exports that this chunk adds, record_remote_workspaces and apply_sandbox_records (src/gobby/hub/node_reports.py:130; src/gobby/hub/remote_sandbox.py:42; src/gobby/servers/routes/nodes.py:217, 224). Every node-supplied text passes through AG-1's redact_terminal_output before anything keeps it, except a report's fingerprint, and a secret-shaped identity is refused (src/gobby/hub/remote_pane.py:150-165; src/gobby/hub/remote_sandbox.py:22-38; src/gobby/hub/node_commands.py:52; src/gobby/servers/routes/node_runs.py:214-216, 282-283; .gobby/plans/node-halves.md Decision 34; D124). The report and checkout routes read the body as a stream up to node_reports.max_request_bytes, 8 MiB by default, and answer 413 with detail report_too_large or checkout_too_large past it, a chunked body included, not axum's 2 MiB default, and a body with the wrong contract version answers 422 unsupported_version (src/gobby/servers/routes/nodes.py:71-93, 178-192; src/gobby/config/node_reports.py). Every packet opens with a summary of at most one screen: what changed since the previous review, what needs Josh's call, and any check that did not pass. Every packet also carries the cutover plan for CP-WAVE4-CUT: the window length and the named triggers; the trigger table, which gives each trigger its default outcome (2 or 3) and who decides; the fix-forward bound (at most two fix cycles, the last fix landing within 24 hours of the first outcome-2 decision, each followed by its own clean window, then outcome 3), which Josh may change in his go; the pinned generation (the one installed when the cutover sets its hold) and the restore members; the recipe; and the loss window: the writes made after the backup, through the rehearsal and the window, which only a backup restore would lose (a drop, or CP-WAVE3-CUT's relocation once it ran; an expand-only rollback loses none, D22), plus every live agent seat's credentials if the recipe restores the backup. On no-go: de_escalate_task(reason='NO-GO from Josh ...: <his words>'). Keep the task open. Link the fixes Josh names with add_dependency(task_id=<review>, depends_on=<fix>). File any new filing as a child of #21542, so the port dispatcher starts it, and label it operator-directed, which the found-work gate exempts (src/gobby/install/shared/workflows/rules/stop-gates/enforce-found-work-ladder.yaml:67). A no-go holds no claim, because escalate_task released it, so this session ends its turn with the task open and its blockers linked, and its final message asks Josh to prompt the port dispatcher, which starts the fixes (D116). When they close, the task shows ready again, the dispatcher names it in its final message, and Josh prompts this session or opens a new one, which claims it, builds a new packet and escalates again. Never close a no-go. If Josh abandons the direction, re-plan the downstream edges before any wont_do close, because that close releases them too.

Triggers: any smoke step failing; a hook decision that differs from the decision corpus or from the known-bad registry's correct value; a hook and tool-call pair out of FIFO order; hook latency above the bound in the window plan; a pipeline run lost, run twice or stuck; a team admission that differs; the live node's reports or commands failing; health or start proof failure. Further triggers: a pipeline wait step that misses or doubles an agent run's or a pipeline execution's completion, and a durable subscriber of a native pipeline execution woken twice or not at all (D71). Further trigger: a stored rule row the native cache skips because the regex crate rejects its pattern, because a skipped block rule fails open (D33). The smoke also opens one managed and one AGY web chat session and runs a tool call and a stop in each, whose lifecycle passes now run natively (D81); a web chat lifecycle decision that differs from the recorded Python pass is also a trigger. Further triggers: a spooled envelope delivered twice or left undelivered, a quarantine file or receipt kept past Python's age, a staged handoff delivered twice or never after a restart, and a missing rule-allow-audit.jsonl line. Hold-open triggers: an attached Telegram question that no longer reaches Telegram or whose answer does not reach the terminal, and a web chat tool approval that a browser response does not resolve (s2-11 5.12). Job triggers: a job this activation swapped in that misses its cadence, errors on every fire, or deletes or changes a row its Python op would keep. A session message, usage update or token event lost, doubled or out of order after the processor starts, an assistant text block mirrored to an attached Telegram conversation out of order, twice or not at all, and a staged handoff delivered twice or left undelivered, are also triggers. It includes a deliberate plain gobby restart with a native pipeline execution running, which must keep running. Further triggers: a native execution interrupted or resumed by a backend respawn; an interrupted execution's subscriber woken twice or not at all. A pipeline wait step that misses or doubles an expansion run's completion is a trigger too (D71). One more trigger: a valid file landed under .gobby/workflows or ~/.gobby/workflows that a restart leaves off its row, or a malformed or refused one that stops a start (D83). (8) Decision: Record the outcome on the task. Each trigger's outcome follows the trigger table in the window plan, which Josh approved with his go: health or start proof failure, any data loss and a schema verify failure are outcome 3 at once, decided by this session; every other named trigger defaults to outcome 2, decided by this session, unless the table names outcome 3; this session asks Josh only for a trigger not in the table, in its own terminal and keeping its claim, waiting as step 7 does, because escalate_task would release the claim that the landing freeze is bound to (GEN-ROLLBACK). Outcome 1, it works: an approved implementation attestation with the window evidence; tag the commit that step 6 promoted (0.9.0 HEAD at promotion) as port/<checkpoint id>, this cutover's id (for example port/CP-WAVE1-CUT), as an annotated tag whose message lists the SHAs of the prepared, regeneration and activation commits it landed, and push the tag, so that A can adopt this checkpoint when Josh decides, by running these steps on its own install with its main checkout moved to the tag in step 6's place, after its own backup and rehearsal (D40 item 4); clear the freeze and message each session that asked to land, clear the hold, release the pin, and close as done. Outcome 2, it works well enough to debug: fix forward on 0.9.0 with the pin still held, for at most two fix cycles, the last fix landing within 24 hours of the first outcome-2 decision, unless Josh's go set another bound (the clean window after each fix does not count toward the 24 hours); past that bound, outcome 3. Before each fix lands, extend the hold and the pin to the end of a new clean window of this cutover's own length (gobby rollback hold extend and pin extend). Give the fix commit, its version bumps included, the code-reviewer seat, fix and recheck until it passes, then stop it, and link its final SHA to this task, because land_commit lands only a SHA linked to the landing task; then land it under the freeze as the hold's owner, as a shipping commit: like the activation commit, it bumps by 0.0.1 every shipped binary whose fingerprint changed since its last bump, gcode and ghook included, with Cargo.lock, the managed pins and the gcode floor in step (D39); check HEAD and wait for its CI as step 6 does, rerun the restore half of the rehearsal against the new HEAD (the pinned generation's step-9 members, a Python start while Python exists, and one read-back), then promote under the token, with step 2's reads first. A fix that needs a schema step goes to outcome 3 or to Josh. After the clean window that follows the last fix, record the window evidence, tag the last commit this cutover promoted as port/<checkpoint id> the same way and push the tag (D40 item 4), then clear the freeze and message each session that asked to land, clear the hold, release the pin, and close as done. Outcome 3: run the recipe, which for a cut whose schema steps are expand-only is the binary restore plus the deactivation commit, with no backup restore, and for a cut that carries a drop, or CP-WAVE3-CUT once its relocation ran, starts with the backup restore. Keep the task open and escalate to Josh, who reassesses before any retry; close this task only as done, after a retry's clean window, and if Josh abandons the direction, re-plan the downstream edges (the blocks edges and docs/port/map-v2.json's depends_on) before any wont_do close, because any close releases blocks edges. Send one project send_message with wake=true naming the in-flight chunks that depend on this stage's review: they stop at their next checkpoint and land nothing until Josh's reassessment is recorded on this task; send a second one releasing them once that reassessment is recorded. A tag push that fails on a GitHub outage changes no outcome: clear the freeze, the hold and the pin as that outcome says, so that chunk sessions can land, retry the push on each later wake and close this task once it succeeds. On P, after closing as done, this session's final message asks Josh to prompt the port dispatcher, because a cut's close does not wake it (D116), and after CP-TEMPLATE-CUT or CP-WAVE3-CUT to name the cap his go at that cut's review set (D23). (9) Rollback recipe: Precede it with step 2's reads and one global send_message that names the rollback and the generation it restores and tells every session to pause task work until DAEMON BACK; for a backup restore it also says that every live agent seat ends and that every write made after the backup is lost, and it is the only notice before that stop, because gobby stop writes stop intent, for which the daemon sends no DAEMON HOLD; the standing ruling, or until Josh gives one the review packet's default, covers an emergency restore during quiet hours. During them the project's rule refuses gobby stop and gobby cutover in this session and lets gobby rollback restore through (.gobby/workflows/rules/quiet-hours.yaml:15-24): the restore runs at once, the deactivation build's promotion waits for the quiet hours to end with the hold and the pin extended, and a backup restore's gobby stop is Josh's to run from his own shell, which that rule does not reach, or waits for them to end too. An expand step needs no backup restore: the deactivation commit reverts this cut's schema inputs with its activation, so the checkout's schema identity matches the restored generation, and the restored generation starts on the hub's expand-only receipts above its head (D22); no write is lost. A drop, or CP-WAVE3-CUT's attachment relocation once it ran, is undone only by the backup restore: before it, end every live agent seat, because the restore drains every restored managed principal and a seat started after the backup has no row in the restored data (src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/cli.py:341; src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/_stores.py:266-269); restore the verified backup with the daemon stopped, before the generation restore below, and relaunch the seats once the restored daemon is healthy; every write made after the backup is lost. Run gobby rollback restore <pinned generation> --bin <members> --hold-token <token> with the members this cutover names, gdaemon alone by default, except that after a schema step (an expand, a drop or a schema-carrying pick) the members always include the stamped set, gcode, gdaemon and ghook, whatever this cut's own line below names: a partial promotion refuses a member whose identity differs from the installed stamp (src/gobby/install/bin_set_coherence.py:97-109, 231-254), start refuses a mixed set (src/gobby/storage/schema_divergence.py:113-157), and gcode and ghook refuse grants minted under another identity (crates/gcore/src/grant/bundle.rs:346-352). Otherwise restore the full set only when gcode or ghook itself broke, because gcode below the checkout floor breaks the code-index gateway (src/gobby/code_index/gcode_gateway.py:831-832). After a stamped-set restore, the code-index gateway refuses the restored gcode until the deactivation build is promoted, because that gcode is below the checkout's gcode pin (src/gobby/code_index/gcode_gateway.py:831-832; src/gobby/code_index/gcode_versions.py:5). The restore burns the activated versions, never the restored target's own. Promote the deactivation build only as step 5 proved it: when a trigger implicates a dormant landing rather than this stage's defaults, stay on the restored generation with the pin and the hold extended, add a revert of that landing to the deactivation commit first, and rerun step 5's deactivation proof on the changed commit. Then give the prepared deactivation commit fresh version bumps, first rebasing it onto 0.9.0 HEAD if an outcome-2 fix or another landing has moved HEAD past the commit it was built on, because land_commit refuses a candidate that shares a changed path with a moved tip and escalates its task (step 3), and every fix commit changes the version lines that this commit bumps. Rerun the code-reviewer seat and step 5's deactivation proof on what the rebase, the bumps and any added revert changed, and link the commit's final SHA to this task, because land_commit lands only a SHA linked to the landing task and step 3 links no deactivation commit. Then land it under the freeze as the hold's owner, which fast-forwards 0.9.0, check HEAD, and promote it under the token. Then clear the freeze, the hold and the pin, and message each session that asked to land that the freeze is clear, saying whether it is among the chunks that outcome 3 stops. Every name in this recipe is install-local (this install's own backup, pin, hold and generations), so A runs it unchanged on its own install if its own adoption of this checkpoint rolls back, with its main checkout moved back to the commit it ran before in place of a deactivation commit (D40 item 4). The pinned target is the generation installed at step 3, CP-WAVE3-CUT's last promotion. The restore members are gdaemon alone. Restoring it puts hook ingress and the rule pass back in Python together, as D27 requires. The restore also returns the message processor to Python: R5 starts Python's SessionMessageProcessor again, which re-registers the live sessions and restores each tail from the shared sidecar. Handoff delivery returns to Python's post-tool hook with it.

### TERM-HOST: Terminal host: Rust becomes the single owner

- **kind:** switch
- **goal:** Wave 5 (callers before callees). After the last Python in-process callers of the host are native (agent spawn, pipelines, cron, rules, hook ingress, teams, wake delivery, handoff delivery, chat, release_composer), Rust takes the gterm host manager: host lifecycle and ownership (host_lifecycle.py, terminal_ownership.py), the native composer ledger (#24571, plan #25276), the reconcile settler and host exit proof (#24572), settlement branches and pane binding (#24574); terminal processes survive an ordinary restart (R6). Once it activates (CP-WAVE5-CUT), no terminal worker op (TERM-1, SES-2, AG-3, CHAT-2) is called, and S3-DELETE deletes them. Its activation switch is the compiled terminal ownership default that TERM-1 separated from the terminal routes' backend: it flips to Native, which moves RouteLatch to Owner and GOBBY_TERMINAL_ROUTE to native, and Python follows the latched value through TERM-1's helper (D19). Owns the native terminal default-flip gate row and replaces guard set G's host checks with a Rust test gate. It also builds #24573, moved here from TERM-1. Plan section 2.9 (.gobby/plans/daemon-side-gterm-adoption-and-terminal-ws.md) keeps 2.8's settler (#24572) as the only settler, with the runtime reporting the prepared spawns it holds through Effects::holds, and the route it plans serves Python's spawn, read and termination callers in Native through a Python runtime client that is not built (#24574, D4). So 2.9's operations (spawn prepare, commit and fail, settled once through that settler; observer reservations; snapshot, full snapshot, history, liveness, session presence, spawn refusal and attach locator reads; terminate and resize on the row's current host epoch) become the native host's in-process terminal runtime for its native callers, proven by 2.9.1-2.9.3's tests, and 2.9.4's HTTP path (POST /api/internal/terminals/runtime) is not built, because no caller outside the daemon remains. From this chunk's activation, node terminals' tails, composer states and stopped marks come from NODEHUB's reported pane store, which moves at the same activation (D19), so nothing calls Python's remote runtime (src/gobby/hub/remote_runtime.py) afterwards. From its activation, its composer ledger and action hold (crates/gterminals/src/write_api.rs) serve AG-2's watchdog composer calls and reprompts in process, so AG-2's three composer ops and D74's reprompt op are no longer called. It also binds the host effects of AG-3's native wake decision on AttentionHost: the composer lock to that action hold, the activity read to its ledger, the lease focus hold to its lease registry, a local wake write to crates/gterminals/src/write/wake_dispatch.rs::dispatch_wake, and a node terminal's composer to NODEHUB's store. So the native decision replaces Python's dispatcher, and AG-3's live-wake ops are no longer called. Its terminal exit cleanup ends an agent run as src/gobby/agents/terminal_cleanup.py:105 does: it delivers to the parent and calls AG-1's deliver_completion, which AG-WAIT's native service serves from the same activation (D71). The transitions from its exit cleanup and its composer attention go to AG-3's native attention family, which activates at the same time (D72). It also binds AG-3's AttentionHost (crates/gdaemon/src/attention_host.rs) to the native host at the same activation: capture to #24573's runtime snapshot, and local write to gterminals' Coordinator::write with Origin::Attention and action key attention-respond:<attention_id> (S2.7 3.4), so respond's local delivery serves natively with the attention family (D72). The native host's output reader reports each run's output to TERM-1's turn-observer seam, as Python's PTY output callback does (src/gobby/runner_broadcasting.py:148-152; D73). HOOK-2's composer-ledger worker ops and D75's handoff delivery op are terminal worker ops too, so from this activation they are not called either: the hook handlers' terminals seam group binds to the native host (s2-11 7.5). Python's terminal loops stop with Python's host manager when this chunk's route value flips at CP-WAVE5-CUT, and the native host's own tasks replace them: the host event reader (src/gobby/terminals/host_event_reader.py:100), the host health loop (src/gobby/terminals/host_manager.py:880), lease publication (src/gobby/terminals/leases.py:292), and the host and frame clients (src/gobby/terminals/host_client.py:323, src/gobby/terminals/frame_client.py:535). It also builds the session liveness job on R4's registry, which no family plan names (src/gobby/sessions/liveness_monitor.py:138-227, 383-481: every 30 seconds on this machine's rows, a session whose terminal exited or whose foreground owner is gone expires conditionally through SES-2's status services, then its hook effects retire through HOOK-3's receipt store, its terminal row is released or marked exited, its summaries dispatch through SES-3B and its processor registration ends). Its tmux branch goes with #25486, so the job reads only native terminals and foreground ownership. Python's in-process suppression (mark_recently_handled, called from the session_end hook, src/gobby/hooks/event_handlers/_session_end.py:82-84) becomes a check on the row: the job skips a session whose updated_at is younger than Python's _RECENTLY_HANDLED_TTL, because HOOK-2's native session end writes that row. Python's lifespan service serves until CP-WAVE5-CUT's activation registers the job (D98), and S3-DELETE deletes the Python monitor (D14). That exit cleanup also runs AG-2's sandbox reap, in the srt_reap and sandbox_reap phases Python's has (src/gobby/agents/terminal_cleanup.py:157-171), so no Python reap remains after CP-WAVE5-CUT. Its action hold (crates/gterminals/src/hold.rs) also binds the composer lock effect of HOOK-2's handoff delivery services, held across each ladder's reads and writes, and at this activation HOOK-3's composition starts those services in place of Python's delivery, with their dispatch recovery in R3's handoffs slot and their shutdown pass in the ordered stop (D75). A hold lapses 10 seconds after its last step (crates/gterminals/src/hold.rs:15), and a ladder waits longer than that between steps (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/sessions/_terminal_compaction.py:382-405), so this chunk adds a renewal to ActionGate that the ladder adapter calls at each read and each poll of a wait; a holder that dies still lapses in 10 seconds. A reprompt or wake adapter that meets a ladder's hold waits at acquire_action for up to the route's 30 seconds (crates/gterminals/src/write_api.rs:505-568), and a wake batch that finds another of its targets held refuses at once (:718-746). Either then reports not delivered, as a blocked wake does (src/gobby/events/wake.py:869-878): the durable message stays queued, and the watchdog's next pass repeats a reprompt (src/gobby/agents/watchdog/recovery.py:396-397). Operator input is not under Python's lock (src/gobby/terminals/composer_lock.py), and natively it queues behind a hold (.gobby/plans/daemon-side-gterm-adoption-and-terminal-ws.md 2.4 and 2.12), so input typed during a ladder waits for its release, and new input gets the explicit error frame once the oldest queued item has waited 30 seconds (crates/gterminals/src/hold.rs:134-151), a known difference that CP-WAVE5-REVIEW's packet carries. TERM-2's two in-flight ops and D103's, D105's and D110's ops are terminal worker ops too. From this activation every pane reservation is native, native writes reach the host through this chunk's Coordinator, the focus hold reads its registry and a hub-local launch spawns on this chunk's host, so none of them is called, and S3-DELETE deletes them. TERM-1's node write branch (#25201) goes live with Owner mode, so a write to a terminal on another machine stays off this host. It also ports send_keys_target_refusal (#25338) over its composer ledger, #24573's snapshot and the provider detection manifests (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/sessions/_terminal_send_keys_gate.py:274-365; crates/gdaemon/src/pane_detection/mod.rs:121), so send_keys and send_wake stop calling TERM-1's gate op at this activation. The Rust test gate is crates/gterminals/tests/host_guard.sh, because one test binary cannot see the hosts another leaks. It lists gterm host processes by their --socket-dir as src/gobby/guard_set_g.py:72-102 does, runs the command it is given, by default cargo nextest run -p gobby-terminals, with TMPDIR set to a fresh short run root (a Unix socket path is limited to 104 bytes, src/gobby/guard_set_g.py:43-45), and then applies the rule of src/gobby/guard_set_g.py:207-238 and tests/terminals/conftest.py:66-80: a host still under the run root is a leak, which it ends, reports with its pid and socket directory and fails on, and a host under the gobby home that was in the first listing and has ended also fails. It replaces only the host checks of guard set G's groups 2, 3 and 7; src/gobby/guard_set_g.py stays until S3-DELETE, whose Terminal Acceptance job runs the crate's suite through this script. Inside a managed run host_guard.sh's run root sits under the run's own TMPDIR, the only place SRT grants Unix sockets, and a host listing that the sandbox hides goes through protocol step 6's route (docs/guides/gterminal-development-guide.md:228-234, 445-453). Four Python fixes also came after the terminal plan, and the native host carries them. Native paste (#23445, #25149): a single write sends text as one paste operation at any length, a submit follows as its own Enter after TMUX_TEXT_ENTER_DELAY_SECONDS, one second, which crates/gterminals/src/native_write.rs:24 already has, and text over 1 MiB raises the typed payload error (src/gobby/terminals/native_runtime.py:594-612, 643-668; tests/terminals/test_native_runtime.py:447-457). A batch's text over NATIVE_PASTE_THRESHOLD_CHARS, 2000, goes as one paste operation with a trailing Return as its own key operation PASTE_SUBMIT_DELAY_MS later, and at or under it keeps its single text write (src/gobby/terminals/native_runtime.py:68-72, 125-138). crates/gterminals/src/native_write.rs:95-129, 311-318 still sends that text as a text write, which loses a long kickoff's head in Claude Code. Epoch redial (#25175): a spawn commit whose transport failed before the request was written redials the epoch it was prepared on, a failed redial leaves the commit unsent, an epoch mismatch fails typed, and the executor resends once (src/gobby/terminals/native_runtime.py:154-158, 405-421; src/gobby/terminals/host_client.py:89-94, 423-445, 753-786; src/gobby/agents/spawn_executor_runtime.py:335-350). Composer ledger: record_queued_submit consumes a flagged submit whenever no block is live (#24842), and record_local_command settles a flagged submit when a local slash command's transcript row is written at or after its receipt time, which unconsumed_submit_at reports (#25382) (src/gobby/terminals/composer_ledger.py:374-406, 408-413, 414-431). record_composer_wipe joins the ledger for HOOK-2's wipe (#25595; src/gobby/terminals/composer_ledger.py:621). The native ledger loads and writes Python's <gobby_home>/runtime/composer_ledger.json at state version 1 (src/gobby/terminals/composer_ledger.py:77, 688-724), so an open terminal's ledger survives this activation and a restored generation reads it back. It also binds its health_state (src/gobby/terminals/host_manager.py:174) to OBS's gterm_host port at that activation, and a host that fails to start marks gterm_host on SEAM-FAMILY's degraded set and records the error on R2's startup-progress row, as Python does (src/gobby/runner_lifecycle_subsystems.py:289-301). Python's start also clears this machine's orphaned operator write latches, the ws: entries (src/gobby/servers/websocket/terminal_ws_write.py:165) whose daemon_epoch is not this start's (src/gobby/runner_init/terminal_wiring.py:91-93; src/gobby/storage/terminal_settlement.py:257-297), and that call stops with Python's host manager at this activation, so the native host does the same at each start, because a terminal refuses new writes at 32 latches (crates/gterminals/src/write.rs:43, 823). The send_keys gate file now also holds wake_target_refusal (#25830, #25901), the check a live wake makes last before its write. It is process inspection only and shares its first step with send_keys_target_refusal: the foreground executable must resolve to the agent CLI build the daemon's PATH launches, or a version-named sibling of it, and a foreground node, npm Claude or the installed SRT runner, is admitted only through the target session's recorded CLI process, live in the foreground by pid and start time (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/sessions/_terminal_send_keys_gate.py:110-131, 134-271). AG-3's wake decision calls it through target_gate, which first withholds every node terminal as node_terminal_withheld, so no node wake types (src/gobby/events/wake_target.py:22-52; src/gobby/events/wake.py:886-890). No pane text decides a wake: the decision reads the session row, the lease focus hold and the composer ledger, and delivers as empty, drain or stranded, where stranded presses only the Enter of a wake prompt the ledger shows unsubmitted (#25922, #25929; src/gobby/events/wake.py:748-835, 891-898).

Operator input typed during a handoff ladder queues behind the hold, where Python's lock let it through: the queue keeps it in order, refuses new input with an explicit error once its oldest item has waited 30 seconds, and discards nothing (.gobby/plans/daemon-side-gterm-adoption-and-terminal-ws.md 2.4).

### AG-WAIT: Agent waits and the completion registry

- **kind:** switch
- **goal:** The event-driven wait_for_* primitives and Python's in-memory completion registry (events/completion_registry.py), single-owner state that moves only once its last Python caller and producer is gone (D19, D71). It takes over the native waiters that AG-2 builds. s2-11's deferred D2 and agents-family's wake and mailbox obligations (:740) land here and in AG-3 (D29). Completion (D71). From its activation (CP-WAVE5-CUT) the native completion service is the only completion owner. It holds AG-2's in-memory waiters, native wait_for_agent and task expansion's in-memory subscribers, whose PLANS seam re-binds to it at that activation, with the caller's lineage read through gsessions, so PLANS' two completion ops are no longer called, and PIPE-2's wait step on an expansion is woken in process, keeping its durable read for a run that ended before it registered (D71). It delivers durable completion_subscribers through AG-3's wake decision, with one owner at a time so that no subscriber row is woken by both, and PIPE-2's delivery for its executions' subscriber rows moves into it. It also takes the startup redelivery of this machine's terminal runs in R3's agents slot, in place of src/gobby/runner_lifecycle_agents.py::_cleanup_terminal_agent_completion_subscribers. AG-1's deliver_completion re-binds to it, so AG-1's delivery op and composed-result op are no longer called (D4), and S3-DELETE deletes them. Coordination waits (agents-family 5.3). Registration and cancel reproduce the transactions of src/gobby/storage/coordination_waits.py::CoordinationWaitManager, including the owner lock taken through gsessions' session_rows. The delivery worker ports src/gobby/events/coordination_waits.py::CoordinationWaitService over gcore's new Pool::listen (crates/gcore/src/postgres_pool/listen.rs), which is one connection outside the pool listening on gobby_coordination_wait. The worker takes the recovery snapshot after every listen and retries an undelivered wake after 5 seconds. It is a job on R4's registry that registers only once the family is active (D37). From the same activation R5 no longer starts Python's CoordinationWaitService, so exactly one delivery worker runs. As the family's last activation, AG-WAIT also brings docs/contracts/agents-native.md and docs/guides/agents.md to native operation (agents-family 11.3). wait_for_output keeps Python's polling, pattern and timeout semantics over the pane read effect, with its matched, timed-out and ended-run outcomes (agents-family 2.2.3). This chunk's service answers AG-2's parked check from CP-WAVE5-CUT (D71). Coordination registration and refresh stay at read committed and lock the owner through session_rows before they read its status, so a wait never registers against a stale owner status (agents-family Decision 16 and 5.3.5). Restart recovery (s2-11 D2, #21564): this chunk ports the recovery steps that consume the hook barrier and takes their places in R3's order at CP-WAVE5-CUT: the barrier's classification and fencing (src/gobby/runner_hook_replay.py:47-164), fed by HOOK-3's startup pass; agent-run reconciliation (src/gobby/runner_lifecycle_reconcile.py:53-437, 486-538; src/gobby/runner_lifecycle_agents.py:159-202, 293-328), which skips fenced runs and which the monitor's reclassification calls for them (src/gobby/runner_lifecycle_reconcile.py:443-483); and session reconciliation with its excluded ids and recovery-safe flag (src/gobby/events/wake.py:194-214; src/gobby/events/wake_active_recovery.py), whose horizon and exclusions AG-3's native wake decision applies to later wakes (src/gobby/events/wake.py:212-213, 585). Their terminal reads use TERM-HOST's native host, which activates with them. From CP-WAVE4-CUT to this activation those steps stay R3's Python entry points, and the Rust side passes them the native pass's fields. D2.2's deletion of src/gobby/runner_hook_replay.py is S3-DELETE's (D14). It also ports the feedback reviewer launch that OBS's review service waits behind (src/gobby/feedback/agent.py:184-364: the configured definition's checks, a native spawn with no checkout through AG-1, the wait on this chunk's completion service and the read of the submitted report). Until then Python's reviewer keeps spawning through its own AgentRunner into Python's terminal host, which moves at this same activation, and native terminal transitions hand its run to Python's completion registry. crates/gdaemon's composition adapts the launch to OBS's reviewer trait, and CP-WAVE5-CUT's activation binds POST /api/feedback/review and the gobby:feedback-review row to OBS's review service, with this chunk's orphaned-run mark in R3's slot, so CRON's feedback worker op and R3's entry point are no longer called, and S3-DELETE deletes them (D14). The interrupted-subscriber wake of PIPE-2's restart recovery moves with that delivery at CP-WAVE5-CUT. Relaunch (D78). This chunk owns the native relaunch: src/gobby/agents/resume_executor.py::resume_agent_run (:116-726) with src/gobby/agents/resume_executor_settlement.py, resume_finalization.py and resume_placement.py, and the relaunch half of src/gobby/storage/agent_resume.py (refuse_parked_daemon_resume, finalize_daemon_resume, register_daemon_resume_waiter, rollback_prepared_daemon_resume and increment_daemon_resume_failure_count). It launches through AG-1's launch path and spawn effect, re-places a placed run through AG-1's placement or refuses it, never launching it unplaced (resume_placement.py:149-236), moves the old run's completion waits to its successor on this chunk's completion service, emits agent_started with the resumed_from_run_id key and the terminal-created event through AG-1's emit (src/gobby/agents/resume_executor_settlement.py:146-148; src/gobby/storage/daemon_resume_keys.py:23) and sends the relaunched notice through AG-3's recovery notice write. Both callers use it: this chunk's agent-run reconciliation (src/gobby/runner_lifecycle_reconcile.py:379, 522) and the parked non-task resume retry (src/gobby/runner_lifecycle_agents.py:334-395), which this chunk ports as a job on R4's registry in place of R4's Python op at CP-WAVE5-CUT. HOOK-1's managed-run ingress finishes a provisional resume through this chunk's finalize from that activation (src/gobby/hooks/agent_run_ingress.py:131-156), in place of HOOK-2's finalize op, and S3-DELETE deletes that op and R4's (D14). Until then Python relaunches, into Python's terminal host.
- **ledger_selectors:** ^MCP gobby-agents:(wait_for_agent|wait_for_output|wait_for_coordination|cancel_coordination_wait)$
- **engines:** events (completion registry, waiters)
- **depends_on:** PIPE-2, AG-2, AG-5, CP-WAVE4-REVIEW, TERM-HOST
- **oracle:** REC-SESSIONS-AGENTS' wait cases on a fake clock (completion, timeout, cancel, waiter restart). REC-SESSIONS-AGENTS' coordination cases: a keyed release, a status set (including one matched at registration), a reply, a timeout, owner end and cancel, a duplicate registration and each refusal. The delivery-worker cases cover a notification after listen, a wait completed while the worker was disconnected, a deadline and a retried first wake. The durable delivery cases cover one wake per subscriber row across the switch from Python's registry, and redelivery at startup (D71). wait_for_output's matched, timed-out and ended-run vectors replay over a recorded pane read (agents-family 2.2.3). An owner transition or deletion committed by a second connection between registration's statements waits for the owner lock or is read after it (agents-family 5.3.5). R3's crash-point corpus with these recovery steps native: a run fenced by a timed-out pass stays out of agent-run reconciliation until a later pass settles, an excluded session stays out of session reconciliation, and each terminal evidence branch (no terminal, a missing row, an ownership mismatch, an exited terminal, a live or uncertain native terminal and an unsupported backend) ends as Python's does (src/gobby/runner_lifecycle_reconcile.py:94-140, 213-230; s2-11 D2.1). The reviewer launch replays tests/feedback/test_feedback_agent.py's outcome classes over a recorded spawn: a submitted report wins over a later lifecycle failure, and a launch failure, a terminal failure, a completion timeout or a success with no report consumes no feedback. The relaunch replays REC-SESSIONS-AGENTS' relaunch cases over a fake launcher, with the durable deltas Python's produce: a parked run's successor and subscriber move, a refusal, a rollback after a failed launch, a provisional resume finished at its first hook, a placed run re-placed or refused, the agent_started event with its resumed_from_run_id key, and the parked retry's failure bound (D78). Task expansion's subscribers are woken once by the native service, across the switch from Python's registry, and PIPE-2's wait step on an expansion resolves once on either side of it (D71).
- **size:** L, 2 checkpoints (4 rows). Python in scope: events completion registry and waiters ~1.5K (CompletionEventRegistry has 24 references); Rust ~1.5K. The restart recovery reads src/gobby/runner_lifecycle_reconcile.py (525 lines), src/gobby/runner_hook_replay.py (164 lines) and src/gobby/events/wake_active_recovery.py, and adds about 0.7K Rust. The feedback reviewer launch adds about 0.4K of Python in scope. The native relaunch (D78) adds about 1.9K of Python in scope and about 1.5K of Rust.
- **decision_refs:** D19, D29, D37, D71, D4, D78, D2, D14
- **seam_gaps:** (none)

- **python_edits:** None.
- **registration:** Same crate as AG-1. Its coordination-wait delivery worker is a job on R4's registry, registered at CP-WAVE5-CUT's activation (D37). Its parked retry job is a job on R4's registry too, registered at CP-WAVE5-CUT's activation in place of R4's op (D37, D78).
- **risks:** Waiters lost across a restart must be re-derivable from durable state, as in Python. The native relaunch and Python's never run together: R4's op and R3's entry points stop in the activation that starts it, and the rollback recipe returns both (D78). Until that activation Python's relaunch of a placed run keeps its unbound pane in Python's in-flight set (src/gobby/terminals/workspace_agent_panes.py:364; src/gobby/storage/workspaces.py:345), which TERM-2's native WorkspaceOps cannot see when a workspace read sweeps dead panes (workspaces.py:889-930). Python's bind then fails as not_found, the launch is released and the run parks (workspace_agent_panes.py:527-528; src/gobby/agents/resume_placement.py:209-236; src/gobby/agents/resume_executor.py:614-621), and the parked retry counts that against its bound of three failures (src/gobby/runner_lifecycle_agents.py:331, 366-394). TERM-2's worker ops narrow this: its native sweep keeps any NULL-terminal pane in that in-flight set, and a failed op call keeps the pane too, so a native read no longer reaches that bind failure, and the bound stays for Python's other bind failures.

### MUX-1: External MCP multiplexer: child pool and bridge

- **kind:** switch
- **goal:** #25259: the external MCP child pool (stdio, streamable-HTTP and legacy SSE servers over its own rmcp client transports) becomes a Rust-owned single-owner service, with status, refresh, the bridge routes and the tool_call WS message; GW-1/GW-2's proxied external servers switch to native. It runs after the last Python in-process callers of external tools (rule preflight, pipeline MCP steps, hook-driven calls) are native. It does not wait on #25207 (D35). Its first deliverable records the external-MCP corpus and maps #21566's D5 registry rows (19, because tool-timeouts stays while gmcp reads it, D65) to MUX-2; the multiplexer plan was rewritten by 2068aaf9a0 after #25259's commit list. MUX-1 also delivers the multiplexer plan's 1.4 (.gobby/plans/external-mcp-transport-multiplexer.md, Decision 11): SecretStore::secret_in and set_in in crates/gruntime/src/secrets.rs, absorbing the secrets set that A1-CONFIG's PATCH /api/config/values landed, so its secret updates go through set_in and #24466's 5.9.10 is met by 1.4's consumer test (crates/gruntime/tests/values_patch.rs::secret_updates_use_scoped_secrets_set). It also delivers #24467's 5.10.6 native half: the native POST /api/config/secrets accepts an optional string project_id, absent or null meaning global and a malformed one answered with the route's existing 422 body, and passes it to set_in, with a test that Python's SecretStore.get reads the scoped value back. That test replaces the criterion's crates/gruntime/tests/secret_save.rs::project_scoped_save_matches_python, which assumed Python's pass-through. Python's route is not changed (D4), so the field stays a native extension, inert until V5B's gclient mcp-proxy add-server prompt sends it (multiplexer plan 5.2), and the A1 corpora replay unchanged against the absorbed set. MUX-1 builds the multiplexer plan's hub side (.gobby/plans/external-mcp-transport-multiplexer.md P1) in crates/gdaemon/src/mcp_client/ (Decision 1). 1.1: Pool, with Decision 6's policy (a changed spec fingerprint replaces the connection; up to three connect retries at 1, 2 and 4 seconds; three failed connects open a 30-second circuit with one half-open probe; a 300-second idle close; one reconnect before a send and no replay after one; no health pings) and Decision 8's call registry (cancel tombstones kept 600 seconds, at most 4,096), the wire types and error codes, which S4-NODE's node handler reuses, and the gdaemon-mcp-fixture test server. Idle close is the pool's own connection timer, not a job. 1.2: the launch environment (${VAR} and ${VAR:-default} expansion, offline npx, the chrome_executable_path and loopback_browser hooks, with the loopback config written to <gobby_home>/mcp/browser-loopback.json) and orphan-proof supervision through gdaemon mcp-child -- <argv> (Decision 7), with server stderr in <gobby_home>/logs/mcp-servers.log; a compile-only Windows clippy job in .github/workflows/rust-ci.yml proves the JobObject path, whose runtime proof stays post-1.0 with Windows (83a9445f). 1.3: the client transports (Decision 2): a stdio child through rmcp's TokioChildProcess, streamable HTTP with the spec's headers and the 30-second timeout and 300-second read timeout that Python's client sets (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/transports/http.py::build_mcp_http_client), and legacy SSE as an rmcp Transport, because rmcp ships no legacy SSE client; a 401 from either HTTP transport, at connect or on a request, answers unauthorized with the server's WWW-Authenticate value and drops the connection, and no configured header or environment value reaches a log line, a status entry, an error or Debug output (1.3.4). 1.5: Backend, which registers each call id, applies Decision 9's deadlines and the loopback-browser policy, resolves $secret: references through 1.4's secret_in and fails closed with missing_secrets, calls Pool::request, and cleans results and errors under untrusted_key, the policies Decision 3 gives Rust, without disclosing a resolved value; GW-1's gateway calls it in process, so no route fronts it. Backend::status keeps each server's last outcome from replies, with no health pings (Decision 6): connected after a successful reply; needs_configuration with the missing names after missing_secrets, or with the auth command as its last error after authorization_required (plan 2.1.8); failed with its code after any other failure. GET /api/mcp/status, MUX-2's registry and OBS's GET /api/admin/status report it. 1.6: OAuth on rmcp's auth feature (Decision 4), through an OAuthStore over secret_in and set_in that keeps Python's secret name (mcp_oauth_ plus the sha256 of project_id, id and url joined by newlines, src/gobby/mcp_proxy/oauth.py:166-167), its OAuthState JSON shape and its advisory lock key (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/oauth_keepalive.py::oauth_lock_key), so stored tokens survive the flip with no re-login, and that ports Python's rotated-token reload, shared backoff, consent clearing, refusal to re-register a client and credential-free failure summaries. 1.7: the login subcommand gdaemon mcp-auth <name> [--project-id] [--timeout] [--shape], which V5B's gclient mcp-proxy auth and oauth-shape execute (plan 5.2) once CP-PREDELETE-CUT's commit B makes gobby the client; until then Python's gobby mcp-proxy auth keeps its own login on the same secret name, shape and lock key. The native OAuth keepalive (a refresh 600 seconds before expiry on a 60-second tick, under the same lock) is the family's job on R4's registry: it registers only from CP-WAVE5-CUT's activation (D37) and replaces Python's keepalive iteration (refresh_due_oauth_servers, src/gobby/mcp_proxy/oauth_keepalive.py:205-228), which S3-DELETE deletes (D14). From that activation GW-1's native cancel route (#24884's 2.1.9) forwards an external call's cancel to Backend::cancel; the registry keeps the caller's session, so another session's cancel leaves the call running, and a cancelled call answers the ordinary failure payload with error_code CANCELLED (plan 2.2). docs/contracts/mcp-multiplexer.md documents the Pool and Backend APIs, the wire types, error codes and policy, the scoped secret store, and the cancel route and its header. The plan's loopback route (/api/internal/mcp/*, 1.5), Python forwarder (2.1) and Python cancellation (2.2) are not built: Python never calls Rust (D19), and no Python client of a Rust endpoint is written (D4). MUX-1 also does the gateway side of the plan's 2.1, whose Python forwarder is not built. From CP-WAVE5-CUT's activation the gateway dispatches external servers through Backend behind its one policy pass (#24884's 2.1.6), and this chunk turns Backend's replies into the payloads Python's ToolProxyService returns today under #24884's 2.1.5 error contract: timeout as the existing timeout result; circuit_open, connect_failed, transport_closed, server_error, oauth_unavailable and untrusted_key with Python's MCPError messages; missing_secrets with Python's needs-configuration message and the names; authorization_required with its auth command; policy_refused with its message (plan 2.1.2, 2.1.3). A call with no timeout, and every list_tools, read_resource and warm call, takes Decision 9's finite 600,000 ms in place of today's unbounded wait. Each list_tools reply passes through 1.5's browser filter and metadata cleaning and is written where Python's cache_discovered_tools writes (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/client_manager/tool_inventory.py:272-305; src/gobby/storage/mcp_tools.py:49). That is the external tool-inventory cache of #24884's 2.1.9, from which the passive GET /api/mcp/tools read and the external schema_hash serve with the filter reapplied (plan :326-330, :782-784) and with no Python on either path. At that activation OBS's native GET /api/admin/status stops taking its mcp_servers block from Python: this chunk supplies the block's external entries from Backend::status, under Python's field names (src/gobby/servers/routes/admin/_health.py:449-480), and its internal entries from GW-1's ToolRegistry. Its native POST /api/mcp/refresh re-embeds the new and changed tools it caches, as Python's does (src/gobby/servers/routes/mcp/endpoints/registry.py:414-454), so this chunk builds the one native tool vector writer, which MCP-FLIP's routes and tool_embeddings seam then call: the port of Python's embed_tool with its tool text, point payload, stale-point delete and collection ensure and repair (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/semantic_search.py:72-101, 184-231, 407-494), generating through AI-1A's embedding generation (#25095), asserting AI-2's serving lease and writing to each managed projection target the switch journal names through #25542's module, and taking gcore's project fence for the tool's project around each point write (crates/gcore/src/project_fence.rs, PROJ-2), as Python's embed_tool takes its project write context (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/semantic_search.py:418) (D8, D47). A tool point's identity stays Python's after #25488: its id is uuid5 of {server_id}/{tool_name} in the DNS namespace, its payload carries source_id, an existing point's source_id is preserved, and the stale delete filters on server_id and tool_name except that point (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/semantic_search.py:37-42, 458-494; 35d1d1d271).

The multiplexer plan's Rust cases against its stdio, streamable-HTTP and legacy SSE fixtures and a stub authorization server: 1.1.1-1.1.8, 1.2.1-1.2.6, 1.3.1-1.3.4, 1.4.1-1.4.3, 1.5.1 run through Backend::request instead of the loopback route, 1.5.2-1.5.4, 1.5.6 and 1.5.7, 1.6.1-1.6.6, whose 1.6.4 round trip over Python's stored OAuthState shows that stored tokens survive the flip with no re-login, 1.7.1-1.7.4, and 2.2.2's ownership and CANCELLED cases driven through GW-1's cancel route. #24884's binding tests crates/gdaemon/tests/mcp_gateway.rs::external_and_internal_calls_share_policy and ::cancel_and_external_inventory_are_native; the reply mapping and budgets of plan 2.1.2 and 2.1.3 through the gateway; 2.2.4's last ordering, where a cancel while Backend builds the request ends the call CANCELLED with zero pool requests; and REC-PLATFORM's GET /api/admin/status case through OBS's handler with its mcp_servers block from Backend::status. ### MUX-2: External MCP server registry

- **kind:** switch
- **goal:** #21566: the server registry and template routes, add, import, list and remove_mcp_server, and persistence of external server configuration. D35: #21566's node work (P3/P4: the MCP commands in the node-commands contract, the node MCP handler, placement and the 4.1 pair proof) moves to S4-NODE, so plan 3.1's edge on #25207 is cut, and Decision 5's placement rule (a call with no caller runs on the local machine) stays. From CP-WAVE5-CUT's flip the native registry calls MUX-1's Backend::disconnect at once on remove, on disable and on a config-changing update, so the next call connects with the new spec (.gobby/plans/external-mcp-transport-multiplexer.md 2.1.6), and list_mcp_servers and the add result report Backend::status, answering needs_configuration with its configure lines after a missing_secrets or authorization_required reply and connected after a successful one (plan 2.1.8). Add and enable warm the server through one Backend list_tools, as MUX-1's POST /api/mcp/refresh does, and that reply fills the add result's connected, full_tool_schemas, needs_configuration and configure fields: configure lists the auth command after authorization_required and names the secrets after missing_secrets. A server's load-time needs_configuration comes from its first reply, with no secret probe at load. Python's preconnect list has no production setter (src/gobby/runner_init/mcp_stack.py:143-150), so the native start warms nothing. Under D91 the native registry refuses the websocket transport on add, import and update, an accepted contract change in D17's triage. gmcp's stdio tool list keeps naming websocket until S3-DELETE, because tests/mcp_proxy/test_gmcp_parity.py pins it to src/gobby/mcp_proxy/stdio_tools.py:259-263, so such an add through gmcp reaches that refusal. CP-WAVE5-CUT lands that commit among its prepared commits before it runs gobby ui build; Python's registry keeps accepting websocket until S3-DELETE (D4). The multiplexer plan's Decision 3 also files sync under #21570, which is not this chunk's: bundled MCP templates sync in TPL (src/gobby/sync_registry.py:35-37), and user MCP templates and server instance files sync in V1B's gobby sync and gobby install. Its native tool registration and removal append the tool change rows in the same transaction as the tools rows and write no tool vector, as Python's registry does (src/gobby/storage/mcp_servers.py:216, 237, 596; src/gobby/storage/mcp_tools.py:65, 84): while a switch journal names a physical target, the switch's replay projects those rows through the tool_embeddings seam, and the dual-write that #25071's criterion 3 names is MUX-1's tool vector writer's, under gcore's project fence (D47). Output repair follows D101, which Josh settles at map approval: under its default this chunk ports src/gobby/mcp_proxy/services/output_repair.py onto Backend's reply path, before the after pass, live from CP-WAVE5-CUT, with the size and oracle D101 states. Triggers: a terminal pane lost or not reattached across a plain restart; a composer or wake failure; a wait that never wakes or wakes twice; an external MCP child missing, doubled or holding stale credentials; a bot that does not reconnect, or an inbound message lost or doubled; any front-door handoff to Python; health or start proof failure. ### CP-PREDELETE-REVIEW: Checkpoint review: retiring Python from the live daemon

- **kind:** checkpoint
- **goal:** Review pause before Python stops running. Its cutover makes the live generation Python-free: gdaemon stops starting the Python worker, the gclient verbs replace the Python CLI, and gclient takes the gobby name. Packet: The seven verb chunks' goldens (V1A, V1B, V2, V3, V4, V5A, V5B) through the renamed binary; S3-FREEZE's frozen corpora and its ledger closure (every row native, delegated or dropped, none proxied); the full-daemon proof on the release build with no Python worker, over every frozen corpus plus a bounded soak loop; V1A's Rust promotion and rollback verbs rehearsed in a temp home; CP-WAVE5-CUT's window record. The irreversible consequence for Josh's go: once S3-DELETE lands after this cutover's window, no generation from before this cutover can be restored. The activation is two commits in one window: commit A (gdaemon's backend default, the gclient bump that ships V1A's verbs, and S3-NAME's gobby-name installer constant turned on, which installs gclient under both names; the recipe's restore removes the installed gobby name), promoted with the Python CLI, then commit B (the console script leaves pyproject.toml, the instruction files switch to gobby, release.yml and its PyPI publish go, and release-gclient.yml ships the client as gobby with release.yml's CI gate and Homebrew tap dispatch, while CI runs on gclient-v* tags instead of v* tags, D55) once gobby --version resolves to the new gclient. From this cutover on, no HTTP route has a Proxy backend, so the deactivation path of D36 phase 3 is gone (D36 phase 4). The deep rollback to Python after S3-DELETE, and its cost: revert S3-DELETE's commit and both of this cutover's commits on 0.9.0 with fresh version bumps; if CP-FINAL-CUT's drops have landed, also revert its activation commit, and POST-CLEAN's if it landed, and replace each drop migration file with a no-op migration of the same number, which keeps later numbers and the embedded schema identity valid and drops nothing on the restored backup (the one named exception to D22's rule that applied migrations are never edited, because the restore discards the hub that applied them); if CP-FINAL-CUT's drops have landed, first restore CP-FINAL-CUT's backup with the daemon stopped; then rebuild and promote the reverted tree with uv run python -m gobby.cli cutover --path <main checkout>. It costs a revert of about 1.6 million deleted lines (582,631 src and 1,056,889 test), a full rebuild, a multi-hour outage and every write since that backup. Outside this repository, GobbyAI/homebrew-tap's gobby formula must install the client archive, with its version_scheme raised, before the first gclient-v* tag after commit B (D55), through the pull request CP-NODE-REVIEW's session opens (D127). Under D60's default the tap's gobby formula also carries gdaemon, gcode, ghook, gterm and gmcp, as resources from their own releases, and its four helper formulae retire. None of those members has a release at its pinned version today, and Josh's publication at .gobby/plans/node-install-enrollment.md E1 gate 3 is the first that does, so until then a Homebrew gobby stays unable to run a daemon, as it is today. This review's replay of REC-CLI's goldens through the renamed binary reads V5B's fixture copy of projects.files-migrate.final-layout for gobby files migrate, and CP-PREDELETE-CUT's commit A lands the real entry and its citation (D48). The full-daemon proof includes R6's no-worker restart form (D68) and V1A's and V1B's gdaemon subcommands (D69). The prepared commits that CP-PREDELETE-CUT lands ahead of commit A include S3-NAME's template commit, with its search result: uv run gobby left only in the consolidation rule's allow list (D39). Every other CLI golden that a family plan gives an entry, such as V3's five clone entries and V5A's cron.cli-* entries, also replays through the renamed binary over its chunk's fixture copy, and commit A lands the real entries and citations (D84). A known short-lived difference: between commit A's promotion and commit B, uv run gobby restart exits 1 on R6's null backend_pid while the restart proceeds (src/gobby/cli/daemon_lifecycle.py:616-619), and the cut's window does not count it as a trigger. Commit A's gdaemon ignores GOBBY_BACKEND_COMMAND, the cut's recipe restores with the Python CLI, and a Python console script ahead of the new gobby on PATH is renamed right after commit A's promotion and deleted at the cut's close. They also include V1A's prepared commit, with the bundled gclient-commands.md and admin/daemon.md references, listed ahead of S3-NAME's template commit, which takes the next PATCH version of admin/daemon.md when the cut's branch is prepared (A17-TEMPLATES). Its full-daemon proof also boots with the worker default off on a fresh hub that holds only V1B's install identity and on a restored copy, showing R2's no-worker start form with its machine row and system session, A1-CONFIG's publisher (the first boot before admission, a live and a restart_required write), GET /api/health's 200 with no worker, R6's fall-through 404 and a WS upgrade on an unclaimed path, the break_glass file, and every documented log file receiving its records. Every packet opens with a summary of at most one screen: what changed since the previous review, what needs Josh's call, and any check that did not pass. Every packet also carries the cutover plan for CP-PREDELETE-CUT: the window length and the named triggers; the trigger table, which gives each trigger its default outcome (2 or 3) and who decides; the fix-forward bound (at most two fix cycles, the last fix landing within 24 hours of the first outcome-2 decision, each followed by its own clean window, then outcome 3), which Josh may change in his go; the pinned generation (the one installed when the cutover sets its hold) and the restore members; the recipe; and the loss window: the writes made after the backup, through the rehearsal and the window, which only a backup restore would lose (a drop, or CP-WAVE3-CUT's relocation once it ran; an expand-only rollback loses none, D22), plus every live agent seat's credentials if the recipe restores the backup. It lists every irreversible step that needs Josh's explicit go, every drop the cutover carries among them; an expand step is not one, because the restore plus the deactivation commit undoes it (D22). At once means the binary restore, because the project's quiet-hours rule refuses gobby stop and gobby cutover in every hooked session and lets gobby rollback restore through (.gobby/workflows/rules/quiet-hours.yaml:15-24), so the deactivation build's promotion waits for them to end, and so does a backup restore unless Josh runs its gobby stop from his own shell. The first two must be green (D34). The third is advisory, but a red run is found work fixed before the cut, and when it has no such run since the previous review, this review starts one through workflow_dispatch and names its result, or names it superseded if a later push cancels it (D85). Before writing the packet, fetch origin and list the pending fixes as D40 item 3 defines them, which is none while ruling 24 stands; the review commits nothing, and its cutover cherry-picks and lands the picks that Josh approves. Category manual: escalate_task, then de_escalate_task after Josh's go, then close_task. Record the packet as a review-packet attestation and keep it out of the checkout. Call escalate_task(reason='needs_human: go or no-go for CP-PREDELETE; packet in attestation <id>'), present the packet and the question in the final message, and end the turn. Josh answers in that terminal. If that session is gone, he answers in any later default session, or with gobby tasks de-escalate, or in the web UI. On go: de_escalate_task(reason='GO from Josh <timestamp>: <his words>'), claim_task, an approved implementation attestation quoting him, then close_task(reason='done', preview=true) and the same call without preview, with no commit; the final message then asks Josh to prompt the port dispatcher, because a review's close does not wake it (D116). On no-go: de_escalate_task(reason='NO-GO from Josh ...: <his words>'). Keep the task open. Link the fixes Josh names with add_dependency(task_id=<review>, depends_on=<fix>). File any new filing as a child of #21542, so the port dispatcher starts it, and label it operator-directed, which the found-work gate exempts (src/gobby/install/shared/workflows/rules/stop-gates/enforce-found-work-ladder.yaml:67). A no-go holds no claim, because escalate_task released it, so this session ends its turn with the task open and its blockers linked, and its final message asks Josh to prompt the port dispatcher, which starts the fixes (D116). When they close, the task shows ready again, the dispatcher names it in its final message, and Josh prompts this session or opens a new one, which claims it, builds a new packet and escalates again. Never close a no-go. If Josh abandons the direction, re-plan the downstream edges before any wont_do close, because that close releases them too.

### CP-PREDELETE-CUT: Checkpoint cutover: the live daemon runs without Python

- **kind:** cutover
- **goal:** Category code. After this cutover the live generation is Python-free. Its window holds the acceptance smoke that step 7 lists. Its activation is two commits in the same window (commit A, then commit B), because the Python console script must outlive commit A's promotion. (1) Announcement: Send one global send_message before anything else. It names the checkpoint, the backup's daemon restart, the activation restart, the window and its triggers, the landing freeze and the loss window (the writes made after the backup, through the rehearsal and the window, which a backup restore would lose). It also tells every session how to wait: a session ready to land during the freeze sends this session a direct message, then registers wait_for_coordination(owner_session=<this session>, reply=true, timeout=3600) and registers it again after every timeout and every prompt (src/gobby/mcp_proxy/tools/coordination.py:52-59); this session messages each of them when the freeze clears. (2) Restart timing: Read project_policy.quiet_hours live at that moment, never from a brief, and start only when the backup, the rehearsal and the whole window, at their planned lengths, end before the next quiet hours. Query the protected-runs route directly, GET http://localhost:<daemon port>/api/admin/cron/protected-runs with the bearer header that daemon_auth_headers() builds (src/gobby/utils/local_token.py:460-475; src/gobby/servers/routes/admin/_lifecycle.py:116-126), and start only on a 200 answer whose runs list is empty; a 401, a 503 or a transport error is not clear, because fetch_protected_runs reports no runs on any error or non-200 answer (src/gobby/cli/_daemon_protected_runs.py:30-55). Every later restart, promotion or restore in this cutover repeats both reads and composes no restart notice by hand: the daemon sends its own HOLD before a restart-intent stop and BACK after every healthy start (AGENTS.md rules 4 and 12), and step (9) sends its own message before a rollback; the standing ruling that the review asks for covers only an emergency rollback during quiet hours.
