A fix that needs a schema step goes to outcome 3 or to Josh. After the clean window that follows the last fix, record the window evidence, tag the last commit this cutover promoted as port/<checkpoint id> the same way and push the tag (D40 item 4), then clear the freeze and message each session that asked to land, clear the hold, release the pin, and close as done. Outcome 3: run the recipe, which for a cut whose schema steps are expand-only is the binary restore plus the deactivation commit, with no backup restore, and for a cut that carries a drop, or CP-WAVE3-CUT once its relocation ran, starts with the backup restore. Keep the task open and escalate to Josh, who reassesses before any retry; close this task only as done, after a retry's clean window, and if Josh abandons the direction, re-plan the downstream edges (the blocks edges and docs/port/map-v2.json's depends_on) before any wont_do close, because any close releases blocks edges. Send one project send_message with wake=true naming the in-flight chunks that depend on this stage's review: they stop at their next checkpoint and land nothing until Josh's reassessment is recorded on this task; send a second one releasing them once that reassessment is recorded. A tag push that fails on a GitHub outage changes no outcome: clear the freeze, the hold and the pin as that outcome says, so that chunk sessions can land, retry the push on each later wake and close this task once it succeeds. On P, after closing as done, this session's final message asks Josh to prompt the port dispatcher, because a cut's close does not wake it (D116), and after CP-TEMPLATE-CUT or CP-WAVE3-CUT to name the cap his go at that cut's review set (D23). At outcome 1 or 2's close, delete each script step 6 renamed, and run uv tool uninstall gobby when it was a uv tool's, because S3-DELETE empties the tree it imports. The commit that step 6 promoted is commit A, and commit B lands after it, so unless a later fix-forward commit is the tagged one, the tag does not hold commit B: the annotation names commit B's SHA and says whether the tag holds it. For a tag that does not hold it, A's adoption moves its main checkout to the tag in step 6's place, promotes, and once gobby --version resolves to the new gclient on A, moves the checkout on to commit B's SHA and sends step 6's project message. For a tag that holds it, A promotes with uv run python -m gobby.cli cutover --path <main checkout> --hold-token <token> (src/gobby/cli/__main__.py:5-8), because the tag's tree has already removed the console script; A's rollback moves the checkout back and so brings it back (D40 item 4). (9) Rollback recipe: Precede it with step 2's reads and one global send_message that names the rollback and the generation it restores and tells every session to pause task work until DAEMON BACK; for a backup restore it also says that every live agent seat ends and that every write made after the backup is lost, and it is the only notice before that stop, because gobby stop writes stop intent, for which the daemon sends no DAEMON HOLD; the standing ruling, or until Josh gives one the review packet's default, covers an emergency restore during quiet hours. During them the project's rule refuses gobby stop and gobby cutover in this session and lets gobby rollback restore through (.gobby/workflows/rules/quiet-hours.yaml:15-24): the restore runs at once, the deactivation build's promotion waits for the quiet hours to end with the hold and the pin extended, and a backup restore's gobby stop is Josh's to run from his own shell, which that rule does not reach, or waits for them to end too. An expand step needs no backup restore: the deactivation commit reverts this cut's schema inputs with its activation, so the checkout's schema identity matches the restored generation, and the restored generation starts on the hub's expand-only receipts above its head (D22); no write is lost. A drop, or CP-WAVE3-CUT's attachment relocation once it ran, is undone only by the backup restore: before it, end every live agent seat, because the restore drains every restored managed principal and a seat started after the backup has no row in the restored data (src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/cli.py:341; src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/_stores.py:266-269); restore the verified backup with the daemon stopped, before the generation restore below, and relaunch the seats once the restored daemon is healthy; every write made after the backup is lost. Run gobby rollback restore <pinned generation> --bin <members> --hold-token <token> with the members this cutover names, gdaemon alone by default, except that after a schema step (an expand, a drop or a schema-carrying pick) the members always include the stamped set, gcode, gdaemon and ghook, whatever this cut's own line below names: a partial promotion refuses a member whose identity differs from the installed stamp (src/gobby/install/bin_set_coherence.py:97-109, 231-254), start refuses a mixed set (src/gobby/storage/schema_divergence.py:113-157), and gcode and ghook refuse grants minted under another identity (crates/gcore/src/grant/bundle.rs:346-352). ### CP-FINAL-REVIEW: Checkpoint review: after Python's deletion

Any other destructive change is named as an irreversible step for Josh's go. The drop migration set itself is an irreversible step for Josh's go: a rollback is a backup restore that loses every write made after CP-FINAL-CUT's backup, through its window. The deep rollback to Python and its cost, as in CP-PREDELETE-REVIEW's packet: revert S3-DELETE's commit and CP-PREDELETE-CUT's two commits with fresh version bumps; if CP-FINAL-CUT's drops have landed, also revert its activation commit, and POST-CLEAN's if it landed, and replace each drop migration file with a no-op migration of the same number, which keeps later numbers and the embedded schema identity valid and drops nothing on the restored backup (the one named exception to D22's rule that applied migrations are never edited, because the restore discards the hub that applied them); restore CP-FINAL-CUT's backup first if its drops have landed; then rebuild and promote with uv run python -m gobby.cli cutover --path <main checkout>; about 1.6 million deleted lines, a full rebuild, a multi-hour outage and every write since that backup. CP-FINAL-CUT's activation commit also adds #25058's two cross-store-recovery waiver entries with the journal flip (D47), and its step 3 seat reviews a literal search of crates/ for project.json, which may find only identity reads, ghook's hooks_disabled read, gprojects' own paths, tests and reads through PROJ-1's metadata guard (D63). For Josh's go, as an accepted contract change: that commit also removes code_index.maintenance_log_file with its settings field, its frozen cases and any stored row through a destructive migration, an irreversible step this go covers, after which the cut runs gobby ui build through V1B's native verb (D65). The prepared commits that CP-FINAL-CUT lands include S3-DELETE's template commit, which takes the commands that only Python could run out of the template tree and rewrites the paths and links that the move and the deletion leave stale, with its search and link results (D39). A pick that carries a schema input, a gcode or ghook version or a template is a prepared commit too. Josh's go approves both lists. It lists every irreversible step that needs Josh's explicit go, every drop the cutover carries among them; an expand step is not one, because the restore plus the deactivation commit undoes it (D22). At once means the binary restore, because the project's quiet-hours rule refuses gobby stop and gobby cutover in every hooked session and lets gobby rollback restore through (.gobby/workflows/rules/quiet-hours.yaml:15-24), so the deactivation build's promotion waits for them to end, and so does a backup restore unless Josh runs its gobby stop from his own shell. When they close, the task shows ready again, the dispatcher names it in its final message, and Josh prompts this session or opens a new one, which claims it, builds a new packet and escalates again. Never close a no-go. If Josh abandons the direction, re-plan the downstream edges before any wont_do close, because that close releases them too.

If it carries an expand step, prove that the restored generation starts and serves on the migrated rehearsal hub, whose expand-only receipts sit above its head (D22), and reads back the rows the activated build wrote, and that it writes through every table the expand step altered (an insert and an update on its own code paths succeed). Then build the deactivation commit, promote it over the restored generation and prove that it starts and serves this stage's corpora with this stage's defaults off, on the hub that an expand step left ahead when the cutover carries one. (7) Observation window: Hold it in this session with a provider background watch that samples the triggers into a log, plus wait_for_coordination on that watch, registered again every 3,600 seconds or less, after every timeout wake and after every prompt; after a compaction, fetch the wait tool's schema again first (AG-WAIT's native wait). The window ends before the next quiet hours. Length and named rollback triggers: 8 hours. Triggers: any query error naming a dropped table or column; a frozen corpus case that fails on the live hub; health or start proof failure. More triggers: a policy read that refuses with no pending entry and no held lock, or a journal entry that stays pending after a project read (D47, D63); gobby ui build failing, or the settings section failing to render once the build finishes (D65). (8) Decision: Record the outcome on the task. Each trigger's outcome follows the trigger table in the window plan, which Josh approved with his go: health or start proof failure, any data loss and a schema verify failure are outcome 3 at once, decided by this session; every other named trigger defaults to outcome 2, decided by this session, unless the table names outcome 3; this session asks Josh only for a trigger not in the table, in its own terminal and keeping its claim, waiting as step 7 does, because escalate_task would release the claim that the landing freeze is bound to (GEN-ROLLBACK). Outcome 1, it works: an approved implementation attestation with the window evidence; tag the commit that step 6 promoted (0.9.0 HEAD at promotion) as port/<checkpoint id>, this cutover's id (for example port/CP-WAVE1-CUT), as an annotated tag whose message lists the SHAs of the prepared, regeneration and activation commits it landed, and push the tag, so that A can adopt this checkpoint when Josh decides, by running these steps on its own install with its main checkout moved to the tag in step 6's place, after its own backup and rehearsal (D40 item 4); clear the freeze and message each session that asked to land, clear the hold, release the pin, and close as done. Outcome 2, it works well enough to debug: fix forward on 0.9.0 with the pin still held, for at most two fix cycles, the last fix landing within 24 hours of the first outcome-2 decision, unless Josh's go set another bound (the clean window after each fix does not count toward the 24 hours); past that bound, outcome 3. Before each fix lands, extend the hold and the pin to the end of a new clean window of this cutover's own length (gobby rollback hold extend and pin extend). Give the fix commit, its version bumps included, the code-reviewer seat, fix and recheck until it passes, then stop it, and link its final SHA to this task, because land_commit lands only a SHA linked to the landing task; then land it under the freeze as the hold's owner, as a shipping commit: like the activation commit, it bumps by 0.0.1 every shipped binary whose fingerprint changed since its last bump, gcode and ghook included, with Cargo.lock, the managed pins and the gcode floor in step (D39); check HEAD and wait for its CI as step 6 does, rerun the restore half of the rehearsal against the new HEAD (the pinned generation's step-9 members and one read-back), then promote under the token, with step 2's reads first. A fix that needs a schema step goes to outcome 3 or to Josh. After the clean window that follows the last fix, record the window evidence, tag the last commit this cutover promoted as port/<checkpoint id> the same way and push the tag (D40 item 4), then clear the freeze and message each session that asked to land, clear the hold, release the pin, and close as done. Outcome 3: run the recipe, which for a cut whose schema steps are expand-only is the binary restore plus the deactivation commit, with no backup restore, and for a cut that carries a drop, or CP-WAVE3-CUT once its relocation ran, starts with the backup restore. Keep the task open and escalate to Josh, who reassesses before any retry; close this task only as done, after a retry's clean window, and if Josh abandons the direction, re-plan the downstream edges (the blocks edges and docs/port/map-v2.json's depends_on) before any wont_do close, because any close releases blocks edges. Send one project send_message with wake=true naming the in-flight chunks that depend on this stage's review: they stop at their next checkpoint and land nothing until Josh's reassessment is recorded on this task; send a second one releasing them once that reassessment is recorded. A tag push that fails on a GitHub outage changes no outcome: clear the freeze, the hold and the pin as that outcome says, so that chunk sessions can land, retry the push on each later wake and close this task once it succeeds. On P, after closing as done, this session's final message asks Josh to prompt the port dispatcher, because a cut's close does not wake it (D116), and after CP-TEMPLATE-CUT or CP-WAVE3-CUT to name the cap his go at that cut's review set (D23). (9) Rollback recipe: Precede it with step 2's reads and one global send_message that names the rollback and the generation it restores and tells every session to pause task work until DAEMON BACK; for a backup restore it also says that every live agent seat ends and that every write made after the backup is lost, and it is the only notice before that stop, because gobby stop writes stop intent, for which the daemon sends no DAEMON HOLD; the standing ruling, or until Josh gives one the review packet's default, covers an emergency restore during quiet hours. During them the project's rule refuses gobby stop and gobby cutover in this session and lets gobby rollback restore through (.gobby/workflows/rules/quiet-hours.yaml:15-24): the restore runs at once, the deactivation build's promotion waits for the quiet hours to end with the hold and the pin extended, and a backup restore's gobby stop is Josh's to run from his own shell, which that rule does not reach, or waits for them to end too. An expand step needs no backup restore: the deactivation commit reverts this cut's schema inputs with its activation, so the checkout's schema identity matches the restored generation, and the restored generation starts on the hub's expand-only receipts above its head (D22); no write is lost. A drop, or CP-WAVE3-CUT's attachment relocation once it ran, is undone only by the backup restore: before it, end every live agent seat, because V1A's restore, a port of Python's, drains every restored managed principal and a seat started after the backup has no row in the restored data; restore the verified backup with the daemon stopped, before the generation restore below, and relaunch the seats once the restored daemon is healthy; every write made after the backup is lost. Run gobby rollback restore <pinned generation> --bin <members> --hold-token <token> with the members this cutover names, gdaemon alone by default, except that after a schema step (an expand, a drop or a schema-carrying pick) the members always include the stamped set, gcode, gdaemon and ghook, whatever this cut's own line below names: a partial promotion refuses a member whose identity differs from the installed stamp and start refuses a mixed set, in V1A's ports of both checks, and gcode and ghook refuse grants minted under another identity (crates/gcore/src/grant/bundle.rs:346-352). Otherwise restore the full set only when gcode or ghook itself broke, because a gcode below the checkout floor breaks the code-index gateway, now in Rust. After a stamped-set restore, the code-index gateway refuses the restored gcode until the deactivation build is promoted, because that gcode is below the checkout's gcode pin, which the gateway, now in Rust, still checks. The restore burns the activated versions, never the restored target's own. Promote the deactivation build only as step 5 proved it: when a trigger implicates a dormant landing rather than this stage's defaults, stay on the restored generation with the pin and the hold extended, add a revert of that landing to the deactivation commit first, and rerun step 5's deactivation proof on the changed commit. Then give the prepared deactivation commit fresh version bumps, first rebasing it onto 0.9.0 HEAD if an outcome-2 fix or another landing has moved HEAD past the commit it was built on, because land_commit refuses a candidate that shares a changed path with a moved tip and escalates its task (step 3), and every fix commit changes the version lines that this commit bumps. Rerun the code-reviewer seat and step 5's deactivation proof on what the rebase, the bumps and any added revert changed, and link the commit's final SHA to this task, because land_commit lands only a SHA linked to the landing task and step 3 links no deactivation commit. Then land it under the freeze as the hold's owner, which fast-forwards 0.9.0, check HEAD, and promote it under the token. Then clear the freeze, the hold and the pin, and message each session that asked to land that the freeze is clear, saying whether it is among the chunks that outcome 3 stops. Every name in this recipe is install-local (this install's own backup, pin, hold and generations), so A runs it unchanged on its own install if its own adoption of this checkpoint rolls back, with its main checkout moved back to the commit it ran before in place of a deactivation commit (D40 item 4). The pinned target is the generation installed at step 3, CP-PREDELETE-CUT's last promotion (commit A's, or a later fix-forward's) unless an emergency cutover on Josh's word promoted a later one; it starts no Python worker, because S3-DELETE landed without a promotion (D39). The restore members are the stamped set, gcode, gdaemon and ghook (gobby rollback restore <generation> --bin gcode,gdaemon,ghook), because this cut's schema inputs change the identity that all three embed. Its drops make the backup restore part of every rollback, as above, and Josh's go for that loss is in the review packet. Its deactivation build is S3-DELETE's build without the drops. That build's project reads and startup step resolve any journal entry the window left, with the journal default off (D47, D63). It also restores D122's telemetry keys, rows and frozen cases.

### S4-NODE: Node mode: node-local spawn, worktrees and node duties

- **kind:** hubnode
- **goal:** Stage 4 (ROADMAP decision 26, after Stage 3). Node mode, the per-machine daemon that holds no datastore credentials (#17436, plan #25258, node duties #21579, node-scoped carve-outs #25328); the node half of agent spawn and worktrees (#24148: code-index preflight, pane monitor, sandbox reaping and records); launch chokepoint gaps (#25364) and run-backed remote delegation (#25423). Lands dormant on 0.9.0 after CP-FINAL-CUT, with the version rule's gdaemon bump, and CP-NODE-CUT's activation first promotes and activates it (D24, D39). D35: #21566's node MCP work (P3/P4) lands here, and #25328 closes as superseded by it. Plan #25258's sections (.gobby/plans/node-mode.md) land as follows. S4-NODE builds 1.1: the hello carries the node's platform and its probed capabilities, agents from verify_srt_installation (crates/gdaemon/src/nodes/agents/sandbox/verify.rs:128) and terminals from an executable <home>/bin/gterm, each with available and a reason; validation refuses more than 8 entries, a duplicate name, a name over 32 bytes or a reason over 512, and the list defaults to empty, so an older node's hello still registers and #24873's skew refusal reaches it, while a malformed list closes 1008; the registry keeps register and stores the hello through set_hello, and GET /api/machines shows each machine's platform and capabilities (new crates/gdaemon/src/nodes/capabilities.rs; nodes/channel.rs, registry.rs and machines_api.rs). 1.1's plan edges on #24875 and #25210 only order edits to the same symbols (node-mode.md:545-554), so S4-INSTALL's handshake chain and S4-ATTACH's relay chain merge onto it. S4-INSTALL builds 1.2, 1.3, 2.1's node half, 2.5, 2.8 and 2.9, which consume its own #24872-#24878 and S4-RELEASE's node family; V3 builds 2.6's pane guard; 2.1's hub half and 2.2-2.4 are V1A's, V5B's and V2's Stage 3 rows and D53; and S4-PROOF carries 2.7 and 2.10. Under D86, 2.7's docs/contracts/cli-inventory.toml and its click-tree test are not built, and its node field becomes #25246's node parity inventory. Windows stays post-1.0 (83a9445f, decision 22, #25249), so #25246's, node-mode.md:71's and node-mode D1's (node-mode.md:2139-2160) '1.0 obligation' text is corrected, and D1's Windows node is not 1.0 work. Hook quarantine retention is this chunk's job: crates/gdaemon/src/nodes/hooks/drain.rs:407 quarantines files that the node-hook-prune job (:56) does not trim, so a job registered through nodes/ register_jobs (crates/gdaemon/src/nodes/hooks/drain.rs:90, crates/gdaemon/src/serve.rs:224-225) trims them at Python's window and bound (src/gobby/hooks/quarantine_retention.py:22-23). The inbox drain already runs there as node-hook-drain. Nothing else on R4's loop list runs on a node, which runs no Python daemon today (#24075): the hub's AG-4 job removes a node's expired workspaces through node commands (hub-mode 4.5), a native node removes its prompt file at launch (crates/gdaemon/src/nodes/agents/launch.rs:255-256), session liveness reads hub rows that a node holds no credential for, so pane state reaches the hub in node reports, and the resource monitor's degraded flag has its only reader in the hub's status. #21566's node MCP work follows .gobby/plans/external-mcp-transport-multiplexer.md P3 and P4. 3.1: mcp.request, mcp.cancel, mcp.disconnect and mcp.status with their replies (crates/gdaemon/src/node_commands/mcp.rs; docs/contracts/node-commands.md) at the next free contract version when they land (D22), with no Python mirror, because no Python remains after CP-FINAL-CUT. 3.2: the node's command handler (crates/gdaemon/src/nodes/agents/commands.rs) runs them on its own Pool from MUX-1's module, outside the per-run queues, holding a resolved spec only in memory, and NodeServices::shutdown reaps its pool's process groups while the host stays up. 3.3 (Decision 5): Backend places a stdio server on the caller's machine and a URL server on the hub's pool (crates/gdaemon/src/mcp_client/placement.rs). The caller comes from GW-1's gateway, and a call with no caller runs on the local machine. A missing machines row, a missing project_checkouts row or no live channel refuses with machine_not_found, checkout_unresolved or node_offline and runs nothing on the hub. The hub resolves secrets and OAuth tokens and sends the resolved spec. An in-memory holder set sends mcp.disconnect to every holder on a removal, disable, config change or disconnect; an offline holder blocks nothing, is listed in failed_holders and stays tracked; and Backend::status merges each holder's mcp.status under its machine id. A node-placed call keeps Decision 9's budgets: a 600,000 ms outer ceiling, with each hop's inner deadline ending first. docs/contracts/mcp-multiplexer.md gains the placement rule and the holder set. #24384's reaper and runner-reap modules already exist from AG-2 (crates/gdaemon/src/nodes/agents/sandbox/reaper.rs, runner_reap.rs): this chunk reuses them and adds the node's start-time use and its records.

### S4-RELEASE: Signed releases, gobby node and enrollment

- **kind:** hubnode
- **goal:** #24851: signed checksums for every binary release, the gmcp release workflow (#24359 makes gmcp a published managed binary as a leaf edge, D6) and node bundles in gdaemon releases. #24852: gdaemon node and the no-toolchain harness, gobby node install and enroll running the sibling gdaemon, gobby node enroll (#24861, D7), remediation naming it, and pair_node enrolling with the Rust verb (#24863). Lands dormant on 0.9.0 after CP-FINAL-CUT, with the version rule's gdaemon bump, and CP-NODE-CUT's activation first promotes and activates it (D24, D39). #24863 closes as superseded (D7; V1B recorded the drop), and S4-PROOF's #24604 rewrite carries its real-hub enrollment proof. #24856 stays as written: its Windows archives already ship. From CP-PREDELETE-CUT's commit B the client's release assets are gobby-<target>.tar.gz holding the gobby binary, under its gclient-v* tags (S3-NAME, D55), so #24851's signing step and its node bundle script read those names. It builds none of V1A's, V1B's or V3's work a second time. #24865's promote_set and #24875's staged activation call V1A's promotion core in gobby-core (crates/gcore) with the verified bundle as the source, and add only the bundle steps: the signed manifest check, the six members and .node-release.json (.gobby/plans/node-install-enrollment.md 3.2, 4.3). #24867-#24871 call V1B's per-CLI hook and MCP-entry writers in gobby-core with the node's home, which leave out what that plan's D13 and D17 exclude (shared content, router commands, the statusline, autoMemoryEnabled, validate_settings.py and home-trust seeding), so the node's hooks match V1B's by construction. #24877 adds its release columns to V3's gobby nodes list behind a --release flag that reads GET /api/machines, so the default output stays REC-CLI's golden, and ships its update verb as gobby nodes update, not a second listing under gobby node (D54). It also builds node-mode's node status and service verbs (.gobby/plans/node-mode.md), after the work of its own and S4-RELEASE's that they consume. 1.2 (:683-787): new crates/gdaemon/src/nodes/channel_status.rs holds the channel state, Connecting from NodeServices::prepare and then Connected, HubUnavailable, AuthFailed (a 401 upgrade or a 4401 close), Refused (holding #24873's refuse frame) or Disconnected, each with its since time, recorded by run_client; the node arm of FrontDoor::handle answers GET /api/node/status locally, before the relay, only for a bearer that passes has_node_key (crates/gdaemon/src/nodes/hooks/ingress.rs:114, made pub(crate)), and otherwise returns 401 node_key_required with nothing sent to the hub; its 200 body gives machine_id, node_version, platform, hub, channel and capabilities. 1.3 (:789-902): gobby node status [--json] in #24860's node family (crates/gclient/src/command/node.rs) runs in the client, exits 1 on a hub bootstrap ('this machine runs the hub, not a node; use gobby status') and 3 when the machine is not enrolled or its node daemon is unreachable, naming #24872's service file state (com.gobby.node.plist or gobby-node.service) and gobby node start, and maps each channel state to its first line and exit code (healthy exits 0; capability unavailable, hub unavailable, auth failed, refused, disconnected and connecting exit 1); it sends its request through V1A's operator HTTP helper (crates/gclient/src/command/api.rs) and adds no second one. 2.1's node half (:912-1048; node-mode O3, O4 and O8): REC-CLI's goldens record a hub, whose dashboard reads the local lock, pid, service, dependencies and schema heads, and a node has none of them, so V1A's verbs leave this branch to this chunk. On a DatastoreMode::Remote bootstrap (read_files_home_view, as V3's guard reads it) gobby status, and gobby health, which node-mode absorbs into status (:1640), skip those reads and report the hub through the node's relay, and node status stays the node's own health. They send GET /api/health with no token. A 503 whose body has backend prints backend <state> and exits 1, so a stopped hub prints backend down; a 502 exits 1; and a connection refused or timed out prints not running with the URL and exits 3. On a 200 they read the token and send GET /api/admin/status. The first line is healthy only when health.status is ok and the admin status is healthy, and otherwise degraded: <services> or degraded: admin status, followed by mode, uptime and, when degraded, the hook runtime state; healthy exits 0 and degraded exits 1. gobby status --json prints {"health": ..., "status": ...}. Any other reply goes to the helper's fallback, a bootstrap read error exits 3 as V3's guard does, and on a hub or with no bootstrap file V1A's golden path is unchanged. 2.5 (:1395-1496): gobby node start, stop and restart exec gdaemon node, whose NodeCommand gains Start, Stop and Restart in node_setup/service.rs over launchctl on macOS and systemctl --user on Linux; restart is #24872's restart step, so a node restart keeps its terminals, and start and restart poll GET /api/node/status every second for up to 30 seconds, then print 'node service running; channel <state>' or the node log path. 2.8 (:2002-2047): serve.rs's non-unix run and the node family's Windows path refuse with WINDOWS_UNSUPPORTED constants that name #25249 and macOS and Linux, not the Python daemon. 2.9 (:2049-2082): #24878's docs/guides/node-setup.md gains a Node commands section (node status states and exit codes, that gobby status on a node reports the hub, start, stop and restart, the read and config verbs that run on a node, and V3's pane refusal text) and a Platforms table (macOS and Linux supported; Windows not yet, #25249, quoting both Windows texts). These verbs have no Python command, so their native tests are their readiness evidence (D86), and gobby node gains them beside install and enroll (D54). V1B's per-CLI writers take the template text as an argument, so node setup passes the copies that .gobby/plans/node-install-enrollment.md:358-365 embeds under crates/gdaemon/assets/node_setup/.

Category manual: escalate_task, then de_escalate_task after Josh's go, then close_task. Record the packet as a review-packet attestation and keep it out of the checkout. Call escalate_task(reason='needs_human: go or no-go for CP-NODE; packet in attestation <id>'), present the packet and the question in the final message, and end the turn. Josh answers in that terminal. If that session is gone, he answers in any later default session, or with gobby tasks de-escalate, or in the web UI. On go: de_escalate_task(reason='GO from Josh <timestamp>: <his words>'), claim_task, an approved implementation attestation quoting him, then close_task(reason='done', preview=true) and the same call without preview, with no commit; the final message then asks Josh to prompt the port dispatcher, because a review's close does not wake it (D116). On no-go: de_escalate_task(reason='NO-GO from Josh ...: <his words>'). Keep the task open. Link the fixes Josh names with add_dependency(task_id=<review>, depends_on=<fix>). File any new filing as a child of #21542, so the port dispatcher starts it, and label it operator-directed, which the found-work gate exempts (stop-gates/enforce-found-work-ladder.yaml, under assets/shared since S3-DELETE moved the templates). A no-go holds no claim, because escalate_task released it, so this session ends its turn with the task open and its blockers linked, and its final message asks Josh to prompt the port dispatcher, which starts the fixes (D116). When they close, the task shows ready again, the dispatcher names it in its final message, and Josh prompts this session or opens a new one, which claims it, builds a new packet and escalates again. Never close a no-go. If Josh abandons the direction, re-plan the downstream edges before any wont_do close, because that close releases them too.

### CP-NODE-CUT: Checkpoint cutover: Stage 4 goes live and the live node is updated

- **kind:** cutover
- **goal:** Category code. Activates Stage 4: node enrollment, signed releases, node install and update, the node code index, node hooks, remote attach and the hub view. (1) Announcement: Send one global send_message before anything else. It names the checkpoint, the backup's daemon restart, the activation restart, the window and its triggers, the landing freeze and the loss window (the writes made after the backup, through the rehearsal and the window, which a backup restore would lose). It also tells every session how to wait: a session ready to land during the freeze sends this session a direct message, then registers wait_for_coordination(owner_session=<this session>, reply=true, timeout=3600) and registers it again after every timeout and every prompt (AG-WAIT's native wait_for_coordination); this session messages each of them when the freeze clears. (2) Restart timing: Read project_policy.quiet_hours live at that moment, never from a brief, and start only when the backup, the rehearsal and the whole window, at their planned lengths, end before the next quiet hours. Query the protected-runs route directly, GET http://localhost:<daemon port>/api/admin/cron/protected-runs with the local CLI bearer token that the native admin route requires, and start only on a 200 answer whose runs list is empty; a 401, a 503 or a transport error is not clear, as V1A's restart and cutover verbs require. Every later restart, promotion or restore in this cutover repeats both reads and composes no restart notice by hand: the daemon sends its own HOLD before a restart-intent stop and BACK after every healthy start (AGENTS.md rules 4 and 12), and step (9) sends its own message before a rollback; the standing ruling that the review asks for covers only an emergency rollback during quiet hours. Whenever a pick, a prepared commit or the activation commit of this cutover changes a bundle source under web/, and again whenever a deactivation commit reverts such a change, run gobby ui build once that promotion's restart is healthy: the daemon serves web/dist from disk, web/dist is untracked (web/.gitignore:2), and no landing or promotion rebuilds it (D65). (3) Hold, pin and freeze: Before anything in this step, prepare this cutover's branch off 0.9.0 HEAD, in a worktree made as protocol step 1 says for an operator-opened session, because the main checkout stays on 0.9.0: first the approved picks that carry no schema input, no gcode or ghook version and no template, each cherry-picked with git cherry-pick -x, and a docs-only commit that records in docs/port/picks.md, one line per full A SHA, every disposition the review packet approved that the file does not yet hold (each plain pick as picked as <new SHA>; each pick that lands as a prepared commit in step 6 as picked at <checkpoint id>, because this commit precedes it and cannot hold its SHA; each fix skipped, ported by <chunk id> or dropped, with its reason), made whenever that list is not empty, and adding a Found Work line in docs/port/record.md under each open chunk named as ported by, with the A SHA, so that chunk ports the fix or drops it before it lands (D40 item 3); before writing it, check each pick's (cherry picked from commit <A sha>) trailer and amend a missing one into that pick on this unlanded branch, because git cherry-pick -x documents the trailer only for picks without conflicts and a pick concluded with git commit -m or redone by hand has none (D40 item 3); then the prepared commits that this cut lands in step 6, in review-packet order: each schema-carrying chunk's commit from port/prepared/<chunk id>, each followed by any dependent chunk's schema-test commit based on it (chunk protocol step 8), with every migration renumbered to the next free number above both the branch's highest migration and the live hub's highest receipt (D22), except one that an earlier cut landed and its deactivation commit reverted, whose receipt the live hub keeps, which is never renumbered and, whenever this cut is that cut's retry or numbers any migration above it, comes first, byte for byte under its own filename and number from the commit on 0.9.0 that landed it, even when no prepared commit carries it any more (D22), one commit that regenerates baseline.sql, the catalog manifest and the pin from a real build, each post-TPL template commit, and each pick that carries a schema input, a gcode or ghook version or a template (D22); then the activation commit, and the deactivation commit, which reverts the activation and every prepared commit. Give all of them the code-reviewer seat, spawned as protocol step 7 says on this branch's worktree, except that a second loss of the seat goes to Josh in this session's own terminal with the claim kept, because escalate_task would release the claim that the landing freeze is bound to (GEN-ROLLBACK); fix and recheck until it passes, then stop it. Then set GEN-ROLLBACK's hold with V1A's gobby rollback hold set, which prints the token that every later promotion and restore in this cutover passes as --hold-token, with an expiry at the planned end of the window, counting the backup and the rehearsal. Pin the generation installed now: it is the only rollback target during the window and any fix-forward, and its manifest (source commit, versions, schema identity) is recorded on the task; check its source commit against the last promotion that the previous cutover recorded at its close (for CP-RUNNER-CUT, GEN-ROLLBACK's landing drill on P, or, if Josh refused that drill at map approval under D38, P's installed .gcode-, .gdaemon- and .ghook-release-identity.json receipts; on A, its installed release-identity receipts, D40 item 4), and record any difference on the task. Set the landing freeze bound to this task with B0-CLOSE's native set_landing_freeze, so that land_commit admits only this task's session until the freeze clears. Then, with the freeze set, rebase the whole cutover branch, deactivation commit included, onto 0.9.0 HEAD, which no other session can now move; if 0.9.0 moved, give each gdaemon-bumping pick and the activation commit the next free gdaemon version again, rewrite the picks.md commit with the rebased picks' SHAs, and rerun the seat on what the rebase changed before step 4. Link the picks.md and activation commits to this task, because land_commit lands only a SHA linked to the landing task. Link the deactivation commit only when this cutover lands it (step 6's refused promotion or the rollback recipe), and whenever a linked SHA that has not landed is replaced (a change after the rehearsal, or a fresh start from step 1), unlink the old SHA with unlink_commit and link the new one, because close_task and gport start refuse a task with a linked commit that is not an ancestor of 0.9.0, and that refusal's request to integrate the commit must never be answered by landing a deactivation commit. If what any linked commit lands, the commits under it included, touches a path in project_policy.security_paths (a template rewrite, a pick or a deactivation commit that reverts one can), send the security-auditor seat the exact SHA of each later land_commit first and wait for its approved security-review attestation, as protocol step 7 says, because the rule's path scope covers every linked commit; since e6523f2b69 land_commit and close_task refuse that SHA without it only for a caller whose definition lacks waive_review_gates, which default holds through capabilities ["*"] (src/gobby/install/shared/workflows/rules/task-closure/security.yaml:29-30; src/gobby/install/shared/workflows/agents/default.yaml:5), so for a default-agent session this wait rests on the protocol and no gate enforces it, and close_task reads the latest approval through the landing receipt (task-closure/security.yaml; D115). With no live seat, this session reruns D115's command itself, because it is operator-opened, and if that fails asks Josh in its own terminal, waiting as step 7 does; it keeps its claim either way, because escalate_task would release the claim that the landing freeze is bound to (GEN-ROLLBACK). Then land the plain picks and the picks.md commit, when there is one, with one land_commit on the picks.md commit's SHA, which now contains 0.9.0's tip and fast-forwards it, under the freeze as the hold's owner: land_commit refuses a candidate that shares a changed path with a moved tip and escalates its task, which would release this session's claim on the task the freeze is bound to (D40). After every landing this cutover makes, this one and those of steps 6, 8 and 9 included, this session runs git push origin 0.9.0 from the main checkout in the background, as D116 says, and checks that commit's CI, because it is unspawned and the port dispatcher pushes only for the sessions it spawned (D1, D34, D85). A red run of this step's landing is fixed on this cutover's branch, with the seat and the rehearsal run on what the fix changes. On A, an adoption pushes nothing and has no run to check. Nothing else lands before step 6. The rehearsal and step 6 use exactly these reviewed commits. Record the window plan as an attestation: start, end, each trigger with its baseline or bound, the trigger table (step 8), the restore members, the rollback commands and the hold token, because a replacement session reads them there. From here on nothing rolls back by itself if this session stops (D118). A usage limit or a provider outage leaves its pane and its claim, and the background watch keeps logging. An outage's next timeout wake reaches this session. A usage limit holds its pane on the provider's menu, where no wake lands until Josh submits a prompt there after the reset. Either way it then reads the watch's whole log since its last read and acts on any trigger it recorded. If its pane is gone, Josh opens a replacement, an unspawned default-agent session in a pane the daemon started (start gate item 14), which takes the claim with claim_task(force=true) once get_session shows the owner is no longer active, reads the token, the pin and the commands from the task's window-plan attestations with list_attestations, the newest that names each, resumes at the step the task's attestations show, registers the watch and its waits again, and sets the hold again if it lapsed. It records any later change, a re-set hold's token included, as a new window-plan attestation with no supersedes_id, because only an attestation's author may correct it. If an outcome-3 trigger needs action while no session can answer, Josh runs step 9's restore from his own shell and the replacement finishes the recipe. (4) Verified backup: Take a verified backup with V1A's gclient hub-backup verb, which archives the same artifacts as the Python verb it replaced: PostgreSQL as pg_dump plus globals, a Qdrant snapshot, a FalkorDB RDB, the volume tars, files_home and the audit logs, each restore-verified as it is taken. It stops the live daemon and starts it again, and its stop runs the same protected-run admission as cutover's. From step 3 on only this session lands or promotes, and it lands nothing more until step 6, so the backup, the rehearsal and the activation all start from the same generation and schema. hub-backup covers only the hub machine, so the session also copies the live node's ~/.gobby/bin and bootstrap.yaml into a backup directory on that machine before the update, bootstrap.yaml with mode 0600, and records their sha256 in a window-plan attestation that supersedes step 3's (supersedes_id). (5) Rollback rehearsal: In an isolated home, restore the backup with V1A's restore, which covers PostgreSQL and files_home, into a fresh rehearsal stack of this cut's own, because that restore takes only the managed production target, the exact gobby_test database or a stack that a rehearsal profile names, and the isolated test hub keeps its data on a 3 GB tmpfs (docker-compose.test.yml:26-27), which this hub, 20 GB on P on 2026-11-05, would fill under every running session's tests. Start three containers from the managed services' images, each with its own gobby-rehearsal- name and volume, a loopback port outside the shared ranges and the ai.gobby.rehearsal labels, with gobby_test as the PostgreSQL user, password and database and the managed service's shared_preload_libraries. Make the isolated home mode 0700, with the profile file in it at mode 0600 and a bootstrap.yaml naming that database and a files_home, as V1A's hub-backup checks. Run the restore with GOBBY_HOME at that home, GOBBY_TEST_PROTECT=1, GOBBY_TEST_ALLOW_DOCKER=1, GOBBY_HUB_REHEARSAL_PROFILE at that file and --database-url at that database. The session keeps the stack, with every daemon in the isolated home stopped, because steps 6, 8 and 9 can rerun parts of this step on it, and removes the stack and its volumes when this cutover closes, finishes outcome 3's recipe or starts again from step 1. Before the first daemon start, copy this install's ~/.gobby/.secret_kek into the isolated home with mode 0600, because the restored DEK is wrapped with it and cannot be unwrapped otherwise, and scrub the restored copy: disable every comms channel, external MCP server, webhook and cron job row; point its databases.qdrant and databases.falkordb settings at that stack's Qdrant and FalkorDB, which are its scratch containers, on their own loopback ports and their own volumes, never the compose stack's fixed-name volumes, empty unless this cut's own text restores the backup's snapshot and RDB into them, because the live containers listen on loopback, which the network mode leaves open, and a daemon on this copy would otherwise write into them and reconcile them against its older rows; and start every daemon in the isolated home on P0-HARNESS's loopback-only network mode, so nothing reaches a live bot, server, store or account. Install the pinned generation into the isolated home's bin directory, then build the cutover branch's reviewed activation commit, with the prepared commits under it, and promote it over the pinned one there, which retains the pinned one. Apply this cutover's schema step if it has one, and run the activated build over the stage's corpora so that it writes rows. Then run gobby rollback restore against the isolated home with the members that step 9 names for this cut (the stamped set when it carries a schema step). If this cutover carries no schema step, prove that the restored generation serves on the unchanged schema and reads back the rows the activated build wrote. If it carries an expand step, prove that the restored generation starts and serves on the migrated rehearsal hub, whose expand-only receipts sit above its head (D22), and reads back the rows the activated build wrote, and that it writes through every table the expand step altered (an insert and an update on its own code paths succeed). If it carries a drop, prove the backup path instead: restore the backup into a fresh hub, start the pinned generation on it and read back rows written before the backup. In every case, finish the way step 9 does. Apply the reviewed deactivation commit to the worktree and prove that the restored generation starts and serves on it, because the recipe lands that commit right after the restore. Then build the deactivation commit, promote it over the restored generation and prove that it starts and serves this stage's corpora with this stage's defaults off, on the hub that an expand step left ahead when the cutover carries one. The restored generation runs against the updated isolated node, and the node's previous binaries come back from its copy. Before the restore, the activated build also runs S4-PROOF's node operator CLI cases (node-mode 2.10) from the updated isolated node. (6) Activation commit: Read quiet hours and the protected-runs route again, live, and continue only when the whole window, at its stated length from the end of this step's CI wait, ends before the next quiet hours; otherwise clear the freeze, the hold and the pin, message each waiting session, and start again from step 1 in a later span. A corpus or golden case's citation of a docs/contracts/parity-waivers.json entry lands in the activation commit that flips that case's surface, with any of its entries not yet landed and the regenerated parity ledger, because a cited case passes only on its native answer and so fails while the old answer serves, and an uncited case passes only on its recording. The activated build replays those cases as Waived; any replay of them on the restored generation or the deactivation build reads them from the deactivation commit's tree and compares with their recordings; and the deactivation commit's revert takes them out (D48). That path takes only a published release whose signed node-release.json contract equals the hub's and whose version is not above the hub's (.gobby/plans/node-install-enrollment.md 4.2), so the update waits for publication: once the promotion's restart is healthy and the pull request D127 names is merged, Josh pushes the release tags in the order CP-NODE-REVIEW approved, the gdaemon tag naming the version this commit's bump gave the promoted hub, and this session checks that each member release carries SHA256SUMS and SHA256SUMS.sig and that the gdaemon release carries the four node bundles and the signed node-release.json, before the hub's release target, which it caches for up to 10 minutes, reaches the live node. It includes S4-HOOKS' transcript commands: the node's transcript.process stops refusing, the hub's remote session owner serves commits, compact boundaries, windows, raw ranges, summaries and tails for node sessions, and SES-3B's processing job pages the node once it reports the new contract version. The window ends before the next quiet hours. Length and named rollback triggers: 8 hours. Triggers: the live node failing to report, attach or replay hooks; a node update that does not activate or leaves a mixed version; a release verification failure; health or start proof failure on the hub or the node. The opening smoke also runs .gobby/plans/node-install-enrollment.md E1 gate 4 on one of Josh's Macs with no Python, Rust or Zig on PATH: the Overview's three commands enroll a node that gobby nodes list (D54) shows connected at the hub's target, the staged SRT under ~/.gobby/tools/srt/ passes the node's verifier, and each CLI present carries Gobby hooks and the gmcp entry. The live node's own update is gate 5's automatic half, and gobby nodes update --machine <ref> (D54), run from a gclient window on the new node against the live node, must reach the hub and print the live node's outcome at the target. Further triggers: a release workflow that fails or whose CI gate times out; a member release without its signature, or a gdaemon release without a node bundle; a fresh enrollment that fails. The opening smoke also runs .gobby/plans/code-index-family.md E1's live pair gates. Gate 3: #24380's preflight warns about nothing on the node and gcode status on the hub's own checkout is unchanged. Gate 4: every command 2.9.1 lists exits 0 with results on the node, and the same commands on the hub's checkout print what they printed before. Gate 5, on the node that the install plan's gate 4 enrolled above: with an embeddings block, every file of a project indexed only on that node reaches vectors_synced within three heartbeat ticks and its gcode search prints semantic results with no embedding_identity_mismatch warning; with the block removed and the node gdaemon restarted, its /api/embeddings reaches the hub, which no automated test proves (code-index 4.1-4.3 test each half against stubs). Gate 7's node check: after a node agent run's workspace is removed, the hub holds no code_indexed_project_states row for its overlay (8.6). Any of them failing is a trigger. Further triggers: gobby node status on the live node reporting a state other than healthy for longer than the bound recorded in the window plan while the hub is up, since hub unavailable while the hub restarts is expected (node-mode V2 item 4); a workspace or pane verb on the live node that is not refused. A node session's transcript, messages or summary that differs from its recorded cases, or a node's pending transcripts left unprocessed after the update, are also triggers. A release job that failed on a GitHub or crates.io outage is no trigger: rerun it with gh run rerun <id> --failed on the same tag. (8) Decision: Record the outcome on the task. ## Decisions

### D1: Landing mechanism for chunk tasks on 0.9.0.
- **resolved_by:** ruling 15
- **recommended_default:** 0.9.0 is the integration branch, and the main checkout moves to it (ruling 15). Chunk tasks land with ordinary land_commit onto 0.9.0, because land_commit and its git hook target the main checkout's current branch (src/gobby/tasks/land_commit.py:153-159; src/gobby/cli/installers/git_hooks.py:106), and P's main checkout sits on 0.9.0. The start gate also moves project_policy's integration branch from 0.5.0 to 0.9.0 (.gobby/workflows/rules/project-operating-policy.yaml:33, with a rule-17 bump), which only seat procedures and the injected policy text read. Each chunk works in its own task worktree off 0.9.0, for example 0.9.0-rust. Option A (a subtree landing target) and option B (close at cutover) are not built, and nothing merges into 0.9.0 from another branch: P's Python fixes, POST-CLEAN and Stage 4 all land on 0.9.0, a gobby fix that Game Goblins needs is a fix task on P, and A commits nothing: it adopts a checkpoint by moving its checkout to the tag (D40). The landing session pushes 0.9.0 to origin after each land, so the port branch always has an off-machine copy. A cutover session is unspawned and pushes for itself after each landing it makes; a spawned session's push goes through the port dispatcher (D116).
- **rationale:** Josh: 'we're not merging back into 0.5.0. 0.9.0 will become the new working branch we'll merge into, and you'll be working in a worktree like 0.9.0-rust'. Ordinary landing keeps land_commit's landing lock, ancestry and clean-tree checks, all five close gates per chunk and blocked_by readiness, with no new landing code. The cost is lost isolation: the live daemon runs from the 0.9.0 checkout, so every landed commit reaches it at the next restart, which the live-checkout constraints and dormancy (D37) address. Order between chunks comes from one blocks edge per depends_on entry among the chunk tasks, which readiness honors, and from gport start, which refuses a chunk until every depends_on task has closed as done and, except for a review, its commit is an ancestor of 0.9.0 HEAD.

### D2: Comms order (#25597 puts comms right after R0 and its seams; the 2026-10-25 edges make comms wait) and the close of #22340.
- **recommended_default:** COMMS-1 in wave 3 after R5, AG-3 and its recorded corpus, with sends through a worker op, live at CP-WAVE3-CUT; COMMS-2 (adapter connections, inbound webhooks, attachments, identities) in wave 5 after the last Python in-process sender, live at CP-WAVE5-CUT. #25597's early order is not adopted. The adapter set follows D28 (rulings 12 and 13). #22340, folded into #24173 on 2026-10-28, closes done citing COMMS-1's landing SHA in place of the #24173 plan SHA its escalation names, because no such plan lands. #25597 closes as wont_do in D31's pass, because its order is not adopted.
- **rationale:** #25597 put comms early so that a broken comms port could roll back to the prior binary. GEN-ROLLBACK's retained generations now give every checkpoint that rollback (D38), so the early order buys nothing. Comms has no oracle until P0-LOWTRAFFIC records one, and adapter connections are single-owner state that cannot run in two implementations.

### D3: Cookie verifier #24967 and #24659 versus nine Stage 2 consumers.
- **recommended_default:** Build #24967 now, in SEAM-CALLERS before the pilot; #24659 lands in CIX-1 on that verifier.
- **rationale:** Nine consumers need it, and the after-hub-node deferral predates decision 26.

### D4: May chunks edit Python on 0.9.0 (record oracles, delete ported families, add facades)?
- **status:** Default. It exceeds ruling 6 (port mechanics in Python), so Josh approves it with the map.
- **recommended_default:** Only: tests/ and scripts/ for recording, and scripts/port/ for the port's checks (start gate); the R0-R6 worker package and runner edits; one-line allow-listed worker-op registrations for single-owner services, added by the Rust caller's chunk; GEN-ROLLBACK's promotion, rollback, landing-freeze-owner, hub-backup admission and protected-runs answer modules (D38); R-RETIRE's runner refusal; TERM-1's dormant terminal route helper (D19); GW-2's dormant loopback compatibility endpoint (D26); S3-NAME's dormant gobby-name installer constant, which CP-PREDELETE-CUT's commit A turns on, and its prepared packaging edits, made in commit B; SCHEMA-WINDOW's preflight edit (src/gobby/storage/schema_divergence.py, reached through src/gobby/cli/daemon_preflight.py only at restart, cutover, hub-backup and pack), a prepared commit that CP-RUNNER-CUT lands (D22); S3-DELETE; and bug fixes and friction fixes, which land on 0.9.0 (rulings 6 and 15). The Rust side stops calling a worker op at the activation that replaces it, and S3-DELETE deletes the op, because pinned and retained generations still call it. Every Python edit other than a bug fix, TMUX-PURGE's purge (D129), R-RETIRE's refusal (inert for the gdaemon-launched worker, which always carries the marker) and GEN-ROLLBACK's generation-retaining promotion (live at landing, so the generation each cutover pins is already retained) is dormant: behaviorally inert at landing, because new CLI processes and lazily imported modules run it at once. No per-family deletion of surfaces or domain modules, no Python client of a Rust endpoint, no modernization (af4be945). Also allowed, each under its own decision: D41's closure-policy op and shim; D47's fence half (src/gobby/projects/write_fence.py, src/gobby/storage/hub/postgres.py, src/gobby/runner_init/services.py), a prepared commit; D67's communications status op and shim; D68's restart start-proof entry in R6's worker package; D70's read of R5's start list in src/gobby/servers/_app_lifecycle.py's pending-interaction expire; D74's composer_locked_write op and shim; D75's handoff delivery op and shim; D81's web chat lifecycle op and shim; D82's after-tool phase in GW-2's preflight op and shim; D98's edit of src/gobby/servers/_app_lifecycle.py's three loop starts; D99's calls to the existing track_proxy_outcome and maybe_repair_output in GW-2's op shim and compatibility endpoint; D103's terminal_operator_write op and shim; D105's terminal_focus_changed op and shim; D110's agent_runtime_spawn op and shim; D121's daemon-owned execution and pipeline execution id fields on GW-2's compatibility endpoint. Each is dormant at landing or lands as a prepared commit, as its decision says, and S3-DELETE deletes it. D64's project.json fix sits in the bug-fix clause.
- **rationale:** Keeps Python whole and equal to its recorded behavior, so differential replay stays valid and every retained generation still finds the Python code it calls. Worker ops are the cheapest correct path for single-owner services while their Python callers remain (ruling 9).

### D5: Re-homing the 254 umbrella #21568 rows, the 15 rows on closed tasks and the ownerless rows.
- **recommended_default:** The map's ledger selectors are the re-homing. gport ledger writes chunk ids into the owner column at the cut. Delegated, dropped and unclassified rows are owned by the chunk that confirms them.
- **rationale:** check_coverage.py shows all 1,094 rows owned exactly once; one mechanism replaces a manual re-cite pass.

### D6: #24359, #24360 OAuth 2.1 scope, #19652 transcript archive, #22075 classifier.
- **recommended_default:** #24359 (gmcp as a published managed binary) moves to S4-RELEASE as a leaf, and the #23275 to #24359 edge is deleted with the move. #24360 (OAuth 2.1 for the HTTP transport) is post-1.0: Josh already ruled CIMD only (2026-10-13), so the only open question is whether port-as-is defers new capability, and it does. #22075 (deferred-by-user) is post-1.0; #19652 has no deferral label, so Josh confirms its post-1.0 move at approval and its D31 disposition records it. #19652, #22075 and #24360 leave the #21542 tree in D31's pass, with no close.
- **rationale:** No ledger row needs #24360: local-first 1.0 uses operator, agent-token and grant callers, and node-to-hub uses enrollment credentials. A bare move of #24359 would leave a Stage 2 holder waiting on Stage 4, so the edge goes with it.

### D7: gobby auth login: port it, or drop it for gobby node enroll (#24863, #24861)?
- **recommended_default:** Drop the CLI verb, as #24863 already decided (node-install-enrollment D12): V1B records the ledger drop before S3-NAME, and #24863 closes as superseded. The web UI HTTP login stays (AUTH). S4-RELEASE builds gobby node enroll (#24861). From CP-PREDELETE-CUT, where the Python CLI leaves, until CP-NODE-CUT activates S4-RELEASE, no CLI enrolls a new node; enrolled nodes are unaffected, and CP-PREDELETE-CUT's smoke proves the existing one.
- **rationale:** One enrollment path. Because Stage 4 now follows CP-FINAL-CUT (D24) the gap is visible for that window, but it only affects enrolling a new node; Josh can instead keep gobby auth login in V1B until CP-NODE-CUT.

### D8: New crate dependencies hdbscan 0.12.0 and kdtree 0.7.0 (#25546), and the embedding serving lease (#25542).
- **recommended_default:** Already approved: Josh approved the stamped memory plan that contains both (attestation aca21b08 on #25479, 2026-11-02). The map places them: hdbscan 0.12.0 and kdtree 0.7.0 exact-pinned and only in the memory crate (MEM-2) after a licence check; #25542's serving lease in AI-2 as the single embedding-serving owner for MEM-2, CIX-2, MCP-FLIP and MUX-1's tool vector writer, its projection-change ledger included, which MEM-2's native writers append to.
- **rationale:** Review refuted the needs-Josh reading. Reclustering parity needs HDBSCAN, and one lease owner avoids three competing collection rebuilds during an embedding switch.

### D9: #21588 voice engine and Crane TTS licence (reserved by Josh).
- **recommended_default:** Josh decides before VOICE starts (VOICE is scheduled after CHAT-2 in wave 3). D107 is the answer VOICE builds unless he rules otherwise at map approval.
- **rationale:** Josh reserved the call; the trait keeps the engine swappable without blocking the surfaces.

### D10: #21564 runbook-seat MCP surfaces admit_team and check_runbook_seats: port or drop? (#25828 removed the third, cold_start_admin, before the cut.)
- **recommended_default:** Port them, with get_team and team_progress, in AG-5 after PIPE-2. Per-tool routing (D26) lets the pilot soak gobby-tasks tools while get_team and team_progress stay proxied until AG-5.
- **rationale:** Bundled team pipelines depend on them, so dropping them breaks runbooks when Python stops serving at CP-PREDELETE-CUT. admit_team runs only from a team pipeline's admit step, so it follows PIPE-2. Admission policy stays declared in YAML (AGENTS rule 16).

### D11: Owners for POST /api/nodes/report and the node runs rows (#21564 or Stage 4 #25269).
- **recommended_default:** NODEHUB (Stage 2, wave 4) owns report, checkouts, runs/* and detection-manifests and absorbs #25269's hub side. HOOK-3 owns nodes/hooks/replay and nodes/receipts, because it is the chunk that dispatches hooks natively. Stage 4 builds the node side against them. Its report and terminate routes, with the reported pane store, the node report inbox and the run reconciler, activate at CP-WAVE5-CUT with the terminal host, the store's last Python in-process reader (D19); remote idle's decision is AG-2's native idle check over the store's facts, and until CP-WAVE5-CUT AG-2 reaches Python's reconciler and store through worker ops.
- **rationale:** The exit rule needs every Python surface delegated before #21574, which precedes Stage 4, and a row-owning chunk upstream of the native dispatch core would need a Python hand-off. It also overrides the Projects plan's transfer of POST /api/nodes/checkouts from #24151 to Projects (.gobby/plans/gdaemon-projects-files-docs-family.md D1, 4.5.5 and 6.3.5, recorded under #24951 on 2026-10-24): NODEHUB keeps that row with the other node endpoints this decision gives it, and its checkout handler calls PROJ-2's native checkout service with 4.5.5's contract, so the service keeps one owner.

### D12: #21559 materialize_managed_launch and the rotate_due loop: the runtime plan keeps them in Python, but Stage 3 deletes Python.
- **resolved_by:** ruling 16
- **recommended_default:** Port both in A1-RUNTIME: materialize_managed_launch as a gruntime service, and rotate_due's native iteration, which A1-RUNTIME registers on R4's single scheduler itself. A1-RUNTIME now depends on R4, which reverses the earlier map's R4-on-A1-RUNTIME edge. The job registers only when the runtime family is active, so it starts at CP-TEMPLATE-READS-CUT.
- **rationale:** S3-DELETE removes Python, so nothing can stay there. Ruling 16 makes the runner a firm switchover that must cover R0-R6 before CP-MCP and the first family, and its notes move R4's native rotate_due registration into A1-RUNTIME, so CP-RUNNER's scope carries no A1 code and the runner is not held for the pilot.

### D13: What is the pilot's compare soak?
- **recommended_default:** Two stages. First, CP-TEMPLATE-REVIEW runs the bounded in-session replay soak: three passes of P0-HARNESS's soak loop over the committed REC-PILOT corpus, weighted by the gport shapes census, then differential and dual-run write replay of the whole corpus in the full-daemon harness, judged by D17. Then CP-TEMPLATE-CUT runs the live Compare day: the tasks and runtime families run in Compare on the live daemon for one full active day, so callers always get Python's answer (crates/gdaemon/src/front_door/routes.rs:186-254) while gdaemon compare-report scores real traffic. A 72h soak runs only if Josh asks, as a detached process between chunks with no claim held. The real-data corpus (a pg_dump of the hub DB without secrets tables, restored into the test hub, never committed) stays off unless Josh approves it. CP-WAVE3-REVIEW's soak is bounded the same way, with an optional detached 24h run. Later families always get differential replay, and each wave's cutover window is its live observation.
- **rationale:** Josh's pilot asks for 'a full compare soak'. Ruling 14's checkpoint cutovers make a live Compare window possible with no new machinery: Compare already gives callers Python's answer and logs every diff, so the live day adds real interleavings and agent load that a replay cannot see, at no risk to callers. A 72h soak inside a chunk session would hold a claim for days on waits bounded at 3,600 s (#25635), and #25460 v2 had already made it optional. The snapshot copies private data, so Josh opts in.

### D14: When is ported Python deleted, given the 1,172-module lazy-import cycle?
- **resolved_by:** ruling 14 permits it; one go is the map's default
- **recommended_default:** All at once in S3-DELETE, after S3-FREEZE and after CP-PREDELETE-CUT has made the live generation Python-free; no per-family deletion of surfaces or domain modules. Flagged: this reverses approved per-family deletion leaves (memory #25562 and #25563, code-index #24709, #24710 and #24713, cron #25035, s2-11 P7, #25499, and #24356's wrapper deletion; the memory plan with per-family deletion was approved on 2026-11-02). Each becomes 'stop serving and freeze' at its family's activation, and the deletion lands in S3-DELETE.
- **rationale:** Josh: 'Yes, it can be deleted in one go, or we can strangler fig it.' One go is the cheaper of the two here: every pinned and retained generation before CP-PREDELETE-CUT still runs Python from the checkout, so a per-family deletion would break generation rollback (D38). Differential replay against Python is the drift oracle until S3-FREEZE. Still-Python callers reach MCP descriptors and managers in-process. Partial deletion inside the 1,172-module lazy-import cycle breaks untested lazy-import paths at runtime. Unreachable Python routes are harmless while the family's backend is Native.

### D15: Homes for port tooling, bundled templates and pin authority.
- **recommended_default:** crates/gport (dev-only, never promoted) replaces the Python ledger generator and the scripts/port/ checks, and holds start, check-slice, census and shapes. gport start refuses a chunk until every depends_on task is closed with closed_reason done and, for every kind except checkpoint, its linked commit is an ancestor of 0.9.0 HEAD. A gobby-assets crate embeds the template tree at build time (build.rs include_bytes!, no new dependency) and moves it to assets/shared at S3-DELETE, with TPL as the single loader and sync owner. Pin and promotion authority, with GEN-ROLLBACK's generation store, window hold and rollback verb (D38), moves to Rust in V1A. #24999's asset script is not built, and S3-FREEZE copies the SRT inputs into gobby-assets for S4-INSTALL's #24866.
- **rationale:** Each must outlive Python. Embedding keeps templates version-locked to the binary, which serves AGENTS rule 17.

### D16: Who owns the 330 operator CLI rows?
- **recommended_default:** Stage 3 verb chunks V1A-V5B over the frozen public API, after their families, with REC-CLI goldens as the oracle. Family chunks add no gclient verbs. A verb with no endpoint behind it adds one in the family crate through Found Work. The memory CLI is a gclient verb set too: #25555, #25556 and #25560 build no gdaemon memory host and no Python forwarder. D69 is the exception for verbs that must work with no daemon running, such as gobby sync and gobby install's content step: they reach the hub through a gdaemon subcommand.
- **rationale:** ROADMAP decision 24 and tasks-family Q6 (#21571). Clients come after stable APIs, and it keeps the pilot's measurement clean.

### D17: Calibration gate thresholds for CP-TEMPLATE-REVIEW and CP-WAVE3-REVIEW.
- **recommended_default:** Proceed when the D11 rate (partial+stub)/(done+partial+stub) is at most 5% of owned rows, the final replay pass has zero unexplained compare mismatches with every mismatch class triaged (fixed, known-bad, or an accepted contract change), and differential replay is 100% equal or classified. Cost data (session hours, tokens, checkpoints, Rust test lines and Python lines per checkpoint, recording cost per case, and cost against relief) resizes later chunks. The gate's result goes into the review packet. A failure is a no-go: a follow-up commit and a re-run of the replay soak, and a second failure means re-planning with Josh. D11 here and in the checkpoint packets names .gobby/plans/task-25341.md's fan-out gate (:131-135), not this map's D11; gport check-slice --report prints the rate from each chunk's status file (P0-RECORD).
- **rationale:** Josh's pilot asks for a full compare soak and a measured partial/stub rate before fan-out, and thresholds turn the measurement into a gate. #25460 v2 had made the D11 gate and the 72h soak paperwork optional after B0. This map keeps the D11 gate before fan-out because its angle is oracle-first, runs the bounded replay soak of D13 in place of a 72h soak, and keeps the paperwork to gport's D11 report plus one compare-report summary.

### D18: Known-bad policy for Python-recorded oracles.
- **recommended_default:** Rust implements the correct value, never python_observed. Shell-guard items in the friction queue are fixed first (start gate); the rest are registry rows. A fix that lands on 0.9.0 later retires its row in the same commit and re-records the affected cases. A row covers a difference below any one ledger surface; a difference on one exact surface takes a docs/contracts/parity-waivers.json entry instead (D84).
- **rationale:** Josh item 4; parity means contracts, not accidents (settled item 5).

### D19: Coexistence rules while Python and Rust implementations share 0.9.0.
- **recommended_default:** Shared DB tables may have two implementations: the corpus proves equal DB deltas, Rust tolerates every Python-written row, both use the same lock keys and notify channels, and Rust emits the events Python caches listen for. Single-owner live state has one owner at a time and moves after its last Python in-process caller (callers before callees). Rust calls Python only through existing endpoints or allow-listed worker ops; Python never calls Rust. A stricter invariant needs a DB constraint Python already satisfies. Because the main checkout runs 0.9.0 (ruling 15), coexistence is live from CP-RUNNER-CUT on (runner job, recovery and lease rows), and from CP-MCP-CUT for the gateway's schema lease rows, not only in tests. A value that gdaemon hands to Python, such as the worker marker or the terminal route GOBBY_TERMINAL_ROUTE (crates/gdaemon/src/state.rs:162-171), is a child-contract value set only by gdaemon's compiled defaults, and Python follows the value gdaemon latches: TERM-1's dormant helper makes both of Python's terminal route reads use the latched value (src/gobby/runner_backend.py:83; src/gobby/runner_init/terminal_wiring.py:64-68), so an activation flips only gdaemon's default and a gdaemon-alone restore hands the old value back in one restart. If Josh refuses that Python edit, the activation flips Python's two reads with gdaemon's default, and the rollback lands the deactivation commit under the freeze as the hold's owner, then restores the pinned generation, then promotes the deactivation build under the token, because Python refuses to start when the two disagree (src/gobby/runner_backend.py:80-91); any other value gdaemon hands Python needs the same order. For project files the shared lock is the owner-only sidecar flock that Python's project initialization takes (src/gobby/utils/durable_file.py:26-38), and for derived writes scoped to a project it is gcore's project fence, which Python's ProjectWriteFence takes through its Python half (D47). S3-DELETE deletes TERM-1's helper with the rest of src/gobby.
- **rationale:** Answers the cross-family and shared-table questions without any Python client of a Rust endpoint and without dual-mode machinery, and keeps every retained generation's Python able to start against the checkout it finds.

### D20: Rows dropped at ledger closure.
- **recommended_default:** Drop the FastAPI docs, redoc and openapi rows (8; the Rust API is documented in docs/contracts), test-types and test-quality CLI (5; no Python tests remain), /api/admin/test/* (4; a harness feature), and /_gobby/ws/bridge (1; dies with Python). Keep the recorded drops #25449 (4), #19319 (1) and tasks compact and clean (#25499, 5). Josh approves each class. D66 adds one more class: gobby sessions renumber and backfill-context-windows (2).
- **rationale:** None of these is a product surface once Python retires.

### D21: #25269, #25201 and #21576 would reverse approved Stage 4 placements.
- **recommended_default:** Move their Python-surface parts to Stage 2 owners: #25269's hub side to NODEHUB, #25201 to TERM-1 (keep hub-mode's remote write branch), #21576 to COMMS-2 on PROJ-2's files_home documents. Node-side parts stay in Stage 4. #25269's hub side activates at CP-WAVE5-CUT, and its remote idle decision runs in AG-2 (D11).
- **rationale:** S3-DELETE removes their Python surfaces before Stage 4 starts. Review flagged the reversal as needing Josh.

### D22: Migration policy on the live 0.9.0 checkout.
- **resolved_by:** Josh, 2026-11-03/04, rulings 19 and 20
- **status:** Resolved.
- **recommended_default:** Migrations are expand-only until CP-FINAL-CUT: a migration adds tables, columns or indexes that Python ignores, together with the GRANT and REVOKE statements on the objects it creates. Schema inputs (migrations with their assets.rs entries, baseline.sql, the pin and the catalog manifest) land only inside a checkpoint cut, in its step 6: after the verified backup (4) and the rehearsal (5), immediately before the activation commit, under the same freeze; the rehearsal builds from the cutover branch, where those commits sit under the activation commit. They cannot land before the backup, because hub-backup's restart start-half proof refuses while the checkout's pin differs from the installed generation's schema identity (src/gobby/cli/hub_backup/cli.py:228-235; src/gobby/storage/schema_divergence.py:251-265, via src/gobby/cli/daemon_preflight.py:68-78), and between cuts the same check would refuse every session's restart. Each schema-carrying chunk (B0-WRITE, SKILLS, CRON, PLANS and PROJ-2, and SES-2 only if Found Work gives it a schema input, because the sessions plan adds none) lands its dormant code at its own landing and closes; its schema inputs and the tests that need the new schema form one prepared commit, reviewed with the chunk, on the append-only branch port/prepared/<chunk id>, recorded by SHA at its close, and the first cut whose activation needs that schema, Compare included, lands it. Dependent chunks apply it only in their isolated harness. The carrying chunk's own tests that need its schema travel in its prepared commit, and a dependent that lands before that cut puts its own schema-dependent tests in its own prepared commit, which the same cut lands after the upstream one (chunk protocol step 8). The cut assembles its branch before the rehearsal: the prepared commits in packet order, each migration renumbered to the next free number, except one that a rollback reverted, which keeps its number and bytes (below), one commit regenerating baseline.sql, the catalog manifest and the pin from a real build, then the activation commit; the deactivation commit reverts all of them. Step 6 lands the whole sequence with one land_commit on the activation SHA, because land_commit refuses a landing that changes migrations, baseline.sql or assets.rs without src/gobby/storage/schema_expected_identity.json (src/gobby/tasks/landing_policy.py:76-91). If the cut's promotion refuses after they landed, the session lands the deactivation commit under the freeze before clearing it, so every session's restart passes again (ruling 15). From CP-RUNNER-CUT on, every retained generation accepts a hub ahead by expand-only receipts (SCHEMA-WINDOW), so a rollback across an expand step is the binary restore plus the deactivation commit, which reverts the cut's schema inputs so that the checkout's schema identity matches the restored generation, with no data loss; a later cut re-lands the same migration file in its step 6 (the retry after Josh's reassessment, or the next cut that needs it), whose receipt then matches. Drops, and every other step outside the expand set, are destructive migrations, carrying the -- gobby:destructive directive and the filename marker that SCHEMA-WINDOW pairs with it and lints for. They happen only at CP-FINAL-CUT and POST-CLEAN, each an irreversible step with its own go from Josh, and rollback there is that cut's backup restore.
